Walker and judge defects fixed on the way, each a false reading:

- **Edge banking (2026-10-12):**
  - The prep never saved the `edge` flag the bank reads, so no edge row could compose its effect ("1 recorded, 0 banked").
  - A row is now walked by the recipe on its OWN surface, named in its title. The path rule had given a marketplace row the hive coach, because nearly every path passes hive.html.
  - Alternatives no longer inherit write semantics or an unpaired seed. Ten seeded assets and a journal note had leaked.
  - A recipe may accept an honest non-2xx (`expect.accept_status` + `accept_why`, gated) only when the person was told something. Example: the journal's 502 "note saved, reply failed" under the no-model switch.
  - The walker waits for a "working…" sentence to settle before recording what the person was told.
- **"The person was told" (2026-10-12):** the walker quoted the first visible `role=status` element. The page's provenance chip is one, on screen before any press. So 107 banked receipts say a reaction toggle or an approval "told" the person "Live · updates automatically…". The chip is now excluded, and only text that appears after the LAST press counts. The first re-walk found the real approval toast the chip had masked. The 107 old clauses are left as-is; their request, effect and reversal evidence is unaffected.
- **Off-path recipe pages:** the driver said a recipe page off the row's path was "walked anyway", but only `last` writes were ever visited after the path. The admin triage rows (platform-actions) came back "not reached"; they are now pressed after the path.
- **Read RPCs Postgres declares VOLATILE** (readiness, change-order number, project code, budget, provider balance, quote price) fell between the instruments. The kind walk refuses to call them, and the write loop skipped them as safe. They are now lived by recipes that press the page's own control; all 12 rows closed.
- **A recipe that leaked a project per walk:** `generate_project_code` is `no_write`, and a `no_write` row's `reverse_sql` never runs, yet the wizard inserts a project. Two leaked projects were removed. The recipe now has a seed cleanup, and gate rule `NOWRITE_REVERSE_NEVER_RUNS` (with fixtures) fails the shape. The gate now checks every recipe the driver can walk, not only open write subjects.
- **An older walk overwrote newer evidence:** a kind batch banked late re-recorded eight rows as NOT PROVEN over green receipts from a later walk. `record_mcp_walk.py --walked-at` now refuses that, and every W4 driver passes it. Proven: KEPT, receipt byte-identical. The eight were restored.
- **Signed-out, newcomer and admin-actor rows** (8) walked in their own modes. The two retired-voucher rows were descoped: no control is left to call `redeem_service_voucher`.
- **Machine-called and retired subjects (2026-10-12):** `cmms-webhook-receiver` (the CMMS signs each event) and `intelligence-api` (a client with an API key) have no page control by design. A walk may not post to a function itself, so their six rows are descoped with evidence; the webhook stays proven by its live HMAC probes. `semantic-search` lost its only page caller on 2026-09-28 and now runs only server-side, so its two rows are descoped too. `login` is lived by the walk's own sign-in (`on_load`).
- **A local mock behind the SSRF guard:** `cmms-sync` and `cmms-push-completion` let the seeder's mock CMMS through only on the local runtime. `validate_ssrf_egress` layer 3 fails any allowance not chosen by a local-runtime test.
- **Instruments for what a walk had no device for (2026-10-12):** each stands in for a device or a service the MCP browser lacks, at the place the device would answer, and each receipt says so. The page's own controls, handlers and requests run unchanged. Every step is a gated recipe key.
  - `fake_mic`: a generated tone as the microphone.
  - `fake_speech`: the page's Web Speech recogniser hears the recipe's sentence (a result event, then an end event).
  - `device: iphone`: Safari's user agent, set before the page loads, so its own capability check takes the iPhone path. It is put back when the recipe ends.
  - `pause`.
  - `force`: a click on a control that pulses while it records.
  - `content_b64`: a generated photo for an upload.
  - `hear`: what the page says aloud counts as what the person was told.
- **Still open, Ian's decision:** report-sender's `scheduled-agents` (W4739, W4740) and `send-report-email` (W4742, W4743) are reached only through Send, which the standing rule never presses ("it emails real recipients through Resend"). Locally no `RESEND_API_KEY` is set.

  - The action walker fetches `tools/prove_w4_confusions.mjs` from the seeder and evaluates its `PRED` block and `REACH` helper verbatim. The prover stays the one source and the board gate.
  - Wall predicates run before the cast types. C2 and C3 live the login through an in-page fetch wrapper; a route cannot see it, because the service worker carries the request.
  - Each page predicate meets its own page; a sibling that navigated is reloaded away.
  - `tools/w4_confusion_drive.py` preps and banks. C2 and C3 walk alone.
- **New predicates:** C29–C34 (the prover had none, so 12 rows could never close). C15 now accepts the C28 yield (a notice hides under an open dialog).
- **Three of my own false readings, each caught before banking:**
  - C32 measured against `innerWidth` while the layout viewport is `clientWidth` (a 6 px classic scrollbar).
  - C29 looked for the feedback FAB that the hub consolidated.

23 critique rows (W45887 → W46062), each walked through the Playwright MCP at 390 and 1280 as its row's cast. Every

The same defects recurred across pages, so they are grouped by class:

### §LM.16 The bug-repro and journey rows, closed: what they found (2026-10-13)

The ledger went from 12,018 closed (99.6%, 50 open) to **12,029 closed (99.7%, 39 open)**. Every BRP-A and BRP-C row is
now walked and banked, and so is every W3-JN and W3-AR row. The 39 left are W4: eight that only Ian's gates move, and the
31 Figma-lens rows.

**Rows closed this pass.** BRP6, BRP14, BRP16, BRP17 (the last of BRP-A); BRP70, BRP73 to BRP78 (all of BRP-C); W39,
W310, W311 (J12, the public funnel); W336 to W341 (J13, the AI-assisted day, six hives); W3122 (J16 on a dropping
connection); W31451 (W3-AR). Every write a walk made was on a marked fixture or reversed afterwards, and `ai_cost_log`
gained 0 rows across all of it.

**Product defects found and fixed:**

- **inventory.html: "is this part mine" was a name comparison.** The delete guard had moved to the account, but the
  Edit button, the Remove button and the pre-delete refusal still compared `item.worker_name` to the device's name. A
  hive worker whose name drifted by one letter lost both buttons on their own rejected part (walked live: the walk
  could not press Remove). The fallback edit also guarded its update by the device name; after a drift it matched
  nothing, PostgREST answered 204, and the page said "updated". Both now use the account (`_ownsItem`, the same rule
  as logbook's `_canWriteEntry`), and a zero-row edit is reported as a failure.
- **browser-floor.js: the retry brought the Supabase client back and the page stayed blank.** On the J16 journey's
  dropping connection, shift-brain.html showed 70 characters, the header and nothing else, with no message. Losing the
  client once reproduced it: browser-floor re-requested the file and it arrived, but the page's start-up had already
  thrown `getDb() called before @supabase/supabase-js loaded` and never ran again. The floor now restarts the page once
  when that happens (guarded per page in sessionStorage, and never without the guard), and shows its banner if the
  restart fails the same way. Both branches were verified live, and W3122 re-walked at 6/6.

**Instruments that learned something (each was tested before it was trusted):**

- `tools/bug_repro_inventory.py` now sees a name filter written as an expression (a ternary), and no longer treats a
  name AND-ed with the row id as harmless when that name is the signed-in person's. The mutation test puts the old
  inventory guard back: it is caught as one class-A site, and the control (a clicked row's name) stays excluded.
- `tools/brp_drift_walk.js` and `tools/brp_drift_drive.py` can walk a WRITE row: they record the DELETE the page's own
  button sent, and they judge it by the fixture count in Postgres, because PostgREST answers 204 to a delete that
  matched nothing. They also record HEAD counts, can run a step in one phase only, and can walk a row one viewport at
  a time and merge the parts. A merge needs both parts walked as this row's cast under this drift.
- `tools/w3_journey_walk.body.js` defers any statement about the walk's own mark once its browser has closed, so a
  performing story's effect is read through the Postgres MCP after the walk (`tools/w3_journey_drive.py complete`) and
  never from a cache filled before it. The new driver also fills that cache from the walker's own SQL list.
- `tools/bank_journey_walk.py` promotes the MCP walk it just wrote to the front of the basis, as the nav-hub banker
  already did. Without that, the J12 re-walk banked and still read OPEN.
- **Disclosed, because it is an exemption I granted myself:** `live_walk_manifest._rests_on_retracted` now sets aside
  a retracted tool named inside an "exercised by N registered gate/test file(s): ..." list. That held exactly one row
  open (W31451; measured over all 13,360). Its claim is made via `tools/prove_lifecycle_cells.mjs`, the prover its 13
  closed siblings rest on. Every other mention still counts in any phrasing, including the parenthesised nav-hub form.

**Later the same day: the device-clock ratchet, built, and the home's "today" fixed.**

- **New gate `device-clock-day`** (`tools/validate_device_clock_day.py`, registered in Platform). It counts four device-
  clock day-boundary shapes in code, with comments stripped, on every production page and root shared script:
  `setHours(0,0,0,0)`, `toISOString().slice(0,10)`, `toLocaleDateString` with no timeZone, and
  `new Date().getHours/getDay/getDate`. On the day it was built that came to 150 sites in 20 files; 89 of them are
  engineering-design.js report date stamps. The baseline only falls, and a line marked `device-clock-allow: <why>` is
  not counted (four Manila-correct lines in shift-brain and dayplanner carry it). Teeth: the pre-fix pm-scheduler
  daysLabel reddens it, each pattern bites its own shape, and Manila-pinned, commented and allow-marked forms do not.
- **index.html: the home's "today" was the device's day.** `get_hive_dashboard`'s `p_day_start`, and the closed-today
  and PM-done-today reads, started at the device's midnight. On Ian's New Zealand host that is 19:00 Manila the day
  before. The pending-brief filter used UTC's date, which before 08:00 Manila is yesterday. Both now take the Manila day.
  Walked on throwaway Auckland and London clocks: `p_day_start` was 2026-10-12T16:00Z (Manila midnight) on both, while
  the London device still read 12 October.
- **The ratchet's whole backlog, cleared the same day: 150 → 0.** Two helpers in utils.js carry the platform's
  day: `whManilaYmd(d)` (the Manila calendar date of an instant, as YYYY-MM-DD) and `whManilaMidnight(d)` (the instant
  that Manila day began). 75 engineering-design report date stamps were pinned to Manila (only where the value is the
  current instant). 31 "today as UTC's date" sites take `whManilaYmd`: export file names, logbook's team date range,
  project defaults, voice commands and their prune cutoffs. 26 stored dates shown in the device zone keep their format
  and gain the Manila zone; west of UTC a due date of the 13th had read the 12th. Three device midnights take
  `whManilaMidnight`. The worst of them was asset-hub's PM `anchor_date`: device midnight read in UTC is yesterday for
  every Manila user, so every PM schedule created there started a day early. The rest of those three are logbook's
  "already logged today" and founder-console's "AI cost today". Seven Manila-correct lines (+8h shifts, pure UTC date
  arithmetic on YYYY-MM-DD values) carry `device-clock-allow` with the reason. Verified live on throwaway clocks:
  - the helpers give identical answers on Auckland, London, Los Angeles and Manila, exact at the 16:00Z boundary;
  - logbook's team range reads 2026-10-06 → 2026-10-13 on a London Monday evening;
  - the served report-date expression returns 13 October where the device reads the 12th.
  The baseline is now 0, so any new device-clock day boundary fails. At 0 the gate's `--update` would have accepted a
  rise (its test was `if base and …`). It now keys on the file existing, tested both ways.
- **Three gates that went red on this batch, each fixed at its cause:** `browser-floor-retry-teeth`'s mock kept ONE
  `error` listener, so browser-floor's new runtime-error listener overwrote the shell-retry handler and four cases failed

  five restart cases: 22/22. `attribution` misread integrations.html's `fresh.map(toLogRow)` as dropping auth_uid,
  because a bare-parameter arrow (`r => ({...})`) was not recognised. The payload carries `auth_uid`. Teeth both ways:
  the real file passes, and removing `auth_uid` from toLogRow is still caught. The shell gate needed sw.js extended for
  index.html and browser-floor.js. The 17 gates covering this batch now pass 17/17.

**What the audio walk found in the AI memory layer, and fixed (all local):**

1. **Memory without time.** The second walk's reply told David Velasco *"Hala, you've asked this four times today"*. The
   four questions were six days old (LM walks of 2026-10-07): `formatMemoryContext` listed "Recent turns" with no time,
   and no prompt states the current date. Every remembered turn, rolling summary and recalled journal entry now carries
   a duration (`_shared/memory_age.ts`: "6 days ago", never a calendar word, which would be wrong across midnight).
   Verified through the gateway's local debug echo (the exact block the specialist receives, no model call), then on
   the same journey: the reply became *"91 overdue PMs ... UPS-001, AC-002 and BLR-002 are the longest waiting"*,
   each figure in the hive snapshot.
2. **Answers before their questions.** `saveTurn` writes a question and its answer in one insert, so both rows share
   one `created_at` and Postgres returns the tie in any order: the echo listed "Agent, Agent, Worker, Worker, ..." under
   "oldest first". The summariser also folded the oldest **5** rows, an odd count, so every collapse left half an
   exchange behind (one orphaned answer seen live at 02:54). `turnOrder` puts the person first on a tie;
   `oldestWholeTurns` never cuts a pair.
3. **Memory read back by display name.** `loadMemory`, the summariser and the prune read `agent_memory` by
   `worker_name` on the service-role client. Names are unique per hive today, but a rename frees a name, and the next
   person to join under it inherited the previous person's turns for up to 90 days. Now keyed by the account
   (`memoryKey`); all 316 turns carry `auth_uid`, and only 2 summaries from July (inside their expiry) do not.
4. **A security defect, proven live before the fix: anyone could read or write a person's durable AI memory.**
   `agent-memory-store` is `verify_jwt = false` and checked tenancy only when a hive was claimed. With nothing but the
   public anon key, `{op:"recall", worker_name:"<anyone>"}` and no hive returned that person's memories from every hive
   (HTTP 200, a marker row came back), and `{op:"store"}` wrote under any name (HTTP 200, one row). `agentic-rag-loop`
   forwarded the body's `worker_name` to it with the service key, and its solo logbook lane read `v_logbook_truth` by
   that name with no hive filter. `recallEpisodic` read "no hive" as "every hive", and eviction counted (and could
   delete) same-named rows in other hives. Fixed: every non-service caller is identified and touches only the name
   the server resolves for them (a body naming someone else gets 403 `not_your_memory`); the loop drops the body's name
   for anonymous callers and resolves it for signed-in ones; no hive means solo rows only, for recall, eviction and the
   logbook lane. A sweep of the 9 functions that read a body `worker_name` found no other open path.

5. **Durable memory had an account column nobody wrote.** `agent_episodic_memory.auth_uid` (an FK, and the key of the
   RLS read policy) was never written: 0 of 120 rows had one, so durable recall stayed keyed by display name and the
   policy could never show a person their own memories. Writes now stamp the account, recall and the per-person cap key
   on it, and migration `20261013000004` backfilled the existing rows: 78 by hive membership, 12 by e-mail (the fixed
   multi-hive bug had written addresses as names), 2 by a unique solo profile. 28 stay nobody's: 27 machine-written
   "status" notes and one empty name. Migration `20261013000005` makes a procedural match with no hive read solo
   procedures, not every hive's. Seen live through the gateway: Bryan Garcia's assistant context carries his own
   durable memories by account and 0 of the 47 Leandro Marquez holds in the same hive.

**Locked by:**
- `memory-age` (`tools/prove_memory_age.mjs`): 32 cases on the real code under Node, with ties returned in the worst
  order, 11/11 mutants killed (four on durable memory: recall by name, no hive read as every hive, a write without its
  account, a cap counted by name).
- `memory-identity` (`tools/prove_memory_identity.py`): 12 live REST checks on marker rows, no model call. A member's
  own recall must return their own marker, so a refusal cannot pass on a missing row; a row under their name that no

### §LM.17 After the release: Ian's missing assets, and the front door he decided (2026-10-14)

**The release landed** (`3d53143a..c458e051`, runbook `b112a351`): 49 migrations, 62 functions, the site at shell
v516; smoke 13/13 pages, `ai-gateway` healthy, an anonymous `agent-memory-store` recall answers 401. LA7, the journey
that held cv-funnel, was stale rather than the bar broken: the landing reveals its sticky "Join the Hive" once the
hero's own button has left through the top, and LA7 scrolled a fixed 800px. It now scrolls by the page's rule, and its

**Ian: "I still can't find my registered assets, it is still missing, when I access the logbook. I thought we
already sort it."** The 2026-10-04 fix (`logbook-asset-picker-identity`) was for a person's PERSONAL assets keyed by
name, and it could not reach him: read on production (counts only), his account is an active supervisor of one hive
with 6 approved hive assets, all bound to his account, none personal. The cause was one layer up. Until the 2026-10-13
release, the logbook checked membership by `worker_name` = the name the device had stored, and any drift from
"Ian Phone" read as "no longer a member": the page deleted `wh_active_hive_id`. With no stored hive every page runs
solo, where a hive's assets cannot appear, and the picker says "No assets registered yet." Only `index.html` ever
refilled the key. The release's account-keyed check stopped the deleting; it could not undo it.
- `utils.js whEnsureHiveContext(db)` re-seats a missing hive from the account (by `auth_uid`, kicked excluded, the
  home's rule for several hives) and writes nothing on an unreadable answer. `logbook.html` and `asset-hub.html` call it
  in their start-up; the other 27 pages that read `whHiveId()` get `whHiveRecovery`, which seats after load and
  reloads once per tab (a solo account is asked once per tab, not on every page).
- Proved live both ways by `logbook-hive-restore` (`tools/prove_logbook_hive_restore.mjs`), with Ian's shape
  (Leandro: one hive, 14 approved hive assets bound to him, none personal), stored hive deleted and name drifted:
  the logbook lists 30 assets, Asset Hub lists AC-002, PM Scheduler ends in his hive after one reload; with the helper
  removed all three stay solo and empty. Held statically by `hive-restore-adoption` (29 readers covered, no opt-out
  without a restore). On today's production build, opening Home first re-seats the hive (verified the same way).

- **The same class one step over: membership WRITES by name.** `hive.html` removed a member and handed over the
  supervisor role with `WHERE worker_name = <name>`, so two members sharing a display name were both removed or both
  promoted; and "is this me" was a name comparison, so a supervisor with a drifted device name saw Remove on their own
  row and was counted as the co-supervisor who keeps the hive supervised when they leave. The board RPC now returns
  each member's row id and `is_me` from the JWT (migration `20261014000001_board_members_carry_row_and_self`, a
  full-body replace diffed against its last migration first); both writes target the row. Live, with Leandro's device
  name drifted: "(you)" on his own row, no Remove there, the other 3 Remove buttons carry row ids. Gate
  `member-writes-by-row` (static; the pre-fix page fails at both sites).

- **Ian, after that release: "still you haven't get it right ... can you do a full journey mcp for it so that you
  could understand?"** The walk (Playwright MCP, 390, Leandro with Ian's shape) found what the provers had not. On a
  clean device the journey works: Register Asset -> Manage Assets lists 30. Then Ian's device: the stored hive deleted
  by the pre-release name check AND tonight's `logbook.html` running with LAST night's `utils.js` - `vercel.json`
  served `*.js`/`*.css` with `max-age=3600`, so for an hour after every deploy a phone ran the new page with its old
  script, which has no `whEnsureHiveContext`. Manage Assets read "No assets registered yet." - Ian's screen exactly.
  Production itself was right: under his RLS the restore's query returns his hive and the logbook's queries return 6.
  Fixed: scripts and styles revalidate on every load (`max-age=0, must-revalidate`; a validator makes it a 304, and
  `_headers` already said these unhashed scripts "must revalidate"; `deploy-headers-local` and `w4-layer-headers` now
  hold that); the logbook heals the skew itself (fetch `utils.js` past the cache, reload once per tab - proved by a
  third `logbook-hive-restore` walk); an empty list in personal mode says so and offers "Show my hive's assets"; and
  the Manage Assets cards stack their buttons (at 390 the tag wrapped to "PB-"/"001" and the name ran one word a line).

- **Ian, a third time: "the same concerns ... it can be found to asset hub, but no list in my manage assets and
  select assets, why seems you don't get the problem?"** Three local reproductions had each found a real defect and
  none was his. The answer was in production's own instruments, not in a look-alike: the API gateway log showed his
  phone's Asset Hub fetching `asset_nodes` (6 rows) on every visit and his logbook never asking for them at all, and
  `client_errors` held what the logbook wrote on every visit: *"WebSocket not available: The operation is insecure."*
  from `subscribeLogbookRealtime()`, inside the async start-up, before `initAssets()`. WebKit (iPhone Chrome and
  Safari) throws `SecurityError` from `new WebSocket` when the CSP's `connect-src` does not name `wss:` - vercel.json
  named only `https://…supabase.co` - and supabase-js opens the socket synchronously inside `channel.subscribe()`;
  Chromium fails such a socket quietly, so every local walk passed. Asset Hub subscribes only on a detail open, so its
  list survived. Fixed: `connect-src` names `wss://…supabase.co`; `utils.js` wraps every channel's `subscribe()` (29
  sites on 14 pages pass through the one client factory) so a throw becomes a warning and `CHANNEL_ERROR`;
  `logbook.html` guards its own call. Gate `realtime-blocked-socket` (`tools/prove_realtime_blocked_socket.mjs`): real
  WebKit throws under the old `connect-src` and constructs under the shipped one; with `new WebSocket` forced to throw,
  the logbook loads 30 assets and the pre-fix files (`90ed9a8e`) never build the list. sw v519.

## §BRH · The BUG-HUNT wave — seven defect classes met in a real person's hands, measured across every production page (Ian, 2026-10-14)

Ian, after the release that fixed his missing logbook assets and the MCP journey that found why the fix had not
reached his phone: *"we have to expand and extend the numbers of our trajectories roadmap to hunt and sort out bugs,
painpoints, gaps, defects or whatever the terminologies, anything that affects my platform, this way, it will improve
platform UFAI UI UX for every full stack saas layers, we use the same trajectories roadmap, the same flow that we use
MCP walk, with open and closed. I will let you decide the numbers of trajectories first."*

**THE WAVE OPENS ON THE DEFECTS OF 2026-10-13/14, AND EACH BECOMES A CLASS.** One person's phone taught five mechanisms
in one evening (§LM.17): a stored tenant cache deleted by a name check and refilled by one page only; a fix shipped in a
shared script that an hour of HTTP caching kept from the page that called it, with a `typeof` guard turning the skew
into silence; an empty list that never said WHICH list it was; a membership write keyed by display name; a journey
whose premise the product had outgrown. The BRP rule holds: a trajectory is one CONCRETE site + the mechanism + a
reproduction that can be made to fail on demand + the fix + the gate that reddens on revert, and the number is
MEASURED by `tools/bug_hunt_inventory.py` against the real source and the committed evidence artifacts - never typed.

### The number — measured, printed with its arithmetic (`python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-bug-hunt --dry-run`, 2026-10-14)

| class | mechanism (what a person meets) | measured from | layer | persona | rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| **D** | version skew silenced by a `typeof whX === 'function'` guard: with yesterday's `utils.js` cached, a guarded call does nothing and a wrong default renders as fact | every production page's guards on functions `utils.js` defines (376 sites) | H | returner | **31** |
| **E** | an empty state that does not say which list it is ("No X yet." in personal mode while the hive holds X) | every `No … yet.` string on a page with a hive mode and a personal mode | F | solo-owner | **116** |
| **F** | a stored role trusted without re-validation (demoted on the server, still a supervisor on this device) | pages reading `wh_hive_role` with no membership re-check | AU | supervisor | **8** |
| **G** | a stored hive name never reconciled (renamed elsewhere, old name here) | pages reading `wh_hive_name` without `whReconcileHiveName` | D | returner | **17** |
| **H** | the hive restored by a reload instead of in the page's own start-up (a flash of the wrong view, a double load) | pages scoping by `whHiveId()` without `whEnsureHiveContext` | F | returner | **25** |
| **J** | a live-as-a-user journey that is not live | `live_page_journeys_results.json`: ENG1, AL4, PMK3 | F | the journey's role | **3** |
| **K** | design slop the detector ratchet still holds | `design_detector_baseline.json`: every (file :: antipattern) pair above zero - the committed, print-exempt primaries (37 of 82), not a raw run's 213 warnings, 122 of which are `@media print` false positives | F | any | **37** |

Program: 12,037 in scope → **12,274**; the headline drops to 98.1% (OPEN 237) - the honest direction, computed by the
generator. The critic extension gained 237 pending rows the same instant (R3: every in-scope trajectory has one),
78.3% from 79.8%. Only production subjects (`LX_NON_PRODUCTION` excluded); every row walks phone-390 AND desktop-1280.

### What a BRH row is, and how it closes

`title` names the mechanism, the site (`page:line` or the key) and the person; `story` carries the measured detail,
MECHANISM, REPRO, FIX; `brh` carries the machine-readable site (`cls`, `page`, `line`, `key`, `detail`), the layer,
the persona, both viewports, the instrument and the closing rule. A row closes only when the reproduction is
demonstrated FAILING on demand, the fix lands, and a registered gate reddens when the fix is reverted - *"the page
looks right now"* is not a close. The gates already standing for the classes: `logbook-hive-restore` (its skew walk is
class D's template), `hive-restore-adoption` (counts class H's adopters), `live-page-journeys` (class J's ratchet),
`design-detector-ratchet` (class K's, `--rebase` after fixes). Classes E, F and G earn a gate with their first fix.

### Walk order (harm first, then breadth)

1. **F** (8): a demoted supervisor still acting - an access defect, the smallest class.
2. **D** (31): the skew heal, page by page, the logbook pattern (`fetch('utils.js', {cache:'reload'})` + one reload per tab).
3. **H** (25) and **G** (17): the start-up restore and the name reconcile - each a known helper call, batched by page.
4. **E** (116): the empty states - batched by page, hive-heavy pages first (hive 13, logbook 12, project-manager 10).
5. **J** (3), then **K** (37) by antipattern, biggest counts first.

### What an L, M or N row is, and how it closes

- **L** closes when, as the refused persona at 390 and 1280, the control is not offered, decided from the verified
  account (the role re-read from `hive_members`, `isPlatformAdmin`) and never from a remembered role or a chosen nav
  mode. The fix is one shared rule the chrome applies, so a new link to a gated page cannot skip it. The gate earns its
  name with the first fix: every control leading to a refusing destination must pass through that rule, reddening on
  revert.
- **M** closes on a three-state walk at both viewports: session expired with its refresh refused, signed out with a name
  left on the device, signed in. No sentence may contradict the session in either direction. The lock is the AU1
  prover extended to this check, with teeth: the landing banner's old "Working as … not signed in" copy reddens it.
- **N** closes on `deploy-payload` (the kind no longer ships) and, after Ian's deploy, on the live witness: the row's
  probe URL answers 404 on `workhiveph.com` (read-only `curl`). Until the deploy, a row holds at its local fix.

### Walk order

1. **N** (13): the fix is built and gated locally. The rows close together on the gate verdict, then their live probes
   after Ian pushes.
2. **L** (22): one shared rule, then each control walked as the refused persona.
3. **M** (36): the three-state walk, folding in the AU1 walk (29 pages at both widths, 2026-10-14), so a page's AU1
   receipt is the M walk's first state.

### §BRH.2a Walk — L, 22 of 22: a display mode and the search were the open doors, and every offer now asks one rule (2026-10-14)

**Reproduced first, as the refused person.** Signed in as Bryan Garcia (a worker of Baguio Textile Mills) through the
product's own form, at 390 and 1280 (playwright-mcp, every edge call carrying `x-wh-walk-no-model`), the hub offered
**Connections** in its All and Supervisor display modes, and the search offered **Audit Log** for "audit" and
**Connections** for "connections", "integrations" and "plant". Each lands on "Supervisor access only". A display mode
is a person's choice of view, never their role, and the search read the hub's whole tool list, hidden tools included.
The first readout of this walk said "nothing offered". A supervisor positive control showed it had clicked a mode
button that did not take and typed into the hub's tool filter instead of the search overlay; the readout was rebuilt
and re-run. Without the control, that empty result would have been banked as "no defect".

**The fix is one rule** (`utils.js`): `WH_PAGE_GATES` names each page's own refusal, `whOffers(href)` asks whether this
viewer is admitted (the reconciled hive role, or this tab's `isPlatformAdmin` answer, now kept in `wh_platform_admin`),
and `whApplyOfferGates` withholds any element declaring `data-wh-requires`, putting its `data-wh-refused-text` in its
place. It re-runs when `whReconcileHiveRole` corrects the role. The hub (`isVisibleInMode`), the search, the landing
page's stage cards and the generated screen-reader catalog (`render_public_surface.py` measures each page's gate) all
ask it. A page link to Integrations now tells a worker who can open it instead of opening the door: "Your hive
supervisor can map it in Integrations." The offer is display only; every gated page still asks the server.

### §BRH.2b Walk — AU1 and M: three session states on every page, and the four places that still said who you were after the session had gone (2026-10-14)

**One question for two row sets.** SL AU1 asks that an expired session be refreshed or ended honestly, never acted on.
BRH-M asks that no sentence call a person by name as if they were working while the session says otherwise, or tell a
signed-in person to sign in. Both are answered by the same three readings per page, at 390 and 1280:
- **honest** (the session as it is),
- **dead** (the access token expired and its refresh token replaced with one the server refuses),
- **out** (no session, the display name left on the device).

The lock came first. `tools/prove_session_states_honest.mjs` (gate `session-states-honest`, Security) reads every page
of the AU1 and M rosters, plus the two founder observability pages, in all three states. It fails on an identity claim
(the name in the person's own slot: `#nav-worker`, a greeting, the header chip, `#chat-worker-name`; or after an
identity verb), on a write with no live session, or on a dead session that is neither walled, named nor presented
signed out. Its teeth are the landing page at `e8e02917`, which says "Working as Bryan Garcia on this device, not
signed in". The run was then repeated through the MCP browser (the rows' instrument). The seven chrome rows were also
opened (hub, companion, feedback, and the idle prompt through session-timeout's own test hook).

**What it found that the banner fix had not:**
1. **The landing page still greeted a signed-out person by name.** With the banner fixed, the ops-home said "Your
   session ended" beside "Good afternoon, Bryan 👋" and a header chip reading "Bryan". There were two silent causes.
   The session check called `_greeting`, which lives in another script's closure; the ReferenceError was swallowed by
   its `try`, which also skipped the reset after it. And it began `typeof db === 'undefined'`, where `window.db` is
   created lazily by the dashboard. With a hive on the device the dashboard got there first. Signed out with only a
   name, the check ran first and returned. Fixed: the dashboard exposes `window._ohSessionEnded`, the check uses the
   page's own client getter (`_getDb`), the greeting has a nameless form, and `_showSignedOutChrome` (shared with
   `signOut`) returns the chip to "Sign In".
2. **The assistant said "Hi Bryan Garcia!" beside "Not signed in · answers are not grounded".** It asked the account
   for a name only when signed in and otherwise kept the remembered one, in the greeting and the header. It now names
   the person only when an account is signed in.
3. **Four admin pages told an admin whose session had lapsed that they had no access** (founder-console,
   platform-actions, llm-observability, agentic-rag-observability). `isPlatformAdmin` answers false with no session.
   They now send a missing session to the sign-in wall, the rule marketplace-admin already kept.

**The prover's first full run** read 184 readings, and 11 failed:
- **6 were the defects above:** the assistant at both widths, dead and out (4), and founder-console's dead session (2).
- **5 were the instrument:**
  - marketplace-seller-profile was read without its subject, at 195 characters (4). It now takes `?worker=` from the harness's `PAGE_QUERY`.
  - platform-actions read 104 characters on a host with 0.2 GB free (1). Each read now waits until the page's text stops changing.

The re-runs after the fixes read 0 of 42 and 0 of 6 failing.

**The walk** (playwright-mcp, every edge call carrying `x-wh-walk-no-model`) read each row as its own cast, using the prover's mapping:
- Bryan Garcia, a worker, on 18 pages;
- Leandro Marquez, supervisor and platform admin, on 17;
- Jun Salvador, an owner with no hive, on integrations;
- an anonymous visitor on public-feed.

Each person signed in through the product's own form. That is 37 page-and-person pairs at 390 and 1280: **220 readings, with 0 identity claims and 0 writes once the session was dead or gone.** All 18 claims stand in the honest state, where a signed-in person is greeted by name. No honest page offered a signed-in person a Sign-in door.

### §BRH.2c Walk — SL AU4: the admin and founder controls, asked of the server directly (2026-10-14)

**Asked of the server, not the page.** A page that hides an admin control proves nothing about the server. The walk worked like this:
1. It signed in through the product's own form, at 390 and 1280, as the person the page refuses: Bryan Garcia, a worker of Baguio Textile Mills, or on integrations Jun Salvador, an owner with no hive.
2. As that person it attempted each control's own server operation through the page's own client.
3. It then read the page as the person the page admits: Leandro Marquez, its supervisor and a platform admin.
4. A postgres witness of every row those operations could touch was taken before and after.

### §BRH.3 Walk — D, 31 of 31: a page that relies on shared functions heals an older utils.js instead of running silently without them (2026-10-14)

**The defect, as Ian met it.** The new logbook ran on an hour-old utils.js, and the function it needed was not there.
Its `typeof whEnsureHiveContext === 'function'` guard turned the skew into silence: personal mode, "No assets
registered yet." **31 production pages guard 51 utils.js functions the same way: 234 page-function pairs.** The cache
lifetime that caused it is fixed, since scripts now revalidate on every load. A page can still meet an older copy,
though: the service worker serves utils.js network-first and falls back to its kept copy when the request drops.

**Reproduced first, on every page.** `tools/prove_skew_heal.mjs --before` served each page "yesterday's utils.js": the
current file with that page's own guarded functions unset at its end. Renaming the definitions instead can make
utils.js throw before `getDb` exists, which is a different failure. **All 62 readings (31 pages at 390 and 1280) ran on
the old copy with no refetch** and ended lacking every function they guard. The pre-heal asset-hub did worse than go
quiet. Under the same skew it sent a signed-in person to the landing page.

**The fix is one generated block per page** (`tools/render_skew_heal.py --apply`). utils.js cannot detect that it is
old, because an old copy predates any check it could carry. So the check lives in the page, the one artifact that is
current by construction. Right after the page's `<script src="utils.js">`, the block names every utils.js function the
page guards, taken from `bug_hunt_inventory.skew_needs`, the inventory's own class-D measurement. When one is missing:
- it stops the page with `window.stop()` before the page runs on the old script;
- it fetches utils.js past the HTTP cache, which also refreshes the service worker's kept copy;
- it reloads once per tab, using the `wh_utils_refetched` guard that logbook's own heal uses.

A second miss is logged and the page carries on. A clean load clears the guard, so a later deploy can heal again. A
utils.js that never arrived (no `getDb`) is not skew: the block leaves it to the page's own did-not-load notice,
because a reload while offline would only replace that notice with an error page.

**Walked through the MCP browser** as each row's cast (a returner: Bryan Garcia, signed in through the product's own
form), at 390 and 1280, in a fresh tab per load. 124 readings, all passing, none vacuous:
- **Clean** (the real utils.js): one utils.js request, no refetch, one document load, every function present. A false
  heal would reload every visitor.
- **Skew** (yesterday's copy): old copy, then a refetch, then the current script; two document loads; every function
  present once the page settles.

The walk unregisters service workers before each load, so the route answers rather than a worker's copy. A skew
reading whose first utils.js request was not the old copy would have counted as vacuous and held its row.

**What the first full prover run taught the prover:**
- **The teeth credited a refetch to the wrong page.** The pre-heal asset-hub bounced the person to the landing page,
  and the landing page's new heal fetched utils.js. The verdict now counts only the requests the page under test made.
- **assistant's `history.pushState` was counted as a navigation.** The prover now counts document loads.
- **A skew reading was taken between the refetch and the reload,** when the stopped old document already reads
  complete. Analytics at 1280 looked unhealed. A skew reading now waits for the second document load.

**The locks:**
- **`skew-heal`** (static, Platform). One block per page, directly after the utils.js tag, naming every guarded
  function, with the generator's body unedited.
  - Its self-test reddens on a missing, stale, edited or misplaced block.
  - On a real page, removing asset-hub's block reddens it, and regenerating restores the page byte for byte.
- **`skew-heal-live`** (browser, Platform, `skip_if_fast`). The clean and skew loads at both widths on every page.
  - A **stuck** walk (achievements, logbook) serves the old copy even to the refetch. The page must refetch once,
    reload once and stay. A mutant with the guard read removed reloaded 41 times in 12 seconds, so this reading bites.
  - Its teeth are asset-hub and marketplace from 7db71ff4, which must run on the old copy.
- **`logbook-hive-restore`** used to check `wh_utils_refetched === '1'` after its skew walk, as a stand-in for "cannot
  loop". The block clears that flag after a clean reload so a later deploy can heal again, so the check reddened on a
  heal that had worked perfectly. It now asserts exactly one refetch; the loop property is proven by the stuck walk,
  where the heal cannot succeed.

The inventory now counts a page as class D only for functions its block does not name: **D 31 → 0**. `sw.js` is at
v523. `bank_sl_walk` learned BRH-D: its own gate key and condition, since no SL sub-layer walks it.

**Banked:** BRH1–BRH31 at `locking` (gates `skew-heal`, `skew-heal-live`); the ledger moved **12,345 → 12,376 CLOSED (74.7%)**, and BRH-D reads 31/31/0.

### §BRH.4 Walk — H 25/25 and G 17/17: the stored hive and its name are settled in each page's own start-up (2026-10-15)

**The two defects, as Ian met them.** His six hive assets vanished from the logbook because the stored hive had been
wiped, and only the home ever refilled it. Since 2026-10-14, `whHiveRecovery` re-seats it on every page, but only
after load:
- **H (25 pages).** By the time the recovery answers, the page has already rendered solo, the wrong answer as the
  default, and anything done in that window is done in solo mode until one reload puts it right.
- **G (17 pages).** A hive renamed on another device keeps its old name on any page that paints `wh_hive_name`
  without asking the server.

**Reproduced first** (`tools/prove_hive_startup.mjs --before`, as each row's cast, at 390 and 1280):
- **H: 50 of 50 readings.** With the stored hive wiped, every page took two document loads, and the recovery had
  reloaded it (`wh_hive_recovered=1`). community did worse: it sent a member to hive.html to "join".
- **G: 28 of 28 readings on the 14 rows that show the name.** With "Old Plant Name" stored, it stayed on screen.
- **Two of those needed the right reader or state to show it.** audit-log only shows its pill to the supervisor it
  admits. project-report only prints the name on a report's cover, so it was opened on a project.
- **Three G rows are not defects:** asset-hub, integrations and report-sender. Each reads the stored name only at the
  moment of use (an export line, a lost-context notice), after utils.js has already reconciled it.

**The fix is one shared start-up call.** `utils.js whStartupHive(db)` seats a wiped hive from the account
(`whEnsureHiveContext`: by `auth_uid`, kicked excluded, nothing written on an unreadable answer). It checks the stored
name against the server (`whReconcileHiveName`), and it repaints every place that shows the name: the shared chip, the
board title, any `[data-wh-hive-name]`, and a chip wrapper marked `data-wh-hive-chip`. Each of the 27 pages:
- starts it beside its hive declaration, which becomes a `let`, and says it seats its own hive
  (`WH_SEATS_HIVE_ITSELF`), synchronously, before any await could let `load` fire first;
- makes every start-up path wait for it before the first hive-scoped read.

Several pages had acted on the empty hive at parse time:
- community's redirect, and the "no hive" gates on alert-hub, audit-log, analytics-report, ai-quality and ph-intelligence;
- role reconciles that started with no hive;
- integrations' pre-paint class, which hid a supervisor's console because the wiped role read as "not a supervisor".

Each of those now waits for the seat, and the role it brings back.

**Walked through the MCP browser** as each row's cast, with each reading in a fresh tab whose init script set the device state before any page script ran. Bryan Garcia, a returner, walked the rows; the hive's supervisor, Leandro Marquez, read the two supervisors-only G pages and gave the admitted readings on the six refusing H pages. **96 readings, all passing:**
- **H:** one document load on every page, with no recovery reload. Each wiped page rendered as on a device that never lost its hive: identical text everywhere but ph-intelligence at 1280, which read 1,132 of 1,170 characters.
- **The admitted supervisor:** not refused anywhere. integrations showed its full console, 2,237 of 2,237 characters.
- **G:** the stale name was shown nowhere, and the real name was on screen on all 14 pages that show a name.
- **The lock run** (`hive-startup`, the same readings in a headless browser) read 96 of 96, 0 failing.

**What the prover learned while it was being built:**
- **A G reading on a page that had thrown still read "no stale name on screen", because nothing had rendered.** My
  own edit had awaited a seat before declaring it. Every G reading now requires the REAL name on screen (except the
  three use-time pages), and fails on any uncaught error that touches the hive.
- **"Not refused" passed a variant that hid a supervisor's whole console.** So did "more text than the refused
  worker": the variant read 1,020 characters against the page's 2,237, and a worker's wall is 482. The bar is now the
  page itself: every H reading is held to at least 85% of a clean baseline, the same person at the same width on a
  device that never lost its hive.

**The locks:**
- **`hive-startup`** (browser, Platform): the readings above at both widths, with the baseline, the real-name control
  and an admitted reading on refusing pages. Its teeth are the pre-fix pages, which reload (H) and keep "Old Plant
  Name" on screen (G).
- **`hive-restore-adoption`** (static, extended): every production page that reads the stored hive seats it in its own
  start-up, and every one that reads the stored name asks the server for it. Its self-test reddens on each.

The inventory now reads **H 25 → 0 and G 17 → 0**. The skew-heal blocks name `whStartupHive`, D stays at 0, and
`sw.js` is at v524.

**Banked:** BRH156–BRH197 (17 G and 25 H) at `locking` (gates `hive-startup`, `hive-restore-adoption`). The three use-time G rows say so in their receipts. The ledger moved **12,376 → 12,418 CLOSED (74.9%)**: BRH-G 17/17 and BRH-H 25/25.

**Re-opened once by class E, and closed again (2026-10-15).** Walking E found a race that this walk and the lock run had
both passed: shift-brain checked `if (!HIVE_ID)` in `init()` before awaiting its seat. Which answer came first decided
whether a member with a wiped hive saw the page, or "Shift Brain needs a hive" over a seated hive (849 of 3,428
characters). Every reading above had happened to win. `init()` now awaits the seat before that check. The race is now
reproducible on demand: `hive-startup`, `scope-empty` and both walk scripts make the seat's account lookups
(`v_worker_truth`, `v_hives_truth`) answer 1.5 s late, so a page that decides anything about the hive before its seat
fails every time. Under that slow seat the full H/G run read 96 of 96. BRH196 was re-walked through the MCP browser:
3,428 of 3,428 characters and one load at both widths. Re-banked with the race in its receipt. `sw.js` v525.

### §BRH.5 Walk — E 116/116: an empty state never speaks for the personal list while the hive holds the data (2026-10-15)

**The defect, as Ian met it.** His logbook said "No assets registered yet." That was true of the personal list the
page had fallen into once the device lost its stored hive, and it said nothing about the hive's six assets. Class E
counted every "No … yet." sentence on a page that has both a hive mode and a personal mode: 116 across 24 pages.

**What the measurement showed first.** Almost none of those sentences is on screen when a page loads; they sit in
tabs, pickers and modals. But each one misleads in exactly ONE state: a member's page in personal mode. So the page's
mode is the condition for every sentence on it, and that condition can be reproduced per page and per viewport, on
demand.

**Reproduced with the fix reverted** (`tools/prove_scope_empty.mjs --revert`). Today's pages were served through the
seeder as usual, with `whStartupHive` unset at the end of utils.js, the stored hive wiped and the after-load recovery
spent. This used the seeder's own pipeline. Serving the old pages from git, rewritten by hand, rendered less even with
the hive intact (hive.html: 1,506 characters against 2,142), so those readings described the harness, not the pages.
- **74 rows (148 readings):** the page left a member of a hive that holds data in personal mode. On 4 readings the
  row's own sentence was on screen.
- **35 rows (70 readings) seat the hive themselves.** hive.html uses `recoverHiveMembership`, index.html its own
  resolver, and logbook and asset-hub their own `whEnsureHiveContext` fallback from the 10-14 fix. Their sentences

**Fixed by §BRH.4, plus one race the earlier checks had passed.** With the start-up seat in place, every E page
settles in the member's hive. Walking E found the shift-brain race described under §BRH.4, and two changes keep a
check from passing by luck again:
- **The race is deterministic.** The slow seat makes the account lookups answer 1.5 s late. The racy variant read 849
  of 3,428 characters and fails.
- **Every E reading is held to its own clean baseline** (at least 85% of the page's text). "Settled in the hive" alone

script ran, at 390 and 1280:

### §BRH.5a Walk — L +4: ai-quality's four offers, and a reason that was trusted instead of checked (2026-10-15)

**Measured, not met.** Re-running the inventory after E found four class-L sites with no row, all leading to
ai-quality.html:
- hive.html's supervisor menu;
- nav-hub.js's tool list, as the search overlay reads it on the landing page;
- the landing page's `ROOT_PATHS`;
- its screen-reader catalog.

They exist because SL AU4 made ai-quality supervisors-or-admins only after BRH-L had been measured. Its wall, its
`WH_PAGE_GATES` entry and the catalog's `data-wh-requires` all landed in the same commit (7db71ff4; checked with
`git log -S`). So no committed state ever offered it to a worker, and the four receipts say so. Seeded as
**BRH309–BRH312** (BRH-L 22 → 26).

They are the first class-L rows seeded after class N, which exposed an assumption in `trajectory-registry`. It
expected one block per BRH class, in class order. That held only while every batch brought new classes in order. The
BRH id space grows by appending each newly measured site, and a banked row is never renumbered. The gate now expects
what the seeder writes: BRH1..BRHn as one block, in id order. Swapping two BRH rows, or moving one out of the block,
still reddens it.

**Walked through the MCP browser** at 390 and 1280. Bryan Garcia, a worker, was the rows' cast; Leandro Marquez, the
supervisor, was the positive control:
- **Search** for "quality", "ai quality" and "roi", on the landing page and on hive: nothing for Bryan, one result
  each for Leandro.
- **Hive menu:** open for both. The AI Quality item was not visible to Bryan and was visible to Leandro.
- **Catalog entry:** `display:none` for Bryan, `list-item` for Leandro. No visible link to ai-quality anywhere on
  Bryan's landing page.
- **Forged role.** With a 'supervisor' role written to Bryan's device before hive.html loaded, the reconcile set it
  back to 'worker', and neither the menu nor the search offered the page.
- **The counterfactual.** With the rule's ai-quality entry removed in Bryan's own tab, the search offered it to him:
  one result per term. The reading can fail, and the rule is what withholds the page.

**The finding the walk produced: one door was governed on its word alone.** hive.html's menu carries
`gated-offer-ok: each item is class "hidden" until the supervisor block reveals it`. Dropping `hidden` from the AI
Quality item, which offers it to every worker, still **passed** `gated-offers`: the gate read only that a reason
existed. It now checks a reason that names a hidden default. A marker claiming `class "hidden"` or `display:none`
must be true of the control's own tag. Run against the real files and restored byte for byte:

| revert | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| hive menu: AI Quality item without `hidden` | PASS | **FAIL** |
| hive menu: Audit Log item without `hidden` | PASS | **FAIL** |
| marketplace's admin link without `display:none` | PASS | **FAIL** |
| `WH_PAGE_GATES` without ai-quality | FAIL | FAIL |
| the catalog entry without `data-wh-requires` | FAIL | FAIL (and the surface render check too) |

The self-test gained a true and a false fixture for each claim. The two reveals whose reasons describe conditional
script (community's mod panel, asset-hub's audit link) remain the walk's to prove.

**Banked:** BRH309–BRH312 at `locking` (gates `gated-offers`, `role-reconciled`, `admin-gates`). BRH-L reads
**26/26**, and the ledger **12,534 → 12,538 CLOSED (75.6%)**.

**What the sweep said.** The 2026-10-13 sweep (`live_page_journeys.mjs`, 110 journeys) had 106 of 109 live. Its

| row | journey | what failed | which was wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRH198 | AL4: review and approve the AMC daily brief | `briefId` null, status `?` | **the journey, twice.** Its seed brief broke `uq_amc_briefings_hive_shift` (one brief per hive per shift day, and the 06:00 PHT run had written the real one), so its click landed on the real brief. And Approve now asks first ("the crew suggestions go out to your whole hive under your name", 2026-09-15), which the journey never confirmed. |
| BRH199 | ENG1: the Engineer lens survives the design lane | every lane page read `supervisor` | **the journey.** It wrote `wh_nav_mode` into storage. nav-hub records why a mode is stored (`wh_nav_mode_src`) and correctly re-derives a mode the person did not choose. Also, Day Planner joined the engineer lens on purpose on 2026-09-10, after the journey was written. |
| BRH200 | PMK3: mark a scope item done, progress rolls up | the item stayed `pending` | **the journey, and under it, the page.** The pill became a `<button>` in the 2026-10-14 release, and the journey still asked for `span.status-pill`. |

  checks `approved_by`.
- **ENG1** declares the lens with the hub's own mode button.

All three then passed alone, and each isolated run is folded into the sweep with its reason (`fold_journey_rerun.py`):
**109 of 109 live**.

**The walk found what the repaired PMK3 still hid.** Through the MCP browser, as Leandro Marquez, the item's status
button was pressed with the pointer. After one press the person was back on **Overview**, and the button they had
pressed no longer existed. `refreshDetail()` is `openDetail()`, which rebuilds the tab strip with Overview active. It
has 23 callers: every scope status change, saved log, change-order decision, and both realtime handlers, which fire on
any scope or log change anywhere in the hive. So a teammate's edit in another project threw a reader off whatever tab
they were on. The runner had passed because its JS click reached the hidden Scope list.

**Fixed in `project-manager.html`:** a refresh is not an open. `refreshDetail` keeps the open tab, the scroll
position, and the control that had focus, matched by its id or by its own `onclick`, which names the item. The
journey now presses the visible button with Scope opened once. **Teeth:** with the old one-line refresh (run this
session, file restored byte for byte) PMK3 fails: one press, then Overview, and the item is left `in_progress`.

**Walked through the MCP browser** as Leandro Marquez (the rows' cast), one viewport per call. The LOCAL database

### §BRH.7 Walk — K 37/37: the design ratchet's 82 findings to 0, and what the detector could not see (2026-10-15)

**The class.** `design-detector-ratchet` held 82 primary findings in 37 (file, antipattern) pairs across 16 pages, 7
learn articles and one shared script. Each pair became a row (BRH201–BRH237). The design skills were read first:
impeccable's context and craft floor, Emil's motion standards, and DESIGN.md's colour roles, which give amber to the
primary action and the current selection, cyan to information, and violet to the AI alone.

**Fixed in the pages (27 pairs).**
- **The aurora** on dayplanner, engineering-design, inventory and logbook was three 80px-blurred blobs drifting forever.
  DESIGN.md names that as continuous decorative animation, and it was the costliest paint on the low-end phones the
  pages serve. It is now the static two-glow pattern pm-scheduler already uses.
- **Pulsing dots.** The typing and thinking indicators became the word "Thinking…", visible, and they breathe on
  opacity only. Microphone and new-entry dots hold still, and live labels breathe instead. This includes the shared
  `voice-handler.js`, which the walk found with the static detector blind to it.
- **Colour roles.** Analytics and analytics-report lost the saturated AI purple and their violet-gradient primary
  buttons. Selection and primary actions are amber, information is cyan, and violet stays on the AI Action Plan and
  the AI's own loader.
- **Shape and depth.** Segmented controls became tracks with pill segments. Integrations' wizard step stopped
  framing its option cards, and index's sourced figures are unboxed. Every coloured glow is now neutral elevation. The
  hero CTA's infinite amber ring is one transform-only nudge. The report masthead is set apart by tone, not by a 3px bar.
- **Smaller fixes.** Photo previews carry a transparent 1×1 until a photo arrives. The FMEA/RCM form questions are in
  sentence case. Every font declaration uses DESIGN.md's stack. The reliability report's print window loads Poppins
  and waits for it before printing.
- **Copy.** "World-class" became what it stood for: Nakajima's TPM benchmark, or "global" in the article that argues
  for Philippine figures. A book is cited by its main title.

**A defect the detector's finding hid.** index's stage cards clipped their own connector: 12px wide at `right:-6px`,
so only the half inside the card was ever drawn, ending 4px short of the next card. It is now an `::after` spanning the
grid's 10px gap exactly, measured at 251 → 261 px.

**What the detector misread, each proven by measurement and held by the ratchet, not excused (10 pairs).**
- **The root's axis guard.** tokens.css R2 sets `html, body { overflow-x: clip }`. A fixed nav is never clipped by it
  (its containing block is the viewport). The ratchet exempts the root and a body that keeps the clip. index's body,
  which overrode it with Tailwind's `overflow-x-hidden`, was a real finding and was fixed.
- **The modal scrim read as a card.** The platform's modal contract (critique C7, `whModalA11y`, `whConfirm`) puts
  `role="dialog"` on the full-bleed overlay. Fixtures proved that a role plus a background makes a "card". The
  ratchet now re-runs the detector with the scrims unpainted and counts only what remains. A dialog that is itself the
  panel still counts (self-tested both ways).
- **A media-blind cascade.** On analytics-report, paper's white overrode the dark screen body by source order. The
  page now states each medium's colour once, so no medium depends on an override.
- **A cascade fight.** hive's unframed hero verdict was overriding a border it never wears. The frame now applies only
  to the other verdicts (`:not(.ss-hero)`).

**The instrument was learned, not guessed.** The detector is a compiled binary with no rule docs. Its rules were
measured on fixtures, and `.tmp/kprobe/bisect.mjs` isolated each finding to its element. Its first version pruned
siblings at only the last level, so a finding from elsewhere read as "this icon causes it"; it now prunes along the
whole path.

**Broke and caught in the same pass.** A comment inside offline-banner.js's CSS ("a \`top\` transition") closed the
JS template literal that sheet lives in. The shared offline banner died on every page, and the console blamed
utils.js. This lesson was already in memory and was not recalled at edit time. It is now a gate: `scripts-parse`
(`tools/validate_scripts_parse.mjs`, Platform, static, about 1s) compiles every shared script and every classic inline
script on 199 served files. Its self-test covers that backtick, a lost escape, a comment that mentions a script tag,
and an ES module. Its first run flagged two pages on exactly that comment case before the fix.

**Walked through the MCP browser** at 390 and 1280. Each row was read in the live render as its cast: Bryan for
"any", Leandro for the reports and analytics, Jun for engineering-design. The landing page was read signed out, as the
visitor who meets it. Integrations gates Jun as a hive-less owner (517 characters), so it was also read as the
supervisor it admits. One probe per antipattern ran on computed styles, live stylesheets and rendered text. The
offline banner was raised with the page's own `offline` event: it slides on `transform` while the page drops 38px in
one step. **74 of 74 readings pass.** The walk itself found the two runtime pulsing dots (assistant's voice dot,
logbook's voice-fill dot), which were fixed and re-walked.

**The lock.** `design-detector-ratchet` was rebased to **82 → 0**: any (file, antipattern) count that rises fails. Its
self-test gained the root clip and the scrim. `scripts-parse` is new. The bug-hunt inventory reads **K 37 → 0**.
`sw.js` is at v527.

**What the instrument still does not read (the next unit).** The ratchet's shared-chrome list is hand-written. Eleven

### §BRH.8 · Ten classes from Supabase's two emails: doors the database opened to anyone holding the public key, and a grant that stops on October 30 (Ian, 2026-10-21)

Ian: *"I just got an email from Vercel and Supabase, kindly check those and add appropriate number of trajectories in
our trajectories roadmap."* Then: *"use MCP to access my Gmail"*, and *"can you just be proactive?"*

**What the emails said** (read through the claude.ai Gmail connector: the connectors had not attached to the running
session, so a fresh headless session with only the Gmail tools read them):
- **Vercel, 2026-10-13** - Deployment Storage at 75% of 10 GB. The email that opened §BRH.2; class N holds it (13 rows,
  locking: the allowlist is built and gated, and closes on Ian's push and his deletion of the stored deployments).
- **Supabase, 2026-10-20, "Action required"** - critical, `rls_disabled_in_public`, project workhive, issues as of 17 Oct.
- **Supabase, 2026-10-20, "Final notice"** - from **2026-10-30** a new table in `public` gets no automatic Data API grant:
  every new table in this project, and every replay of the schema (a local `supabase db reset`, a preview branch, a new
  project).

**What production holds** (the claude.ai Supabase connector, read-only: `get_advisors` and one catalog SELECT). The email
names one lint; the advisor it links holds nine kinds - 13 public tables with RLS off · 5 SECURITY DEFINER views · 73
functions with a mutable search_path · 94 SECURITY DEFINER functions anon may execute (113 for authenticated) · 2
extensions in `public` · 1 materialized view in the API · leaked-password protection off · 12 RLS tables with no
policy (INFO). A fingerprint of production's schema against the local database found what no advisor reports: **ten
`debug_*` functions exist only in production**, every one executable by anon, six of them SECURITY DEFINER.

**Fixed before a row was seeded - the doors that need nothing but the public key** (`20261015500000_brh_close_anon_doors`):
- the ten `debug_*` functions are dropped. `debug_definer_all_workers()` ran past every policy and returned the ten
  highest-level workers' names and account ids to anyone; `debug_table_policies()` handed out any table's policy text;
- EXECUTE is taken from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated on six server-only writers whose bodies check no caller:
  `enqueue_user_push` (a Web Push to any account with any title, body and link), `consume_ai_global_budget` (spends the
  platform's daily AI budget until every AI feature refuses everyone), `ai_cache_bump`, `ai_cache_sweep_expired`,
  `prune_embedding_cache`, `record_ai_chain_depth`. Every caller is the service role or another definer function;
- `v_kpi_truth`'s SELECT is taken from anon (seven hives' KPIs to a signed-out visitor).

Reproduced first: the local database had never run `20260901000002`, the migration that DROPPED `enqueue_user_push` and
created its 5-argument version. Applying it opened the function to anon exactly as in production; `20261015500000`
closed it (anon and authenticated false, service_role true). **Applied locally. Production needs Ian's go-ahead, and the
migration must reach production BEFORE the commit is pushed: the repository is public, and the commit names the doors.**

**Two mechanisms the measurement taught.**
1. **A revoke from PUBLIC never reaches anon on Supabase.** Supabase grants EXECUTE to anon, authenticated and
   service_role explicitly on every new function, so `revoke ... from public` leaves anon's own grant standing. 32
   functions are closed on paper and open in fact - `my_logbook_summary`, written this morning, among them.
2. **DROP + CREATE restores the defaults.** A function dropped and re-created, or given a new signature, takes the
   default privileges again. `20260803000033` closed `enqueue_user_push`; `20260901000002` re-created it with
   `p_category`, and production served it to anyone from 2026-09-01. 7 functions.

#### The number - measured, printed with its arithmetic (`python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-bug-hunt --dry-run`, 2026-10-21)

| class | mechanism (what reaches a person) | measured from | layer | persona | rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| **P** | a public table anyone holding the public key can read, because RLS is off | advisor `rls_disabled_in_public` | S | oversight | **13** |
| **Q** | an object production holds that no migration creates | production's fingerprint against the local database: the ten `debug_*` functions | S | oversight | **10** |
| **R** | a view that runs as its owner, past the reader's row policies | advisor `security_definer_view` | S | oversight | **5** |
| **S** | a SECURITY DEFINER function anyone may execute, whose body checks no caller | advisor `anon_security_definer_function_executable` (94) against each local body: no caller check, not a trigger, not a Q object | S | oversight | **26** |
| **T** | a function whose search_path the caller can change | advisor `function_search_path_mutable` (73) less the five Q drops | S | oversight | **68** |
| **U** | an extension installed in `public` | advisor `extension_in_public` (vector, pg_net) | S | oversight | **2** |
| **V** | a materialized view the API serves past every row policy | advisor `materialized_view_in_api` (`v_kpi_truth`) | S | oversight | **1** |
| **W** | sign-up and password change accept passwords known to be leaked | advisor `auth_leaked_password_protection` | S | oversight | **1** |
| **X** | API access resting on the automatic grant that stops 2026-10-30 | local ACLs against the explicit GRANTs in 679 migrations, per (role, kind): service_role 173 tables · 63 views · 1 materialized view; anon 42 tables · 17 views; authenticated 36 tables · 7 views | CI | oversight | **7** |
| **Y** | a revoke a migration meant, which does not hold | the migrations' revokes against the local ACL: 32 revoked from PUBLIC only, 7 re-created after their revoke (a function S holds is counted once, there) | S | oversight | **39** |
| | | | | **= 172** | **BRH323..BRH494** |

Program: 16,682 in scope -> **16,854**. The critic extension gained 172 pending rows the same instant (R3). Not seeded:
the 12 INFO `rls_enabled_no_policy` tables (RLS on with no policy refuses anon and authenticated outright - the safe
state for a server-only table), and the 113 authenticated-executable definer functions as a class of their own (each
one's caller check is the subject of its S or Y row).

#### What a P..Y row is, and how it closes

Each row is an API probe made as the person the defect exposes - anon with only the public key, or a member of another
hive - walked by platform staff from the home (N's precedent). It closes when the probe is shown answering on demand,
the fix lands as a migration, and a gate reddens on revert. A row whose fix must reach production holds at its local
fix until Ian applies the migration, then closes on the advisor's re-read (`get_advisors` through the connector,
read-only). Gates earned with the first fixes: **S/Q/Y** - every anon-executable SECURITY DEFINER function carries a
declared reason, no `debug_*` function exists, and every function a migration closed to anon stays closed, including
after a re-creation; **P** - every public table has RLS on; **X** - a replay of the schema under the new default reaches
what each role reaches today, and every new table's migration carries its own GRANT.

#### Walk order (harm first; X before its deadline)

1. **S, Q** - the doors open to anyone. The six server-only writers and the ten debug functions are closed locally
   (`20261015500000`, production pending Ian); the other 20 S functions next, each kept only with a proof that it
   returns public facts.
2. **P** (13) - tables anyone reads: per table, the readers it needs. Seven have no page or edge reader at all.
3. **V** (1) - a member reading another hive's KPIs: a membership-checked read, and voice-handler.js pointed at it.
4. **Y** (39) - the revokes that do not hold.
5. **X** (7) - **before 2026-10-30**: the explicit-grant migration generated from today's ACL, the replay proof, the
   gate on new migrations.
6. **R** (5), **T** (68), **U** (2), **W** (1 - the switch is in Ian's Supabase dashboard).

#### Consumers that learned the classes (the bind audit)

`tools/supabase_advisor_evidence.py` (new: the committed `supabase_advisor_evidence.json`, built from the advisor,
production's fingerprint and the local database) · `tools/bug_hunt_inventory.py` (`advisor_sites`, classes P..Y) ·
`tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py` (`BRH_CLASS` P..Y) · `tools/critic_seed_missing.py` (+172) · the momentum guard (every
specced row is buildable).

- **A revoke from PUBLIC never reaches anon on Supabase, and DROP + CREATE restores the defaults** - 39 functions closed

### §BRH.9 · Six classes that keep the platform on two free plans: what Vercel stores, what the database keeps, and what production's AI is missing (Ian, 2026-10-21)

Ian, after §BRH.8: *"why is it, you just ignore my concerns and did not make necessary numbers of trajectories for
these to add for our trajectories roadmap, you know that my platform always free, and also in vercel, why is it I am
already at 70% where we deploy only my platform is not that massive, also I am not upgrading to pro, can you just be
proactive and do appropriately what is needed for my platform."*

He was right on three counts. §BRH.8's reply sent the Vercel storage back to him ("delete the old deployments"),
named two findings as "not yet trajectories", and offered the Pro plan for a check the platform already does for free.
The rule this section holds is that **no fix needs a paid plan.** The free plans are:

- **Vercel Hobby:** 10 GB of Deployment Storage. Old builds are removed outside a small protected set: the newest
  production builds and anything aliased.
- **Supabase Free:** a 500 MB database and 1 GB of storage. There are no daily backups, and a project is paused
  after 7 days of low activity.

**Measured** (`tools/free_plan_evidence.py` → `free_plan_evidence.json`):
- Vercel's record on the public repository, read without a credential.
- Vercel's own dashboard, signed in as the owner (`--dashboard`; no credential is kept).
- Production, read-only through the Supabase connector.
- The local tree.

- **Vercel: Deployment Storage stood at 9.90 of the free 10 GB, every day from 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-20.** That is
  the dashboard's own line; the emails' 70-75% was already behind it. The project keeps production builds for 30
  days and always its 10 newest, and it held 22. The 18 built before the allowlist `.vercelignore` (cd7bcfca,
  2026-10-14) each uploaded about **612.7 MB** under the old denylist, for a 19.5 MB site. They are 10 from
  2026-09-29 and 8 from 2026-10-13, and each of those two days raised the line by about 5 GB. The repository's record
  also shows 60 builds by a second project, *skillful-growth*, on 2026-04-25..26. That record is history: the
  dashboard lists one project, and *skillful-growth* stores nothing.
- **The database is 134 MB of the free 500 MB, and 77 MB of it (57%) was `cron.job_run_details`.** That was 443,228
  run records since April with nothing removing them. Four jobs run every minute, so about 5,800 rows arrived each
  day, roughly 350 MB a year: on its own, enough to carry the database past the free limit.
- **Photos are stored inside rows as base64:** 22 in `logbook.photo` (4.35 MB) and 5 in `inventory_items.photo`.
  23 list reads on 7 pages ship that column, so every load pays for every photo in free egress.
- **The AI's reference corpus is not in production.** `industry_standards` holds 10 rows there (0 embedded) against
  41 locally, `industry_standards_chunks` 0 against 781, and `persona_knowledge` 0 against 434. The embedding

  pages call, it is the only one.

| class | mechanism | measured from | layer | rows |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| **Z** | deployments that outgrow the free 10 GB of Deployment Storage | the repository's deployment record (2 projects, 785 builds) and Vercel's dashboard (1 project, 22 builds kept, 9.90 GB) | H | 2 |
