### §BRH.9a Walk — AB 8/8: a photo lives in Storage, and a list carries its name, never the picture (2026-10-22)

**What was wrong.** Production (read-only, 2026-10-21) held 22 logbook photos (4.35 MB) and 5 part photos (0.54 MB)
inside their rows as base64 text. The free 500 MB database grew with every photo while the free 1 GB of file storage
sat empty. Every read of such a row carried its photo, whether the screen showed it or not:
- the dayplanner read up to 1,001 logbook rows with `select *`;
- the inventory read up to 2,000 parts that way, four times;
- logbook's two feeds named `photo` in their column lists;
- both tables are in the realtime publication, so every change to a row with a photo also sent the photo to every
  subscriber.

**Reproduced on demand.** `tools/prove_photos_in_storage.py` makes rows that hold their photos as production does, then
reads them as the real cast (Rosa dela Cruz and Ben Ocampo of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet):

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| R1 the old read shape | `select=*` over 4 logbook rows: 825,202 bytes, 4 images |
| R2 the read the pages send | 3,702 bytes, 0 images (223x smaller); inventory 411,708 → 1,340 bytes |
| R3 a new inline photo, as the signed-in worker | HTTP 400 P0001, 0 rows written |
| R4 an upload into someone else's folder | refused |
| R5 who may see a photo | a teammate who can read the row: yes; before any row names it, an outsider, signed out: no |
| R6 deleting | refused while a row names the object; allowed to its owner once none does |
| R7 the one-time move | 6 of 6 copied, read back byte for byte, named, then cleared |

Every row and object the proof makes is its own and is removed at the end.

**The fix.**
- Migration `20261021000010`:
  - a private bucket `entry-photos` (1 MB, images only);
  - the row keeps `photo_path` and a 160 px `photo_thumb_path`, and a CHECK keeps image data out of both;
  - a photo is readable by its uploader, or by whoever can read a row that names it. The policy asks
    `wh_entry_photo_visible`, which runs as the reader, so the tables' own RLS decides and a photo is exactly as
    private as its entry;
  - uploads go only into the uploader's folder, and an object a row still names cannot be deleted by a client;
  - the server refuses new inline image data. A legacy row can still re-send its own photo unchanged, so a page left
    open across the deploy keeps saving.
- `utils.js`:
  - `whPhotoSettle` uploads a picked photo before its row;
  - `whPhotoHydrate` draws photos by name from one signed-URL request;
  - `whPhotoDrop` takes back an upload no row names;
  - `whRowCols` gives every column except `photo`.
- Every write path uploads first:
  - logbook: new entry, edit, offline drain;
  - inventory: the part form, the offline queue (a new `prepare` step in `offline-queue.js`, stored before the
    write so a retry never uploads twice), and the old-device migration.
- An edit sends the photo columns only when the person changed the photo, so it can never erase one by accident.
- The six list reads on dayplanner, hive and inventory now read `whRowCols`. The logbook feeds name the two paths, and
  the logbook insert reads back its id only.

**Walked** at phone-390 (CPU 4x slower) and desktop-1280, with no model called, on 26 page visits:
- 0 reads asked for a picture;
- 8 stored photos were drawn by name, and all 8 painted.

Ben saved a 1.39 MB camera photo through Log a Repair. The page made two uploads (163,738 + 7,349 bytes), then a
1,029-byte insert with `photo` NULL. From there:
- a text edit kept the photo's names;
- a replacement deleted the old objects only after the write landed;
- Remove cleared both the names and the objects;
- an offline save kept the picture in the queue and uploaded it before a 919-byte insert on reconnect.

Rosa's part photo went the same way. Ben, as her teammate, sees its thumbnail.

**Found along the way:**
1. **The detector over-counted.** Of the 23 "photo-shipping list reads", 14 were writes without `.select()`, which
   return no rows; 9 were real. `free_plan_evidence.photo_reads` now reads only reads, understands
   `whRowCols('<source>')` and resolves column constants. On HEAD it finds the 9; on the tree, 0. So BRH505
   (integrations) and BRH508 (pm-scheduler) were measurement errors: those pages never shipped a photo. Their rows
   say so.
2. **Save Entry stayed disabled after any successful edit.** `cancelEditMode` put back the label and not the button,
   so the next job could not be logged until a reload. Fixed.
3. **An instrument went blind in LB3.** Since LB3, the logbook list draws rows with `content-visibility: auto`, and
   `prove_captured_fields_are_readable` counted badges with `innerText`. A card below the fold has no rendered text,
   so a badge the card held read as absent. It counts `textContent` now (1 of 1). Other provers that count long-list
   rows by `innerText` need the same audit.
4. **Two reds that predate this change are fixed.** `_headers` lacked `api.pwnedpasswords.com`, which `vercel.json`
   grants (drift). `whUseThen` had an unmarked empty `.catch`.
5. **An instrument hazard.** The local gateway answers a refused upload before reading a large body, and the unread
   bytes stall the next request on that connection for a minute. The proof's refused upload uses a small body.
6. **`cdn.plot.ly` answered 503** to the host and to the browser on 2026-10-21/22. `analytics.html` loaded Plotly only
   from there, so its charts failed whenever that CDN did. **Fixed the same day:**
   - Plotly 2.26.0 is now served from this origin (`vendor/plotly-basic-2.26.0.min.js`). It was taken from the npm
     mirrors, and its SHA-384 equals the integrity value the page had always pinned, so it is the same file. Like
     `vendor/supabase-js`, it is not precached.
   - `.gitattributes` keeps `vendor/**` out of line-ending conversion, so a Windows checkout cannot change the bytes
     the hash pins.
   - Analytics' policy and the base policy no longer name the CDN. `build_csp_profiles` merged analytics into the
     group whose policy names only what its code loads; 10 policies became 9. Analytics was re-measured into its own
     file and merged, so the full sweep's record was not overwritten.
   - Walked as Rosa: the script loaded 200 from the origin at 390 and 1280, and the Predictive phase drew its charts.
7. **`csp-ratchet` had been red since ENH-R (2026-10-19).** The Sources nudge was index.html's 13th un-nonced inline
   script. It is now the first line of the inline script that already follows the area: the same moment, and the same
   guard, so skew-heal still names it. `render_sources_area` accepts and holds that form; there are 3 new self-test
   cases. The count is back to 12.
8. **`prove_recovery_path` found controls by `innerText` only.** It now falls back to `textContent`, so a card below
   the fold of a long list is still found by its words. `prove_stored_text_escaped` already counted with `textContent`.

**Gates.**
- `photos-in-storage`, new: 21 mutants. The pre-fix files of the six pages, `utils.js` and `offline-queue.js` turn it
  red with 30 problems. Its live part (bucket, policies, invoker function, CHECKs, a rolled-back refusal probe, no
  inline rows) skips when the database is down and turns red if a live query fails.
- `free-plan-budget`: F3 is now 0 (it was 23).
- `file-storage-owned`: the two photo pickers' disposition is now "stored".

**Where it stands.** BRH501–508 are walked, banked and CLOSED (60%, locking).

**Owed: the production move.** It is outward, so it is the owner's step:
1. Push the migration and the pages.
2. Run `tools/move_inline_photos_to_storage.py --target prod`. This is the copy pass: each photo is uploaded as it is,
   read back byte for byte, then named on its row, and the inline text stays so old pages keep showing it. It needs
   `WH_PHOTO_MOVE_URL` and `WH_PHOTO_MOVE_SERVICE_KEY` in the environment.
3. Once the new pages are live, run it again with `--clear`.

**NEXT:**
- LB3's six open rows with the CPU-time instrument (the walk now traces every measured visit and books each task at
  its main-thread CPU time x the throttle);
- then LB4 (35), RL1 (31), RL2 (24), RL3 (36).

### §BRH.8b Walk — the database classes, live: 177 of 177 closed (2026-10-22)

The P..Y rows were fixed and gated on 2026-10-21 from API probes and production's advisor, and the ledger still counted
all of them OPEN. Each row declares `playwright-mcp + postgres-mcp` at both viewports, and none held a receipt from that
instrument. `tools/brh_db_walk.py` is the walk §BRH.8 describes: "an API probe made as the person the defect exposes,
walked by platform staff from the home".
- The platform admin signs in through the product's form on index.html at phone-390 and desktop-1280.
- From that page, every probe goes through a second client that holds only the public key: a stranger.
- A positive control runs first (the public listing grid, which a stranger may read: 20 rows), so an instrument
  refused everything cannot pass as a fix.
- Each probe's expected answer comes from the gate that holds its class, never from the walker. Definer-doors supplies
  SIGNED_OUT and POLICY_HELPERS (what a stranger keeps); public-read-surface supplies DECLARED (what a stranger may read).
- A volatile function the catalog still lets anon run is never called: a probe must not write.
- The catalog is read through the postgres MCP and saved with the MCP's own digest of each result set (equal to psql's).

**What the walk showed.**

| Class | Rows | What the stranger met |
|---|---:|---|
| P | 13 | 8 declared-public tables answered; 5 refused (401, no grant) |
| Q | 10 | the `debug_*` functions do not exist (PGRST202) |
| R | 5 | the two public grids answered; one service view refused outright |
| S | 26 | 15 refused (42501); 8 declared reads answered; 3 volatile ones kept by declaration, not called |
| T | 68 | each function's search_path pinned (the catalog) |
| V | 1 | `v_kpi_truth` refused |
| Y | 39 | 32 refused; the 7 policy helpers answered false or empty |
| X | 7 | anon and authenticated still read through their explicit grants; service_role holds every public table (180), view (66) and the materialized view (the catalog), with api-grants-explicit |
| U | 1 | vector lives in `extensions` |
| AA | 4 | each purge job ran today |
| AE | 1 | the keep-alive's own question answers (41 rows) |
| W | 1 | the sign-up form refused `password123` before any account request; `/auth/v1/signup` was blocked at the network and never asked |
| AD | 1 | the worker's hive board never asked `compute_hive_readiness`; a snapshot aged past 24 hours refreshed through `refresh_hive_readiness` (200), and a fresh one needed no call |

**Two lessons, built into the instruments.**
1. **A stranger's 0 over an empty view proves nothing.** Two service views returned 0 rows to a stranger, and 0 rows
   to the database too. The verdict now counts a 200-with-0 as a refusal only when a party reads rows. Two rows were
   staged (a broadcast, and a job en route), Bryan Garcia read 1 from each through a second in-page client while the
   stranger read 0, and both rows were then removed with their journal events.
2. **The name of the thing is not the question, a fourth time.** Eight walked rows sat open because the ledger routed
   them by a word in their object's name: "cache" went to the profiler, "emails" and "delivery" to the mail catcher,
   "cron" to grafana. `live_walk_manifest.py` now routes these classes by their own lens sentence. The rule is
   disclosed beside it: added in the same session as the walks, and removing it re-opens exactly those eight.

**Still open in BRH, each for a reason outside this machine:**
- N (11) and Z (1) are re-probed on workhiveph.com after the deploy.
- BRH445 (pg_net) moves with a switch in the Supabase dashboard.
- BRH515 (backups) and AC (5, production's AI corpus) are owed on production.

**AE's backup gap closed locally (BRH515 → locking, 2026-10-29).** Supabase Free keeps no daily backups, and nothing in
the repository took one. `.github/workflows/backup.yml` now runs `tools/backup_dump.sh` every day at 02:41 UTC:
- It dumps roles, schema and data the way Supabase's restore guide does (`supabase db dump`, CLI 2.90.0 pinned).
- It encrypts the files with `gpg --symmetric` under a passphrase before anything reaches the upload directory.
- It decrypts its own output and counts every COPY block, then keeps only the `.gpg` file as the run's artifact for 30
  days. The repository is public, so a readable dump would be readable by anyone.

The script's header says how to restore. Without both secrets the run fails and names what is missing, because a backup
that was not taken must never show green.

`backup-roundtrip` (`tools/prove_backup_roundtrip.py`) runs the same script against the local database with a passphrase
made for the run. It proved:
- 213 tables, 54 MB encrypted, and the first packet is a passphrase-encrypted session key.
- No COPY line, table definition or hive name can be read in the file.
- A wrong passphrase is refused.
- The 23 critical tables' 35,233 rows are each counted in the backup.
- `hives`, `logbook` and `inventory_items` restore into a scratch schema row for row (count plus md5).

`free-plan-budget` F6 holds the workflow and the script. Its 7 new mutants: the workflow or its schedule taken out, the
passphrase not passed, the whole out-dir uploaded, the encryption or the read-back taken out, the dump written beside the
upload.

**Owed (the owner's):** two repository secrets, set once.
- `SUPABASE_DB_URL`: the session pooler string from the project's Connect panel. The runner has no IPv6 route to the
  direct connection.
- `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE`: 20 characters or more, kept outside the repository.

The first green scheduled run is the row's last witness. Not covered: Storage objects (the photos AB moved there). A
database dump does not carry them, and Supabase's own guide transfers them separately.

### §BRH.10 · Seven classes from what the 2026-10-24 release left open: the signed-in product never checked on production, a cause the analytics cannot group, a census that credits lookalikes, free credit no gate holds, and photos the release hid (Ian, 2026-10-24)

Ian, on the release report's open items: *"can we be proactive on this below, you have to understand these first, and
make a necessary and appropriate number of trajectories to add for the existing number of trajectories in our
trajectories roadmap."* The count is derived, never typed: `tools/release_followup_evidence.py` measures each item from
the source, the local database and production (read-only through the Supabase connector, `--prod
.tmp/release_followup_prod.json`), `tools/bug_hunt_inventory.py` turns each measured site into one row, and
`tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-bug-hunt` seeded **49 rows, BRH519..BRH567** (16,722 -> 16,771 in scope).

**What each item is, once understood:**

- **The signed-in product was never checked on production (AF 2, AG 26, AH 5).** The deploy's smoke walked the 120
  public pages; its signed-in tier and the runbook's five Tier-0 flows did not run, because production has no account
  the smoke can sign in with. Reading the instrument showed that credentials alone would not have been enough:
  `tools/post_deploy_smoke.mjs:71` seeds a LOCAL hive (Baguio Textile Mills' id), a worker name and the supervisor
  role into storage instead of asking the server who the account is, so against production it would claim a hive the
  account is not in - the "stored hive is a cache of a server fact" class, in the instrument. AF is the instrument
  and the identity (an account with its own bench hive holding no tenant's data, credentials only in `.env`, the
  smoke refusing to act outside it). AG is one row per page of the smoke's app roster: the page opened on production
  as the bench supervisor after a deploy, its own UI drawn, no page error. AH is one row per Tier-0 flow (sign in; a
  logbook entry; one AI action within budget; a parts reservation accepted twice fast on asset-hub, proving the
  UNIQUE; the logs read for 54000/23505/500), each walked in the bench hive with its writes undone.
- **A breakdown cause the analytics cannot group (AI 8).** The logbook form offers 12 causes. Three writers store
  the cause as said instead: the voice entry (`voice-logbook-entry` asks the model for "diagnosed cause if
  mentioned"), the CSV import (`integrations.html`) and the CMMS sync (`cmms-sync`). Four readers group by the exact
  text: repeat failures (`descriptive.py`, machine x cause), the Pareto (`diagnostic.py`), and the failure-signature
  scan's two rules - `repeat_failure` keys on the lower-cased text, so a reworded cause hides a real repeat, and
  `multi_symptom` counts distinct texts, so one cause said three ways raises a false multi-symptom alert. Locally 11
  stored causes sit outside the list (10 written by the AI eval bench's voice runs); production has 0 of 28 today, so
  this is preventive there and real here. The fix keeps what was said beside a cause from the list, and every reader
  groups by the listed cause.
- **An adoption census that credits lookalikes (AJ 4).** `tools/component_adoption_census.class_used` matches
  `\bcls\b`, and `\b` treats "-" as a word edge, so heat-tile counts as .tile, pulse-card as .card and stat-pill as
  .pill. Measured: .card 21 pages, .pill 19, .tile 5, .filter-chip 2 credited without the class. Correcting it lowers
  those floors; each row names its lowered floor with the pages that never adopted, and each such page converges on
  the canonical component or is recorded as a justified bespoke container.
- **Free credit no gate holds to its policy (AK 2).** Starter grants are free credit by design (500 credits, once per
  verified seller, against the supply cap). `validate_credit_solvency.py`'s one rule is vouchers <= revenue, and it
  never asks the grant records. Production's one grant follows the policy (once, 500, to a KYB-verified seller), so
  the gate row is preventive. The console row is not: the corrected liability cover reads 0.00x in red on production
  (no top-ups, 500 credits owed, all of it free starter credit) and says nothing about why. The fix splits what is
  owed by its backing so a low cover reads with its reason.
- **A release that shipped ahead of its data move (AL 2) - the urgent one.** BRH-AB moved photos out of their rows,
  and since the 2026-10-24 deploy the pages read only a photo's stored path (`whRowCols` leaves the inline column
  out). Production's copy pass has not run: **22 logbook photos and 5 part photos show nothing on production right
  now** (`v_logbook_truth` returns no path for all 22). The pictures are intact in their rows. The copy pass is the
  owner's step (`tools/move_inline_photos_to_storage.py --target prod`, with `WH_PHOTO_MOVE_URL` and
  `WH_PHOTO_MOVE_SERVICE_KEY`), is non-destructive (it keeps the inline text), and restores every photo; `--clear`

### §BRH.11 · Two defects met in Ian's own hands: no install icon to tap, and a hub panel swallowed at the top of the screen (Ian, 2026-10-26)

Ian, the same day the lens plan was being drawn: *"Since my app is a webapp, users should have something icon where
they can just click or tap to easily install it and visible right away on their homescreen for desktop and phone"* and
*"Navhub is slop, like when you open or tap it it becomes invisible when opened. then also when you open it and put it
at the top, the open where all the of it is being swallowed at the top, it is not the same in ios that it will also
adjust to keep it not being swallowed … make appropriate and necessary number of trajectories for these above also."*
The count is derived, never typed: two site functions in `tools/bug_hunt_inventory.py` measured each from the pages,
`manifest.json`, the PNGs and `nav-hub.js`; `tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-bug-hunt` seeded **94 rows,
BRH568..BRH661** (16,771 -> 16,865 in scope), against the pre-fix source so the replay keeps them once the fixes land.

**What each defect is, once measured:**

- **An install icon a person cannot find (AM 34).** The only install control lived on the landing page inside the
  desktop header (`hidden md:flex`) and showed only after `beforeinstallprompt` — which iOS Safari never fires and
  Chromium fires only once its installability test passes — so a person on a phone never saw it anywhere; 29 other
  hub hosts had no control at all. The icon that would have landed was wrong three ways: `manifest.json` declared one
  640x640 transparent PNG as 192x192 and 512x512 and `maskable` (Android masks a maskable icon to its 80% safe zone
  and fills the rest from the icon's own edge, so a transparent logo is cropped on a see-through ground); the
  apple-touch-icon the hub injects on every host (`nav-hub.js` head boilerplate) pointed at a RELATIVE
  `workhive-logo-tight.png` — a file that lives in `brand_assets/` and not at the root, so it 404'd on the root pages
  and, resolving against the served url, under every `/learn/` and `/tools/` page too (the
  [[feedback_a_relative_ref_resolves_against_the_served_url]] class) — and that file was 768x543, which iOS letterboxes.
  One row per host with no control at rest (30), one per wrong icon fact (3), and one that asks rather than accuses:
  the installed app's `start_url /` must land a signed-in person at their home under the declared name and theme.
- **The hub's panel opens where a person cannot see it (AN 60).** `#wh-hub-panel` was anchored by `bottom: 68px`
  (nav-hub.js:885) and so always grew UPWARD from the FAB; the drag clamped the FAB's bottom to `innerHeight - 80`
  (:1752) and said nothing about the panel; nothing read `env(safe-area-inset-top)`; the stored position
  (`wh-hub-position`) was clamped once at load and never again, while iOS changes `innerHeight` every time Safari's
  toolbar collapses — which is the "iOS does not adjust" Ian saw. Two rows per hub host (30 x 2): the panel opened
  where the FAB rests, and the panel opened after the FAB is dragged to the top. **Reproduced before the fix** by
  `tools/prove_hub_panel_on_screen.mjs` against nav-hub.js `6e5888860c79`: at rest the panel sat inside the viewport
  (61..752 of 844); planted at the top it opened at **-679..12 of 844** on hive and logbook at both viewports — the
  12px sliver Ian described, with `elementFromPoint` at the header finding nothing.

**The fixes, landed the same day (one shared change each, the per-host rows what a person meets — BRH-D's shape):**

- **AN** — `nav-hub.js`: `placePanel()` measures the room above and below the FAB (the safe-area insets read through
  `--wh-sat`/`--wh-sab`, since `env()` is CSS-only) and anchors the panel on the side that has it
  (`#wh-hub.wh-panel-below`), capped to that room so it scrolls rather than clips; `clampBottom()` honours the top
  inset in the drag and at load; the position is re-clamped on every `resize`. After the fix the planted-top case
  opens **below** the FAB at 92..793 of 844 — 32 of 32 cases green across Chromium AND WebKit, both viewports, four
  hosts. Gate **`hub-panel-on-screen`** (`tools/validate_hub_panel_on_screen.py`): the static facts in nav-hub.js (a
  revert reddens it without a browser) + the prover's report taken against THIS nav-hub.js (`nav_hub_sha`) with
  WebKit required.
- **AM** — an Install control in the hub's assist row on every host, visible at rest, acting per platform: the native
  prompt where the browser has one, the per-platform guide with the icon that lands everywhere else (iOS Safari:
  Share -> Add to Home Screen; Chrome on iPhone: open in Safari; Android: the browser menu; desktop: the address-bar
  icon — report-sender's copy, now one source), hidden once installed; `window.WHHub.openInstallGuide` lets the
  landing's three buttons (header, mobile menu, and a new hero control) show at rest and fall back to the guide
  instead of doing nothing. True renditions cut from the 1024 source with PIL: `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`,
  `icon-512-maskable.png` (the logo at 72% on the hub's navy), `apple-touch-icon-180.png` (iOS fills transparency
  with black, so a solid ground is the honest icon); `manifest.json` declares each at its true size and purpose; the
  hub injects the apple-touch-icon root-absolute with `sizes="180x180"`. Gate **`install-affordance`**
  (`tools/validate_install_affordance.py`): the measure itself — `install_affordance_sites()` must return nothing but
  the `start_url` lens and the shared chrome must carry a control visible at rest; the browser half is the prover's
  `install` case. After both fixes the inventory reads **AM 1 (the carried `start_url` lens) · AN 0**.

| class | rows | ids | layer | cast | whose step first |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AM an install icon a person cannot find | 34 | BRH568-601 | F | worker / supervisor (gate-checked per host) | local - built the same day; the per-host walks bank them |
| AN the hub's panel opens off the screen | 60 | BRH602-661 | F | worker / supervisor / returner | local - built the same day; the all-hosts sweep banks them |

## §KA · KEEP ABREAST — SEO · AEO · GEO as a living system, not a static one (Ian, 2026-10-26)

Ian: *"I want to also you add necessary appropriate numbers of my SEO AEO GEO … because my issues is, it's like static,
I want it its always keeping up to date or that will trigger or trip that we need that it needs to keep abreast
also."* Measured the same day, the lane was static in exactly that way: Wave O (T151–T162) locked since August with 0
open rows; 109 of 120 sitemap `<lastmod>` values read May or August — typed as `today` by `scaffold_article.py` at
scaffold time and never derived again — while 115 URLs promised `monthly`; the refresh queue
(`content_freshness_report.json`) held all 6 pillars and all 4 comparisons at 78 days against a 30-day target and the
census that ranks it is ADVISORY on the board, so nothing consumed it; the IndexNow key was live and `indexnow_submit.py`
existed, but no runbook step called it and no receipt existed — the 2026-10-24 release shipped 120 pages the index was
never told about; `seo_scoreboard.json` was hand-run on 2026-09-06 and hard-coded "deployed to production 0/1" four
releases after launch; 59 of 62 SEO evidence chunks in `substrate/external/` were past their 30-day TTL; two nightly CI
jobs ran and neither carried any of it.

**The structure, built first (the trajectory registry is the inbox):**
- `tools/freshness_trip.py` — the trip. Reads the refresh queue, the spine's TTL (68 chunks: the 45 the program cites
  plus the SEO-topic rest), the sitemap against the pages' own `dateModified`, the AI-crawler roster chunks against
  `robots.txt`, the scoreboard's age, the IndexNow and share-of-voice receipts; writes `seo_trip_report.json`;
  `--seed` re-opens the KA row whose unit tripped (status back to `specced`, the trip in its basis) — a trip is a row
  Ian meets in this roadmap, not a log line. On the board as **`seo-trip`** (WARN, never FAIL: a failing gate here would
  reward a fake date bump, the census's own reasoning); on the header as the generated **KEEP ABREAST** line; in CI as
  the `keep-abreast` nightly job of its own, red only when a trip is past its grace (window + 14 days — neglect, not
  natural ageing). First reading: **246 trips open, 245 past grace**.
- `tools/refresh_public_page.py` — a refresh is a PAIRED WRITE across five surfaces (JSON-LD `dateModified`, the visible
  Last-updated line, `<lastmod>`, the markdown twin, the IndexNow push) and **refuses a date-only change** (the content
  hash with its dates masked must have moved). `--sync-sitemap` derives every `<lastmod>` FROM the page's own date and
  `<changefreq>` from the kind's window — nothing invented: **112 entries moved**, the two hubs keep `weekly`. Gate
  **`sitemap-promise`** (FAIL) now holds it: 120/120. The trip then read **78 open / 77 past grace** (refresh 10 ·
  evidence 65 · board · push · voice 1 each) — the 168 sitemap disagreements were one derivation away.
- `tools/seo_scoreboard.py` on the board (**`seo-scoreboard`**, regenerates every full run; it had read "deployed 0/1"
  because nobody re-ran it); the IndexNow push written into `PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_RUNBOOK.md` as a standing post-deploy
  step with its receipt (`indexnow_receipts.json`).

**The rows (seeded by `seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-keep-abreast`, THE NUMBER from the trip's census, never typed):**

| lens | the row asks | derivation | rows | ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **KA-R** the refresh, per public URL | the five freshness surfaces agree; inside its kind's window or holding an open refresh; a refresh is content, never a date | 120 sitemap URLs | 120 | KA1–120 |
| **KA-E** the evidence, per source | within its TTL; on re-fetch a changed sha produces a diff note and a decision on the lever it anchors | 68 spine chunks (45 cited + 23 SEO-topic) | 68 | KA121–188 |
| **KA-S** the engines' side, per URL | pushed (an IndexNow receipt) after its last change; indexed state read when the credential exists, never assumed | 120 sitemap URLs | 120 | KA189–308 |

**366 rows, KA1..KA366** (16,865 → 17,231 in scope). Layer B stays honest: KA-V's engine half runs through Ian's
monthly 45-prompt sheet (`geo_sov_audit.py --template` / `--score`) — never a paid API; KA-S closes on what we control
(the push and its receipt), the indexed-state read enriching the row once the one shared Search Console credential row

**KA-E walked — 62 of 68 banked, 2 descoped, 4 open on blocked sources (2026-10-31).** Every cited source past its TTL

## §HS · The hive at its full size: thirty members, their roles, their tenants, at the same time (Ian, 2026-10-29)

Ian, after finding his workmates' older posts cluttered on production's community page: *"you have to expand our
trajectories roadmap with appropriate and necessary number of trajectories that based or anchor in the logic of my
platform, where there are multiple tenants like multi tenancy, Role Based, with up to 30 hive members, how they behave
when they have a post, or lists of, concurrency, anything needed numbers of trajectories, just expand my ideas and
understand my ideas first, then add on for those what I have missed."*

**The idea, understood.** A hive is a tenant of up to thirty members, and the platform has to be measured the way a full
hive uses it:
- Each member holds a role (worker, supervisor) and may belong to more than one hive.
- What members make (posts, log entries, parts, PM completions, projects, listings) is a LIST every other member reads.
- On that list the same item offers different actions to its author, a teammate and a supervisor.
- Thirty people act at once: two touch the same item, a whole shift writes in the same minutes.

The community defect was all of it on one card. A supervisor's view of a teammate's post was 300px tall for two lines,
with:
- the text indented behind an avatar-only gutter;
- the date dropped onto its own line;
- four reaction pills reading "0";
- a row of four icon-only moderation buttons;
- the page's floating controls on top.

Fixed the same day: the card is 201px with one "Post actions" menu that names every action. No gate saw any of it,
because none looked at a list as a full hive's member reads it.

**Ian's six ideas → seven lenses:**

| Ian said | lens | the row asks |
|---|---|---|
| posts / lists of 30 | **L1** thirty members' items, read as a list | each item legible at 390 and 1280; a count only when there is one; no row holding a lone control; nothing fixed over it |
| role based | **L2** each role sees the actions it may take | author, teammate and supervisor each get exactly their actions, named in words, in one place; the busiest view is as clean as the quietest |
| multi tenancy | **L7** a member of two hives | only the active hive's items; switching hives replaces the list whole; an action lands in the list's own hive |
| concurrency | **W1** two members change the same item at once | one change lands; the other member is told what changed and by whom; nothing lost silently |
| concurrency, at 30 | **W2** a shift of thirty writes at once | no honest write refused by a per-person or per-hive limit; every item kept in order; a waiting write says so |

**What the ideas missed - added:**

| lens | why |
|---|---|
| **L3** a teammate's new item arrives as you read | thirty members make items while others read; realtime must not move what you are reading or typing |
| **L4** a year of the hive | thirty members fill a list fast; paged, counted honestly past the cap, searchable |
| **L5** a member who has left | thirty is not a fixed thirty; an item outlives its author's membership |
| **L6** thirty names | long, alike and duplicate display names; "mine" by account (the name-is-not-an-identity family) |
| **H1** presence at thirty | the "Online now" row with thirty people |
| **H2** the @mention picker at thirty | the right member within two letters; namesakes told apart |
| **H3** thirty open channels | thirty members with a page open, inside the Free plan's realtime budget (connections, messages) |
| **H4** thirty members on one hive's AI budget | the one who reaches it is told; everyone else keeps working |

**THE NUMBER, measured by `tools/hive_scale_census.py` (never typed).** The units come from `canonical_registry.json`'s
surfaces × each relation's own columns × the page source:
- **61 member lists:** a hive-scoped relation with an author column, read with `.order`/`.range`, on 24 pages.
- **41 member writes:** written, attributed, trail excluded.
- **Hive features:** presence 2 · mention picker 1 · realtime 12 · AI 8.

A cell is empty when no in-scope row names its unit AND its ask on that page; L7 skips founder pages, which read across
hives by design.

| L1 | L2 | L3 | L4 | L5 | L6 | L7 | W1 | W2 | H1 | H2 | H3 | H4 | **total** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 60 | 61 | 61 | 45 | 60 | 61 | 44 | 37 | 37 | 2 | 1 | 10 | 7 | **486** |

**486 rows, HS1..HS486** (37,479 → 37,965 in scope), seeded by `seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-hive-scale`. They are wired
in the same change into:
- the registry validator's positional replay;
- the LXP replay's exclusions (it renamed two LXP waves until HS was excluded - the fourth wave to teach that);
- the priority tiers;
- the header's wave names;
- the ledger's declared instrument.

**Where they sit in the order:**
- **T1:** L1, L2 and W1 on production pages (130 rows) - what a person in a full hive meets today.
- **T4:** the other production lenses.
- **T5:** founder lists (73).

**The instrument - built 2026-10-29:** a thirty-member hive (the seed's hives hold 3 to 9 members each).
`test-data-seeder/seeders/full_hive.py` seeds Batangas Refinery Maintenance (pinned id `30303030-…`) with its own
`Random(30)`, run by the orchestrator after the walk casts:
- **Members:** 30 - 3 supervisors and 27 workers. Display names are unique per hive (`UNIQUE hive_id, worker_name`), so L6
  uses long and alike names: a "Jr.", Ana/Anna, Joel/Joey.
- **L7:** Liza Mercado also holds a seat in Baguio Textile Mills.
- **L5:** Rodel Ignacio has left (`deactivated`); his work stays on the lists.
- **A year of attributed work:**
  - 420 log entries by all 30;
  - 220 PM completions on 10 assets;
  - 40 parts with 220 stock movements, each ledger built by `inventory.py`'s `_gen_ledger`, so stock is conserved;
  - 4 projects with 32 items;
  - 70 posts by 29 members, with 193 replies and 491 reactions.

Two seed truths it exposed, both fixed in the seed:
- **XP:** the XP triggers stamped every seeded row now(), so five years of work read as 23,778 XP events "this week".
  `orchestrator.date_seeded_xp` dates each XP row to the work that earned it (233 remain this week), and `query-indexes`
  holds again.
- **The reputation probe** chose the top XP holder whatever the RPC is defined for; its fixture now requires a public post,
  a badge or a seller profile.

**T1 walked - 2026-10-30: all 99 L1/L2 rows on 21 pages, locking.** `tools/prove_hive_scale_lists.mjs` (gate
`hive-scale-lists`, skip_if_fast) signs in as Joel Cruz (worker) and Ernesto Villareal (supervisor) of the full hive, reads
every item of each member list at phone-390 and desktop-1280 (who, when, no zero count, no line of unnamed controls,
nothing fixed over it, inside the screen) and replays every action an item offers as that person in a rolled-back
transaction. Lists of one's own work are judged as "exactly mine"; reads the census counted in dead code are measured by
request capture. `tools/bank_hs_rows.py` banks a row only from a fresh, non-teeth receipt of a 30-member hive.

What it found (each fixed, the server-side ones locked by a psql probe that fails on the old policy):
- **The server looser than the page** - migrations 20261030000001..5: a worker could publish/unpublish their post and a
  supervisor rewrite a member's words (`community__sharing_is_the_supervisors`, `community__a_posts_words_are_its_authors`);
  a worker could not report an announcement; any member could rewrite or delete any FMEA mode, approved ones included
  (`asset-hub__a_failure_mode_is_its_proposers`); a project's own team could not read its roster
  (`project-manager__a_team_reads_its_roster`); any member could write the CMMS sync pushed to SAP
  (`integrations__only_a_supervisor_writes_the_cmms_sync`).
- **Lists that did not say who or when** - logbook asset history and part uses, inventory part history (it showed only the
  viewer's own movements), FMEA rows, project link-picker options, CMMS conflict cards, the project-report chooser,
  marketplace and seller-profile cards, hive's PM card (a time of day with no date), community's reason line (a code).
- **Only at scale** - the project link picker THREW past 50 rows (`const` reassigned; new gate `const-not-reassigned`);
  low-stock alerts keyed by part NAME (two bins hid each other); a departed member offered as an assignee; the asset
  marketplace card matched nothing (discipline vs equipment-type vocabularies).
- **Seed structure the walk needed** (full_hive.py, own random streams, existing rows linked once with triggers off):
  an asset register with links, FMEA modes, PM tasks, project owners/dates/WBS/teams/change orders/progress, calcs,
  CMMS work orders, two sellers with inquiries, a freelance provider; `orchestrator.attribute_seeded_trail` gives every
  seeded trail row to the member who did it.

**W1 - the database half, 2026-10-30: 31 rows at 45% (`fixing`).** `tools/prove_hive_scale_writes.mjs` (gate
`hive-scale-writes`) replays each two-member race in one rolled-back transaction as the two people, with the page's own
write and guard (teeth: five planted unguarded writes fail). Found and fixed: an alert dismissal REPLACED a teammate's record
and the first Undo deleted the second's; community's edit conflict threw away the typed text; two supervisors removing one
member both "succeeded" and "transfer supervisor and leave" could promote a removed member and leave no supervisor; logbook's
asset edit and project-manager's status button overwrote a teammate's change; two supervisors importing one CMMS file logged
every work order twice. Still owed per row: the two-context BROWSER walk that watches the sentence the second member sees
(today held statically by `oc-guard-speaks` and named in each scenario) - the rows say so and are not counted closed.

**W1 - the browser half, 2026-10-30: 31 races walked by two people in two browsers.** `tools/prove_hive_scale_races.mjs`
(gate `hive-scale-races`, board-only, ~45 min) opens the page for member A at phone-390 and member B at desktop-1280, then
swaps them; A holds the item, B changes it first, A acts through the page's own control, and the walk reads A's screen
for the page's sentence and the database for B's change. Every touched row is snapshotted and restored. Where the live
feed would bring B's change to A first (a task's status, an acknowledgement), A's connection is dropped, as a phone in a
basement would - with it up, the move reaches A and A's tap is an honest next move, which the walk also recorded. Six
defects the database half could not see, each walked FAILING on the HEAD page before its fix:
- **inventory's part edit overwrote a teammate silently** - its guard read the stamp (and the count) from the LIVE cache,
  which the realtime feed refreshes, so B's save reached the cache first and A's stale form matched B's stamp ("Part
  updated."); an untouched count field undid a teammate's use through `inventory_adjust`. Snapshotted at form open now.
  The sweep of every `updated_at` guard that followed found the same class twice more: asset-hub's RCM strategy editor
  (`rcm_strategies` feed) and project-manager's lessons-learned (`projects` feed, whose conflict branch also reloaded the
  pane and wiped the writer's text) - both snapshot when the person starts, both walked (`X-STRATEGY`, `X-LESSONS`).
- **the offline machine merge duplicated** - a fresh uuid per run, so two tabs or devices merging the same local list
  wrote two rows (HEAD: 2 rows, both pairings); the id is now SHA-256 of the account and the tag, upserted ignoring
  duplicates.
- **logbook PM completions were one atomic batch** - a task already completed today refused every ticked task and the
  page said "did NOT record, so those PMs still count as due" beside "1 PM task -> compliance"; each task is written alone
  and told by kind. And a recognised refresh-retry ("no duplicate created") went on to run the parts deduction and PM
  writes again - a retry took the parts twice; it stops there now.
- **three sentences named the wrong cause** - a duplicate role assignment said "change it to something different"
  (now: "<name> already has the <role> role ... Nothing more to do"); a listing conflict blamed "someone else" on a record
  only its owner may edit (now: "saved from another tab or device"); the import said "1 assets are".
- seed: change orders sat on work-order projects, whose Change orders tab the page never shows (a decision no supervisor
  could see) - placed only on capex / contractor / shutdown projects now.

no-access gate - walked as an absence: no control exists to race on.

## §ED · Engineering design, one calculator at a time — its guide, its form, its report, its saved copy, its bill of materials, its drawing (Ian, 2026-10-31)

Ian: *"there are many flops in engineering design calculator, in the guide, you find it and you will see"*, then *"when
you found it, make necessary and appropriate number of trajectories to add to the roadmap"*, then *"just make appropriate
number of trajectories for overall engineering design."*

**The idea, understood.** `engineering-design.html` is not one page to a person. It is 55 calculators, and each one is
its own code:
- its own form, built by `renderInputForm`;
- its own report renderer (`render<Calc>Report`);
- its own entry in the Guide tab (`GUIDES[id]`);
- its own stored shape, which History re-renders;
- its own bill of materials and scope;
- for 51 of them, its own drawing.

A flop in one calculator is invisible from the page as a whole, and the page is how the registry read it.

**What the registry had.** 451 in-scope rows on `engineering-design.html` read it as one page: a layer, an action, a
persona. The 52 rows that name a calculator walk its search door (`tools/<slug>-calculator/`), not the calculator inside
the app. No row named the Guide tab.

The engines are already held: `validate_calc_formula_accuracy.py` pins 58/58 calc types to hand-computed oracles (296
assertions). What nobody walked is the page around each engine.

**The guide, measured live** (2026-10-31, through the Playwright MCP, every calculator selected and its form read):
- **Built, with no guide.** Transformer Sizing, Harmonic Distortion and Clean Agent Suppression open a Guide that says
  *"No guide available yet … check back after it is built."*
- **Guide and form disagree.** Across the other 52, the guides name 75 fields no form label matches, and the forms carry
  141 labels no guide describes. Some are renames; the walk decides each one.
- **Fields that do not exist.** Load Estimation's guide describes System Voltage, Phase Configuration, Power Factor and
  Demand Factor. Its form has none of them.
- **On a phone:**
  - every tip, note and standard is 12.5px at 55% white, below the page's own contrast floor;
  - 134 empty formula entries each open a three-line hole;
  - 398 formula lines wrap, and the continuation reads as the next formula.
- **A stale entry.** `BOM_SOW_SUPPORTED` still lists "Gear / Belt Drive", a calculator that no longer exists.

**The lenses** — one row per (calculator, lens) the registry does not already hold:

| lens | the row asks | units |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** the guide tells the truth about this calculator | the Guide names exactly the fields this calculator's form carries and describes every one; its formulas, constants and standards are the engine's and the report's | every built calculator |
| **F1** the form refuses what it cannot compute | blank, zero, negative and out-of-range inputs are refused before Calculate, in crew words that name the field; every input shows its unit and a sane default | every built calculator |
| **R1** the report reads true, on screen and on paper | every figure is the engine's value with its unit and clause; the verdict matches the result card; the printed/PDF report is whole | every built calculator |
| **S1** saved, reopened from History, the same calculation | the inputs, every figure and the report are the ones saved — this calculator's stored shape through its own renderer | every built calculator |
| **B1** the bill of materials and scope are this result's | the BOM/SOW sizes its items from this result, names its standard, survives edit, save and download | `BOM_SOW_SUPPORTED` |
| **D1** the drawing matches the numbers | the drawing's labels and title block carry the result; legible at 390 and 1280; downloads as the same drawing | the drawing dispatch (`_runDrawing`) |
| **GR1–GR3** the guide renderer, once for all 55 | faint text · a hole per empty formula entry · a wrapped formula read as two | one row per measured site |
| **I1** every value the form sends reaches the engine *(added the same day)* | each value the form sends is read by its engine and changes the result as the field says, or the form says it is recorded only | each calculator `tools/census_calc_input_reach.py` finds sending a key its engine never reads |
| **E1** the engine a person is served is the oracle-verified engine *(added the same day)* | the page's result comes from the Python engine the oracle pins, not the edge function's unchecked TypeScript fallback, and the report renders every field it reads from it | each calculator `tools/census_calc_served_engine.py` finds answered by TypeScript |

`engineering-design.js`:
- **55 built calculators** (`CALC_TYPES_UI`, `available: true`): 52 with a guide, 3 without;
- **55 with BOM/SOW**;
- **51 drawn**;

`python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-engineering-design` seeded **ED1..ED329**: the program went from 36,534 to
36,863 in scope, and each row has its pending critic row.

**I1, added the same day, from what the first walks found.** Reading the guides against their engines found the same
defect twice before noon:
- **Pipe Sizing:** the form sends "Cold Water Supply", "Chilled Water Supply", "Hot Water Supply" and "General Water",
  and the engine knew none of them. Five of seven services were sized on the General velocity range, so a domestic
  cold-water pipe could be chosen at up to 3.0 m/s against its 2.5 limit.
- **Pump Sizing:** the engine read none of the form's `pressure_head`, `fittings_allowance` or `fluid_density`. TDH left
  out the discharge back-pressure, so a pump feeding a pressure vessel came out short by exactly that head. The engine
  also refused the form's default diameter of 0 ("Auto"). That case did not fail in front of the person: the edge
  function fell through to its TypeScript fallback, which is the next finding.

Both are fixed in the engine, with oracle vectors that fail on the old code. Because the class is "a value the person
types does nothing", it was measured across all 55 calculators instead of one engine at a time.
`tools/census_calc_input_reach.py` compares the top-level keys `collectInputs()` sends with the keys each engine module
reads. **20 of 55 calculators send 62 keys their engine never reads:**
- AHU Sizing ignores ten form values. It hard-codes the chilled-water temperatures to 7/12 °C and one unit.
- Cooling Tower ignores eight.
- Short Circuit ignores five, among them the transformer kVA and %Z.
- Storm Drain ignores six.
- UPS, Wire Sizing, Shaft Design and Fire Pump ignore four or five each.

Three calculators (Duct Sizing, LPS, V-Belt) have no Python handler, so the census cannot see them. **20 rows,
ED330..ED349, all T1.** On each walk, every key is decided one of two ways: the engine uses it, or the field says it is
recorded on the report only.

**The census had a blind spot, found by the walk (2026-11-01).** Compressed Air sends its tool list as the shorthand `tools,`, and the census's first parser counted only `name: value`, so no list sent in shorthand was ever measured. The engine ignored every tool a person listed (20 impact wrenches sized the same 2.2 kW compressor as the default three). The parser now splits the payload at its top-level commas, and found one more calculator: Refrigerant Pipe Sizing's `lines` schedule. That adds row ED354, so I1 is 21 rows.

**E1, from walking Wire Sizing the same day.** `engineering-design.html` sends every calculation to the
`engineering-calc-agent` edge function. That function tries the Python engine first and falls through silently to its own
TypeScript implementation in two cases: Python has no handler under the name the frontend sends, or Python raises on the
form's payload. The oracle pins only the Python modules, so a calculator in either case is answered by an engine nothing
checks.

`tools/census_calc_served_engine.py` runs every Python handler on the form's real default payload
(`tools/fixtures/ed_default_payloads.json`, read from `collectInputs()` in the page). **51 of 55 are served by Python.**
Four are not:
- **Wire Sizing:** the form sends `power_w`, and `wire_sizing.py` accepts only `load_kw`, `load_kva` or `load_amps`. It
  refuses every form calculation.
- **Duct Sizing, LPS and V-Belt:** Python registers these as "Duct Sizing", "Lightning Protection (LPS)" and
  "Gear / Belt Drive". The frontend sends "Duct Sizing (Equal Friction)", "Lightning Protection System (LPS)" and
  "V-Belt Drive Design". Three oracle-verified engines have never answered a person.

**4 rows, ED350..ED353, all T1.** Switching the served engine changes the result shape the report renders, so each walk
compares the Python output with the TypeScript output and with the report's reads before it switches.

**Correction (2026-11-02): two of the four were the census's false reading.** `main.py` already maps the frontend's
longer names, for example `handlers["Lightning Protection System (LPS)"] = handlers["Lightning Protection (LPS)"]`
(commit 84fbae35). The census's first parser followed only `= <name>_calc`, so it reported LPS and V-Belt as having no
handler. Python has always answered both. The real count was **53 of 55**: Wire Sizing raised on its payload, and so did
Duct Sizing, whose alias Python reached before raising (walked: `source: typescript`). The census now follows aliases.
ED352 and ED353 carry a correction.

Reading those two engines under the right name still found one real defect:
- **LPS:** sends `earth_type` (Type A radial or Type B ring), which the engine had never read. It decided "ring required"
  from the LPL and the building length. It now follows the person's choice (IEC 62305-3 §5.4.2). Type A gives an electrode
  at each down conductor, never fewer than two. Type B gives a ring about 1 m outside the walls, whose mean radius is
  checked against l1, with supplementary electrodes added when it falls short.
- **V-Belt:** nothing to fix. `power_input` and `power_unit` are echoes (the form converts HP to kW), so they are
  recorded with that reason.

**Duct Sizing (ED350) was a genuine fall-through.** `duct_sizing.py` read only `sections` / `flow_m3s`, so it raised
on the page's `segments[]` schedule, and the TypeScript sized every duct a person drew. The page's segment method is
now ported into Python with the TypeScript's result keys, and it fixes three defects the TypeScript had:
- **The duct material changed nothing.** Roughness was fixed at 0.09 mm, with smooth-pipe Blasius below Re 1e5, so a
  flexible duct was sized as smooth steel. Friction is now Colebrook (Swamee-Jain) at the guide's own roughness values
  (0.09, 0.05 and 1.5 mm, all inside ASHRAE Ch.21 Table 1 ranges), both in sizing and in the pressure drop. A flexible
  supply main grows from Ø500 to Ø550.
- **The fan's duct loss was the sum of every segment, parallel branches included.** It is now the index run: the mains
  plus the worst branch on each side (ASHRAE Ch.21 critical path). For the form's defaults that is 38.49 Pa against a
  44.26 Pa sum, and the report and guide say so.
- **The drawing read one duct's numbers that the TypeScript never returned.** It printed "Ø0mm or 0×0mm, v = 0.00 m/s".
  It is now given the fan-side main. The chart's velocity colours (`velocity_ok` / `velocity_note`) arrive with each
  segment as well.

The TypeScript fallback still carries the old method, and it answers only when Python is down.

**ED255 / R1, closed for the R1 walk to confirm (2026-11-02):** the V-belt AI narrative called the typed 7.5 kW the
design power (it is 9.0 kW). The grounding rail asks only whether a number exists, so it passed. A second rail,
`namedFigureMismatch` in engineering-calc-agent, now drops any report section that names a `design_<quantity>` result and
quotes another figure; the report's own text takes its place. It is run in node by `narration-rail-holds-every-figure`
against seven cases. The door page's "SPB" was not a section key: the engine drew B's geometry but the flat estimate's
rating (4 belts where B's ANSI/RMA rating needs 6). An unknown section now resolves to B once, rating included, and the
door example is the classical B section (6 belts). Both items wait for ED257's R1 walk; R1 has no prover yet.

**UPS / R1, closed for the R1 walk to confirm (2026-11-02):** the battery Ah was energy only, kW × t / (V × 0.80 × 0.98),
which reads every block at its 20-hour capacity. A VRLA block gives about half of that in a 15-minute discharge. The
engine now sizes from a published constant-power table: CSB GP12170, datasheet RA240531, W per 12 V block to 1.75 V/cell
at 25 °C (677 W at 5 min, 395 W at 15 min, 161 W at 60 min per 17 Ah). The table is scaled per Ah of 20-hour capacity
and multiplied by the IEEE 1184 aging factor of 1.25, with log-log interpolation in time. The autonomy check inverts the
same table. A 50 kW, 15-minute UPS now needs 144.5 Ah, not 69.9, and the old figure would have run about 7 minutes. The
guide says the final battery comes from the chosen maker's own table. The walk also found the UPS report's signature
row, and AHU's summary tiles, running past a 390 px phone (403 and 402 px). Gate `report-grids-reflow` now holds every
fixed multi-column grid in the report renderers.

**R1 has a prover (2026-11-02): `tools/prove_engineering_reports.mjs`, gate `engineering-reports`.** For each
calculator it takes the served Python handler's answer on the form's own payload (`tools/ed_report_cases.py`). It
renders the report through the live path (`_renderComputed`, with no AI narrative) and reads it at phone-390, at
desktop-1280 and on paper (print media at A4 width). It checks that the report states each headline figure the engine
computed, that no figure is broken, that the report fits the phone and that it prints whole. Its first run passed 46 of
55, and every one of the nine was a real fault:
- Solar printed 66.5 m² of roof, from a ×1.15 alias, for the engine's ×1.3 figure of 75.1 m².
- The Shaft report worked its own ASME elliptic diameter (25.6 mm) and never showed the engine's DE-Goodman Se, σ or nf.
- Short Circuit never stated its fault MVA, and labelled its peak "1.8 × Isc".
- The chiller kW/TR and the cooling-tower effectiveness appeared only in the drawings.
- The air-cooled chiller's reference row cited a minimum COP of 2.84 under a check judged at 2.96.
- FCU called an average of 7.0, 10.5 and 4.2 kW units the unit capacity.
- Wire returned a voltage drop at an assumed 30 m while saying it was not checked.

All 55 now read true, held by the ratchet `engineering_reports_baseline.json`. The headline check is not yet "every
figure": the R1 rows bank when the walk holds and the report's working has been read against its engine, as G1 did.

**I1 by value: the census asks per choice, not only per key (2026-11-02).** `census_calc_input_reach` proves each key
the form sends is read, but it cannot see a value the engine does not know. The vibration isolator was the first case:
the engine read the key, yet every isolator computed as a rubber mount. `tools/census_form_option_reach.py` (gate
`form-option-reach`) runs every toggle option against a garbage value. It found 20 choices the engines never saw:
- Earthing's "Substation (IEEE 80)" fell back to the 10 Ω limit, so a grid of 8.4 Ω read PASS against IEEE 80's 1 Ω.
- LPS's "Galvanized Steel" and "Aluminum" took copper's 16 mm² down conductor, where the standard asks 50 and 25 mm².
- STP's "UV" plant was still dosed with chlorine.

Fourteen are right by a rule and are recorded with their reasons. The same test on the door pages' examples, gate
`door-examples-are-keys`, found 20 more ("Manila", "SA-516-70", "R410A", and a stairwell "Office" computed as
unsprinklered).

**R1 and S1 banked, 110 rows (2026-11-02).** The report prover gained an "every figure" check. Every number in a report's
figure cells must trace to the served engine, its inputs, a stated unit conversion or the renderer's own constant. It

- Beam back-solved Ix 1000× small, printed with a raw `&sup6;`.
- Beam also back-solved Zx and Aw.
- Shaft computed the ASME cross-check itself, under a label that named the wrong branch.

**D1 banked, 51 rows (2026-11-02).** `tools/prove_engineering_drawings.mjs` (gate `engineering-drawings`) runs the

The drawings had also been computing their own figures:
- a chiller's kW/TR of 0.963, where the engine says 1.172;
- a fire pump churn at 121% of rated pressure, where the engine uses NFPA 20's 140%;
- a relief valve labelled "115% MAWP";

**F1 banked, 55 rows (2026-11-02).** `tools/prove_engineering_forms.mjs` (gate `engineering-forms`) walks every form
field by field. The engine call is held at the network: nothing computes, saves or spends AI quota. The first version
patched `db.functions.invoke`. That is a getter that builds a new client on every read, so the first run sent real
calculations and spent the walker's daily AI quota. The route is now held with `page.route`. Per field, the walk checks:
- a blank is refused before Calculate, in words that name the field, unless the label says what a blank means;
- a 0 the field's range forbids is refused;
- a typed 0 where 0 is real reaches the engine as 0;
- the field declares a minimum and, if it has a dimension, shows its unit.

The first walk passed 0 of 55 forms:
- 312 blank fields computed with a number nobody saw. The page's range check skipped a blank, and the payload read
  `parseFloat(v(id)) || default`.
- 59 typed zeros were swapped for defaults: a straight pipe at 20% fittings, a hoist's 0 kg sling at 15 kg, a
  pure-torsion shaft at 2,000 N, a 0% harmonic dropped from the spectrum.
- Four engines swapped a 0 as well: the sprinkler hose stream (back to the hazard table's 946–1,893 L/min), the fire-pump
  suction head (back to 1.5 m), pipe fittings (back to 20%) and the chiller ambient (back to 35 °C).
- A bearing with Fr = Fa = 0 read "L10 = 0 h, FAIL"; it is now refused in words. Pure axial load still computes.
- 50 fields were named by their placeholder ("0", "3.0", "Auto", "e.g. 15000"), so a screen reader said "0, spin
  button" and a refusal would have named "0".

The fix:
- the page refuses a blank by name;
- `n0(id, d)` keeps any finite number in 46 payload reads;
- where 0 is impossible, the field declares a minimum above it (ceiling height, fluid density, heat-exchanger flows, a
  custom fixture's DFU, rate or flow, cable weight) and the Voc coefficient a maximum below it;
- 15 fields whose label states what a blank means carry `data-optional`;
- the required loads that opened at 0 open empty;
- the five fields with no minimum (suction head, heat-exchanger temperatures) declare one;
- the heat exchanger's four temperatures have distinct names instead of "Inlet / Outlet" twice.

Five oracle vectors fail on the old engines; the oracle passes 175/175. The prover only accepts `data-optional` when the
label says what a blank means, so the marker cannot be used to silence a field. Its teeth plant three defects: a quiet
optional marker, a payload that swaps 0, and a field with its minimum removed. Each is named. 55 of 55 forms now hold.

**B1 banked, 55 rows (2026-11-02).** `tools/prove_engineering_boms.mjs` (gate `engineering-boms`) generates each
calculator's BOM and SOW through the page's own `generateBomSowChecklist()`. The call goes to the real
`engineering-bom-sow` agent on the free-tier chain, and the walk captures the body the agent receives at the network.
For each calculator it then checks:
- every value the agent reads has a key present in that body, or is recorded with its reason (another mode of the
  calculator, or a stated basis the form does not ask for);
- the BOM and SOW carry no N/A, undefined or NaN;
- they state the engine's rating, and the SOW names a standard;
- a quantity edited in the checklist, and one corrected in the documents, both reach the downloaded CSV;
- the documents fit a 390 px phone.

The first walk passed 0 of 54. A probe of four had already shown the agents doing the engineering arithmetic themselves:
- **Transformer:** the prompt asked for an "MCCB rated minimum 125% of I2", and the model wrote 125 A for a 144 A
  secondary.
- **Fire pump:** the prompt said "jockey approx. 10% of main pump flow", while the engine had computed 28.4 L/min (1%).
  It also said "relief valve set at 10% above churn pressure: NFPA 20 requirement". NFPA 20 §4.20 requires a relief
  valve where a diesel driver's 121% of churn plus static suction exceeds the components' rating; a valve set above
  churn never opens.

Six agents now compute every rating in code (`STD_OCPD_A`, `ocpdAtLeast`) and state it as a figure, and the model
writes the words around it:
- transformer 200 A;
- generator, at the form's own voltage (it was 415 V whatever the form said);
- PFC: conductors at 135% (NEC 460.8(A)), and the breaker the next standard rating;
- fire pump: the engine's jockey pump and the §4.20 rule;
- boiler feed pump: 110% of the design steam;
- cooling-tower side-stream filter: 10% of the circulating flow.

The grounding check found agents reading keys nothing sends:
- the boiler read `feedwater_temp`, `tds_max` and `tds_makeup`; the form sends `fw_temp_c` and `_ppm`, so every BOM
  used 80 °C, 3500 ppm and 200 ppm;
- water treatment read a PNS status the engine never returns;
- the beam read `results.cover_mm`, while the form sends `inputs.cover_mm`;
- the noise BOM ordered hearing protection and audiometry for "all 50 exposed workers", a count the form never asks for.

The heat exchanger listed pass partition plates for a single-pass tube side. On the page, the documents' cells were
inputs bound to nothing, so a corrected quantity reached the PDF (which clones the DOM) but not the CSV (which reads the
data). The documents' signature grid also ran a 390 px phone to 514. The report's phone rule reached `#report-panel`
only; `report-grids-reflow` now holds `.doc-panel` and the preview renderers too. Its first walk passed 0 of 54. After the fixes, 55 of 55 hold; the fix walk also showed one transient agent failure, so a content fault is now regenerated once before it counts, and grounding, edit and fit are never retried. Its teeth plant a phantom key, a broken figure and an edit the CSV lost. Each is named.

**A size past the end of its list (2026-11-02).** While the B1 walk ran, the cooling-tower answer read
`pump_power_kw: 6695.8` and `recommended_pump_kw: 90` for an 86 m³/h, 20 m duty that needs 6.7 kW. A second line had
overwritten the correct one, so watts were printed as kW. The motor pick
`next((s for s in SIZES if s >= need), SIZES[-1])` then ran off the end of its list and answered the largest motor, with
nothing said.

`tools/census_selection_ceiling.py` (gate `selection-ceiling`) rewrites every such pick in memory to record when it falls
back. It then drives every served case ×10 and ×1000. 44 picks in 29 engines are written that way, and 30 answered the
largest size silently. One example: a 1,000 m² office was given one 50 kW unit for an 86.6 kW design.

They now pick through `calcs/_catalog.pick_at_least`. `@discloses` returns what ran past its list as `exceeds_catalog`,
the page states it above whichever report rendered, and the BOM's scope opens with it. The census reads 0 open; its
teeth strip `@discloses` and find all 30 again. Two oracle vectors pin it: the condenser pump at 6.087 kW, and the
1,000 m² office.

**B1 is held for the agent, not one sample of it.** The BOM's words are a model's. The gate ratchets on grounding, edit and fit, which are deterministic, and on content after one regeneration. It is skip_if_fast, because a full walk is 55 agent calls (about 20 minutes on the free-tier chain).

Ian: *"we have to add more appropriate number of open trajectories to the existing trajectories roadmap, for the U x F x A
x I x UI x UX x each architectural full stack saas layers x each production pages x each public pages x personas x journey
scenarios."* Decided the same day (three measured sizings put to Ian): **every gate-admitted persona** — 19,618 cells in
the plan's census, 19,182 once the seeder measured it against the live registry (the five founder surfaces the hub offers
nobody keep `oversight` as their single cast, casts()' own rule).

**The cell, and where each axis's applicability comes from — nothing typed (`tools/cube_census.py`):**
- **pages** — `sublayer_inventory.page_classes()`: production 27 · founder 9 · public 119 (edge functions are not pages;
  their contracts are W3-FN's).
- **layers** — a layer applies to a page when the inventory's sub-layer roster puts the page in it
  (`sublayer_inventory.collect()`: 12.9 layers per production page, 12.3 founder, 9.0 public).
- **personas** — production/founder: admitted when the journey-paths gate accepts the persona's OWN route to the page
  (`_path` → `role_blocked_hops` + `broken_hops`): all 13 signed-in personas on the field pages, four (supervisor ·

  do); **A once per (page, layer)** — viewport, network and offline do not change with the cast.
- **UI/UX** — every row carries its critic cell and is graded on the 33-class rubric by the critic deepwalk; the

- **journey** — every row's `pages` is the route the gate accepts for its persona, so every cube row is a journey hop.

2.2×; walks do not:** one walk of a page as one persona answers every layer × pillar row of that cell (the LX batch rule,

## §SE · §OUT · §JS — The outcome waves: the person's belief, the figures that show it moved, and the journeys where they were thin (Ian, 2026-10-26)

Ian: *"all of these will improve both the self-efficacy of the users and system characteristics of my platform. from these
this will increase the intention to use and satisfaction of the users that will lead to better usage of my platform."* The
five lenses are the roadmap's axes; **self-efficacy, intention to use, satisfaction and usage were not** — no row asked
whether a person who had never done the task believes, after this page, that they can; none connected a page's improvement
to a movement in use or return. Decided with Ian the same day: satisfaction inferred from behaviour only (no new control);
self-efficacy over the product pages AND the public funnel; every journey stage degraded and aged; the seller as recasts
plus the layer floor. `tools/trajectory_outcome_gaps.py` is the one place that decides the size; the three seeders import it.

**§SE — self-efficacy (Bandura's four sources), one row per (page, source) — 282 rows, SE1..SE282.**

| source | the row asks | derivation | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| mastery | a person who has never used this page completes its primary action without leaving the page for help (a fresh seeded member, never on the page; steps counted) — and, on the public funnel, a stranger computes / reads to the answer unaided | 27 production pages + 60 calculators + 54 learn articles | 141 |
| vicarious | before the first action the page shows what a finished one looks like — a template, a sample, a peer's record, a worked example | 27 production pages + 60 calculators (the generator's reserved worked-example block) | 87 |
| verbal persuasion | the completed action is confirmed in words that name what was done and what it now enables (the L4 told sentence, the success microinteraction, the onboarding step flipping) | 27 production pages | 27 |
| emotional state | the person can act without fear: the destructive act can be undone or recovered, the error path names a remedy | 27 production pages | 27 |

**§OUT — outcomes as figures, one row per (page, outcome) plus the console and the gates — 87 rows, OUT1..OUT87.**
Per production page: **use** (every primary action records a `feature_use` — the L3 lane the pages missed), **return**
(accounts that used the page again within 7 and 30 days, from `analytics_events` by `auth_uid`), **satisfaction** (repeat use
of the same page by the same account within 7 days, stated as "repeat use", never "satisfied"; the feedback form stays the
only direct voice). Plus the console's three figure surfaces on `founder-console.html` (each with its period and basis beside
it, the OPC pattern) and the three never-typed gates (`tools/prove_outcome_figures.py` recomputes each figure through psql and
compares it with the console).

**§JS — journey scenarios where they were thin — 41 rows, JS1..JS41.** The census measured less than the plan expected,
and the measure is the number: W4's `--condition` fixtures had already walked most archetypes degraded, and the cube had
already seeded the seller on every layer (60–69 rows each against the 12-row floor). What remained: **30 degraded walks** (10
archetypes × offline-3g · dependency-down · release-mid-way), **2 aged walks** (month-3, year-2), **9 seller recasts** (the
three two-sided trade archetypes × the three vertical pairs, walked with the seller as the walker).

Seeded by `seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-self-efficacy / --add-outcomes / --add-journey-conditions` (37,017 → 37,427 in
scope). In the priority queue (§PRIORITY) SE and OUT are **T2** — the model's dependent variables come right after the
