## §OD · The open-source design lens — Penpot as the canvas, Project Wallace as the code-side lens (Ian, 2026-11-03)

Ian: *"instead of relying in figma, there are so many open source in github repos, that we can get to, do not just limit,
be proactive ... just extend my ideas"*, then *"you control my browser ... can you just be proactive"*, then *"we have to
extend the number of our trajectories roadmap through penpot, you have to plan the appropriate and necessary numbers to
add for our trajectories roadmap."*

**The idea, understood.** The Figma design lens was retired on 2026-10-13. Ian's seat allowed 20 metered MCP calls a month,
and its 31 rows needed 100 to 150. The design source stayed in code (tokens.css and the shared components). That decision
stands. What was lost was an instrument, not a goal, and open source has both halves of it:

| Instrument | Repo (licence) | What it does here |
|---|---|---|
| Penpot, hosted MCP | penpot/penpot `mcp/` (MPL-2.0) | The canvas. Ian's account (free "Professional": "no limits"), the "WorkHive design source" file, and a "WorkHive tokens" colour library holding tokens.css's 20 colours. No call cap is published. |
| css-analyzer | projectwallace/css-analyzer (MIT) | The code-side lens. It reads each served page's own CSS and sorts every value by what tokens.css says. |
| odiff | dmtrKovalenko/odiff (MIT) | The pixel comparison that tells a comp and its live page apart. |
| taste-skill v2, ui-ux-pro-max | Leonxlnx/taste-skill, nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill (MIT) | Installed as skills: app-screen art direction, and a local palette/type/UX database. |

**What the code-side lens measured** (2026-11-03, 164 served files, `tools/prove_design_source_drift.py`):
- 1,213 literals that ARE a token's value, alpha included (`rgba(255,255,255,0.80)` is `--wh-text-muted`).
- 7,022 palette tints typed by hand.
- 959 off-palette colours.
- 1,349 raw font sizes and 227 raw z-indexes.

The synthesis:
- **A missing token.** The deep background `#0d1824` is hard-coded on 120 files, with its near-twin `#0f1923` on 18
  more. No token holds it.
- **Missing triplets.** Six palette colours are tinted by hand 50 or more times, but have no `-rgb` triplet to tint from:
  cloud 1,450, navy-mid 730, red 199, navy 141, navy-light 77 and violet 63. So their tints *cannot* come from the
  token.
- **Tailwind leakage.** Tailwind's red-500, orange-400 and gray-200 have leaked in beside the platform's own colours.

**The number, measured, never typed** (`tools/open_design_census.py`: population × what each unit owes − rows already
there). 193 rows, **OD1..OD193**:
- **OD-P (43).** A page unit's comp lives in the WorkHive Penpot file, drawn from the token library, at 390 and 1280.
  It agrees with the live page by odiff. The units are the 41 served pages plus the two GENERATED families (the learn
  articles and the calculator pages). Their generator is the unit, because a per-page fix is reverted by the next build.
  The learn family carries 13 template generations, so its row closes when the regenerated family measures as one.
- **OD-D (133).** A unit's own CSS takes its values from tokens.css, one row per drift class that is non-zero today:
  colour 47, type scale 48, stacking 38, over 48 units (the page units, plus four hand-written stylesheets and one
  Tailwind build).
  - Typeface is not counted: rubric S1 already owns it, and R1 owns spacing. An OD row on those axes would duplicate a
    CX-UX cell.
- **OD-S (17).** The design system owns what the pages improvise:
  - 8 missing colour tokens. These are off-palette colours on 5 or more units, with near-identical ones merged at
    delta-E < 3. A cluster that close to an existing token is a mistyped token and stays a page row.
  - 6 `-rgb` triplets.
  - 3 scales: neutral overlay/shadow, type, and z-index.

**Priority.** OD-D on a production page is T3, because a page that types its own red looks unlike its neighbours to the
person working on it. OD-D on founder and public pages is T5. OD-S is T4, the design system's own health. OD-P is T6.

**Held by.** The gate `design-source-drift` is a ratchet over design_source_drift_baseline.json (1,103 (file :: metric)
counts on the first reading). Any rise fails, a new page counts from 0, and fixes lower the floor.

### §OD.1 The type scale, 2026-11-04: 5,379 hand-typed font sizes to 0

**Measured first.** The pages typed 100 distinct sizes, 5,379 times, and the weight sat on a few steps. tokens.css
declares those steps as `--wh-fs-2xs`..`--wh-fs-5xl`, with three `-plus` half-steps, `--wh-fs-hero` and
`--wh-fs-display`. Paper gets its own scale, `--wh-print-fs-*` in pt. A size is matched only within its medium: 12px is 9pt
exactly, and a screen label is never respelled as a print step.

**Each move carries its own proof** (`tools/fix_token_literals.py`):
- 4,714 exact sizes were respelled as `var(--wh-fs-x, <size>)`, proven invisible. The fallback must also equal the token,
  because the fallback is the first paint.
- 570 sizes within half a pixel of a step (at the 16px base) moved onto it, with a half-pixel proof. This includes 204
  px sizes, which now follow a reader's larger default text size, and the analytics report's fine print inside
  `@media print`.
- 85 off-scale sizes (page titles at 1.3 to 1.8rem, stat numbers, empty-state glyphs, the article family's 1.55rem h2)
  went to the nearest step, ties to the larger. This is a visible change, so the proof checks that each landed on
  exactly that step.
- The compiled Tailwind sheets were respelled by `--tailwind`. tw_public_build.mjs runs that after every build, and it
  skips the header comment, whose config JSON is data the tw-public-sheets gate compares.
- The three generator templates were respelled too, because the shipped page is the source.

**Decided on purpose, not respelled:**
- pm-scheduler's two 0.6 and 0.65rem chips were lifted to the 12px floor (`text-xs`).
- Seven Tailwind arbitrary-size rules that no live page uses were removed from wh-tw.css, as a re-harvest would.
- Relative sizes (`inherit`, `em`, `%`) take the parent's size. The lens no longer counts them.

**What it found on the way:**
- Three gates read a respelled value only as a bare literal: content_mobile_gate's prose size (it passed BLIND),
  analytics C1's KPI tier, and print-is-readable's body ink. Each now reads through the var(), and keeps its teeth.
- A sheet header is data, as described above.
- utils.js injects copies of component rules, and one copy stayed behind the stylesheet. That is the new gate
  `injected-css-parity`, which also caught a pre-existing 0.75/0.78rem drift.
- The lifecycle gate had read founder-console.html without the operator-actions.js its queue moved into on 10-22.

### §OD.2 The Penpot comps, 2026-11-04: drawn as each row's cast, and the mirror fixed before the batch

**Penpot was never waiting on a person** (Ian: *"can you just be proactive, you already have control over my
browser"*). The DevTools browser signed in with the `.env` credentials (clipboard paste; nothing printed), opened
"WorkHive design source" by its file id, and its MCP menu already read "MCP connected". `penpot_sync_tokens.mjs` then
synced 38 tokens (9 stale removed), and `--check` agreed.

**The first comp passed on numbers and was the wrong picture.** logbook's board matched the live page within 5.4%, and
it was the sign-in wall. Four defects in `tools/penpot_comp_from_page.mjs`, each found by looking at the board, never by
its number:
- **It drew pages signed out.** Each OD-P row names a persona. `--cast` now signs in through the journeys' own
  `signIn` (anon / worker / oversight as the supervisor, prove_csp_exact's mapping), and `assertSignedIn` refuses a
  comp of the wall.
- **One failing shape dropped its batch.** An exception inside a 120-shape `execute_code` came back as text the
  client read as a result. Each shape is now its own try, and failures are counted and named in the receipt; any
  failure fails the comp.
- **The face.** Penpot's default font has no 500 or 800. Text is set in Poppins (the page's face) at its own weight.
- **Ghosts, slabs and wraps.** A closed `<details>` kept its computed display (`checkVisibility()` now decides). A
  heavy blur is decoration a box mirror cannot draw (left out), and every box carries its painted opacity (its own
  times its ancestors'). Text sits at its own Range rect, not its element's.

### KA-V: the share-of-voice run on free-tier engines (Ian: "find something else with a free tier, and delete this Perplexity")

`tools/geo_sov_free_run.py` asks the fixed prompt set (prompt_audit_queries.json; the 45 KA-V units are 45 of its 55
ids) of engines that search the live web as they answer, through the providers' own free-tier APIs:
- Groq `gpt-oss-20b` / `gpt-oss-120b` with `browser_search`. 200,000 tokens per model per day, so a few prompts a day.
- Mistral conversations with `web_search`. Left to choose, it answered generic prompts from memory, so it is told it
  is a web answer engine and retried once with the search asked in the input. An answer with no sources is recorded
  as None, never as a miss.
- Gemini grounded on Google Search, opt-in: 20 requests per model per day on this key.

The consumer apps stay hand-filled columns, because their terms forbid scripting them. Perplexity is gone from
`geo_sov_audit.ENGINES` (its API is paid). The run resumes and never re-asks a read cell. `tools/sov_daily.cmd` is
scheduled daily 21:30 ("WorkHive SOV daily", when the host is idle) and scores the month (`--score`), so the voice
trip reads the newest sheet. Measured on its first day: Groq's free budget covers 2 to 3 browser-search prompts per
model, and Mistral's web_search answered 17 of 55; a refused cell is asked again on the next run, and a spent engine
is skipped for the rest of that run. The scorer now writes `scored_at` beside `last_run`; the voice trip and two
scoreboard readers had each asked for a name it never wrote, and all three read "never been scored" after a scored run.
`bank_ka_rows.py --lens V` banks a row when all of these hold:
- its expected page is citation-eligible: answer-first, twin current, no freshness trip;
- no voice trip;
- every engine the month declares has a reading for its prompt.

Whether WorkHive was cited is recorded in the basis, never required.
### §OD.3 The stacking scale and the last colours, 2026-11-04: OD-D and OD-S fully banked

**Stacking (`tools/fix_stacking_tokens.py`).** 30 z-index values became 26 rungs (`--wh-z-*`), named by the role of the
layers on each: art, base, sticky, menu, sheet, modal, toast, drawer, skip-link, retired. Two values share a rung only
where no page context holds both, so the map is monotone. Merged values move UP to their rung's largest member.
`proves_order_kept` re-reads every one of 155 page contexts, each made of:
- its own layers, read by the element, so a style attribute keeps its role;
- the sheets it links;
- the z-indexes its scripts and the shell chrome set, as fixed points.

Every pair's order must hold. A name tokens.css already held at another value (`--wh-z-sticky` 100, `--wh-z-modal` 1100,
used through `var()`) is never reused. The compiled Tailwind sheet's six z-utilities took the same rungs.
`validate_file_storage` read `z-index:\s*[1-9]` and went red on two correctly raised buttons; it now reads through
`var()`, and its mutation proves it bites.

**Colour, to zero hand-typed.** In order, each pass with its own proof:
- `#fff` / `#000` and the `-rgb` triplets the tints lacked became tokens. White TEXT alphas went through the triplet.
- Overlay-range alphas (white <= .20, any black) never go through the triplet. `--retire-overlay` moves each onto a
  `--wh-white-NN` / `--wh-black-NN` step only when its composite over every dark ground the pages use stays within the
  JND. Black gained -10/-20/-45/-75 steps.
- The census's own rule (delta-E < 3 is a mistyped token) retired the near-twins.
- The improvised palette was named, not changed. 53 colours that 2+ units typed (or one unit typed 5+ times) became
  tokens; Tailwind's own colours keep their Tailwind names (emerald-400, slate-400).
- The printed documents' paper palette became `--wh-doc-*`, and the rest of the long tail Tailwind names.
- One-offs within delta-E 5, then 10, were snapped, each move proven within its bound.
- `white` / `black` in value position became tokens. Lowercase only, and never in a comment: the proof refused a note
  reading "this doc's WHITE print surface".
- The drift lens now skips alpha-0 (`#0000`, `rgba(0,0,0,0)`): it is `transparent` spelled another way.

Drift went from 11,343 counted values (2026-11-03) to 274, which are now font families alone. OD-D 133/133 and OD-S
17/17 are in locking.

**OD-P (Penpot).** See §OD.2. The comps redraw on `load` plus a settle, not `networkidle`: twelve signed-in pages hold a
realtime socket and never went idle.

### §OD.4 What an OD row closes on, 2026-11-04: the instrument it declared, by name

**The ledger could not see 173 banked rows.** The headline stayed at 36,593 after OD-D and OD-S banked, because every
OD basis named its banker (`tools/bank_od_rows.py`) and no instrument. The ledger read those bases as prose, routed the
rows by their lens words to a person-shaped walk, and held all 193 open. Each OD row had declared its instrument when it
was seeded: the Wallace css-analyzer for D and S, and "penpot-mcp + playwright-mcp + odiff" for P. The ledger never
learned it. This is the ★×16 shape: the target grew, the bind did not.
- `live_walk_manifest` routes an OD row by `od.instrument`, as it does HS and ED rows.
- `bank_od_rows --restamp` adds a segment naming the instrument that took the reading. It appends, newest last, as
  `bank_sl_walk._bank` does, because the registry gate reads the last `pct -> N` as the row's account of itself. The
  first restamp prepended, and it was corrected the same day; both segments of those rows read 60, so no account moved.
- 150 D/S rows close: **36,743 of 37,001 (99.3%), 258 open.**

**P keeps both halves, and the live half must be an MCP.** OD-P is the design lens's successor, so it inherits the
design rule that every "-mcp" half is load-bearing. For an OD row, that half must also be named in the basis as an MCP
reading. The comp tool's own Playwright library screenshot does not count
([[feedback_a_library_batch_is_not_an_mcp_walk]]).
- The 23 drawn comps stayed open, correctly.
- `penpot_comp_from_page --live-shots <dir>` now measures agreement against a full-page screenshot the chrome-devtools
  MCP took as the row's cast, each cast in its own isolated context. The library read still supplies the boxes the
  board is drawn from: that is construction, not evidence.
- `--verify-only` re-exports a board already drawn, without redrawing it.
- The receipt records `live_reader`, the shot's path and its sha256.

**A scrollbar gutter is not a pixel ratio.** Headful Chrome on Windows lays a page out beside a classic scrollbar, so
every MCP shot came back 384 or 1274 wide. Scaling that to the board's width stretched the page vertically by the same
1.5%. A 6,600px page ended 100px out of step at its foot, analytics read 25% apart, and every diff doubled.
- A narrower shot is now pasted unscaled. Only a real device pixel ratio is rescaled.
- The 390 shots are retaken with mobile emulation. Its overlay scrollbars lay the page out at the full 390, as a phone
  does.
- The 1280 shots keep the desktop scrollbar a real window has.
- Measured on the 13 drawn worker comps at 1280: 1.3% to 8.8%, all pass.

**Penpot stores a "/" in a name as its path separator.** "about/index.html @ 390" reads back as
"about / index.html @ 390". An exact-name match never found a nested page's board, so verify refused all five
public-root pages. A redraw also left its old board behind next to the new one: the first batch's failed runs had
already orphaned boards for index, privacy-policy and the AHU calculator. Board names are now compared with the
separator's spaces removed.

**Where OD-P stands, end of 2026-11-04.** 25 pages pass at both widths against the chrome-devtools MCP render, and 27
OD-P rows are banked with the MCP named as the live reader. Analytics (OD7) reads open again: its board predates the
mirror fixes, so od-rows-hold stays red until it is redrawn. 16 pages are still owed a comp. The redraws need a quiet
host, for two reasons:
- **Penpot's main thread on a saturated host.** A plugin call overran the server's 120 s task limit, and the heartbeat
  lapsed behind it. Comps now go 40 shapes per call, and the canvas viewport is parked on an empty area so the 66
  boards are not re-rendered.
- **The journeys' sign-in timeouts.** The sign-in page did not load its client in time at under 0.5 GB free.
Penpot's tab must also stay connected after a reload (MCP -> "MCP connected"). A silent AudioContext keeps the tab
from throttling, but only while it is the tab that is loaded.

**Pages drawn before the mirror fixes are redrawn.** analytics' board still carried both aurora blobs, painted solid
at full size, because it was drawn before the glow and opacity fixes landed. Its diff against the true-width MCP render
was 21%, and the board was wrong, not the page. Five of the six old-code boards already passed against their MCP
captures, so only analytics (OD7) is redrawn.

**The tab now belongs to a tool, and the host runs one heavy job at a time.** The afternoon lost the Penpot tab three
times. Each Claude session restart restarted the chrome-devtools browser, signed out, and the host itself gave out:
CPU at 94-100% and 0.3-0.5 GB free under comps, MCP walks, the coding agent and a peer session. Docker Desktop's
engine died, taking Supabase, the edge runtime, the Python API forwarder and the seeder on :5000 with it.
- **`tools/penpot_tab.mjs`** now holds the file in a headless Chromium with a persistent profile. It signs in from
  `.env` in-process, waits for "MCP connected", and reopens on a drop. A headless page has no window to lose focus,
  and a session restart does not touch it.
- **One heavy job at a time.** Comps, browser gates and timing walks run serially while an agent drives browsers.
  After a crash: launch Docker Desktop, `docker start supabase_edge_runtime_workhive workhive_python_api_fwd`, wait for
  the database to report healthy, then restart the seeder (`test-data-seeder/venv/Scripts/python.exe app.py`).
- **INP rows (OWN597-604) wait for a quiet host.** Their timing walk is ready (`.playwright-mcp/inp_walk.js`: a
  Playwright MCP CDP session, 390 dpr 3, 4x CPU, three fresh loads, a fixed-loop calibration). Its first run on the
  saturated host read 232-2,496 ms, mostly presentation delay, with a calibration of 0.2x-5.8x. The host set that
  pace, not the throttle, so none of it is banked.


## §GJ · Group journeys — the people of one scenario, every hand-off between them, in milestones that each end in a push (Ian, 2026-11-04)

Ian: *"add the numbers of trajectories in our trajectories roadmap … consider the UFAI UI UX, personas, group of personas,
journey scenarios, full stack saas layers, production/founder/public pages"* — then *"use the existing trajectories
roadmap"* and *"the open trajectories are set in milestones, and at every milestone we push to production."*

**What was missing.** Every axis Ian named was already an axis of the cube (§CX), except a GROUP of personas. Measured
on 2026-11-04 over 40,184 rows: two people in one row ~600 (1.5%), a group of three 18; the stages that need two or more
people were the thin ones (comply 143 · grow 131 · trade 87 · integrate 36 · lifetime 16); arriving because someone else
acted was barely walked (email-push 167 · deep-link 60). The cube asks what ONE person can tell, may do and finds wired on
a page. A team meets the hand-off: **A acts, B must see it, C must not.**

**The cell.** (scenario, hand-off, a layer the receiving page carries, pillar U/F/I per member of the cast) + A once per
(hand-off, layer) + one UX row per (scenario, member). Pillars read across the hand-off:
- **U** — this member can tell who did it, when, from where and what it now enables (the sender can tell it was received);
- **F** — the sender's act is wired into what this member sees: the record, the count, the push;
- **I** — this member may act on it exactly as the roles allow; a member of another hive may not (0 rows, in words);
- **A** — it survives the receiver's 3G while the sender's network is fine, at phone-390 / desktop-1280 swapped.

**The number is the census's** (`tools/group_journey_census.py`, never typed): 34 scenario walks — 24 W3-JN archetypes
that name a pair, re-expressed as hand-offs, and 10 group stories the registry lacked (G-SHIFT, G-SENSOR, G-MULTI, G-ESC,
G-ADV, G-LEAVE, G-SVC, G-MOD, G-ONB, G-PUBLIC). Casts are resolved from the database (hive_members, the platform admins,
sellers, providers, API keys); a cast the database cannot hold is refused, and an oversight member must not belong to the
hive they judge (both admins are Baguio members, so the first run cast a supervisor's colleague as "the platform").

| floor | rows |
|---|---|
| F1 hand-off × member | 298 |
| F2 hand-off × layer | 1,643 |
| **F3 hand-off × layer × pillar × member (+A) — the pick, mirrors §CX** | **13,063** (58 already answered by a pair-bearing row) |

**Every hop is a data path the product has (the premise check before the first walk).** The first draft authored hops
from the archetype titles and seeded 14,102 rows on them. Read against each receiving page's own reads, a third of the
claims had no path: a breakdown does not raise an alert-hub alert (alerts are failure signatures and sensor anomalies), a
supervisor does not plan a worker's day (`schedule_items` is a person's own), a PM has an owner and no assignee, the
provider has no dispute reply, community has no appeal. Nothing was walked or banked, so the rows were removed and the
wave re-seeded on corrected hops: 127 hand-offs, each naming the mechanism it rides (logbook-feed;
`notify_wo_assigned` → push → `logbook.html?status=Open`; `notify_submission_decided`; `shift_plans.published_by`;
`report_community_post`; `raise_service_objection`; the failure-signature scan a member may trigger for their own hive).
The census's have-key now carries the receiving page, so a hop rewritten at the same index can never read as answered.

**Seeded 2026-11-04: GJ1..GJ13085** in their own shard (`trajectory_registry_gj.json`, compact; critic rows in
`critic_registry_gj.json`) — GJ-PROD 12,120 · GJ-FND 575 · GJ-PUB 310 · GJ-UX 80. Program 37,001 → 50,086 in scope.

### §GJ.1 The milestones — each block closes with a production push

| milestone | block | scenarios | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M7** | the shift's hand-offs (GJ-PROD) | J2 J3 J9 J22 J23 J29 J17 G-SHIFT G-SENSOR G-MULTI | 4,323 |
| **M8** | the record's hand-offs (GJ-PROD) | J4 J21 J24 J14 G-ESC G-ADV G-LEAVE | 2,240 |
| **M9** | the market's and the team's growth (GJ-PROD) | J1 J25 J19 J5 J6 J27 J7 J15 J10 J30 J8 J12 J31 G-SVC G-MOD G-ONB G-PUBLIC | 5,557 |
| **M10** | founder and public hand-offs (GJ-FND + GJ-PUB) | every hop whose receiving page is founder or public | 885 |
| **M11** | the group's UX face (GJ-UX) | scenario × member, graded by the critic deepwalk | 80 |

A row's block is `gj.milestone` (declared once, in `group_journey_census.GJ_MILESTONES`); `trajectory_priority.py` orders
the queue block-major and counts each block; the header names the block that is DUE; the runbook's
`# M<n> release (date) ✅ DEPLOYED` heading closes it (`released()` reads `M\d+`). The next block starts after its
predecessor's push is recorded.

### §GJ.2 The instrument and the banker

- **`tools/prove_group_journeys.mjs`** — one Chromium context per member, signed in as their own account; per hop the
  sender acts through the page's own controls (the LOG1-3 wizard, exported from `live_page_journeys.registry.mjs`; the
  entry's own edit modal; the page's own Refresh), the receiver lands by the hop's channel and the screen is read (U),
  psql AS THE RECEIVER finds the record or the push in `service_outbox` (F), a member of another hive reads 0 rows (I),
  and the landing is re-read on 3G (A). Two passes with viewports swapped. Everything tagged is removed after; today's
  analytics snapshot and the hive's failure alerts are snapshotted and restored. `--teeth` plants a push that never fires
  and a foreign member who is let in — both must read FAIL.
- **`tools/bank_gj_rows.py`** — banks a row (locking, 60) only when the receipt is a real two-pass walk under 3 h old and
  the hand-off's act and the row's pillar held in both passes. The walk answers F · D · S · A · C · L directly; the
  contract layers (AU · AV · H · LB · RL · CI · CA) bank only when the cube's own row for the same (page, layer, pillar,
  persona) is closed. `--check` is gate **`gj-rows-hold`** (Platform, every board).

### §GJ.3 Walk order

M7 first, one scenario per batch in the queue's order (evidence → page class → pillar F I U A → persona → weakest
layer); defects fixed as found and locked by a gate; a recipe per hand-off added to the prover as each scenario is walked.

### §GJ.4 J2 walked: breakdown to close-out, Wilfredo Malabanan (worker) × Ramon Castillo (supervisor), Baguio

The instrument's first scenario. `--teeth` bites (a push that never fires reads F FAIL, a foreign member let in reads
I FAIL). What the two browsers found, each fixed in the change that walked it:

- **A supervisor could not hand a worker's job to anyone (hand-off 2, a defect).** The work-order form says "supervisors
  approve, assign, and verify", and `tg_guard_approval` reserves those states for them, but logbook's UPDATE policy is
  the author's alone. On a teammate's entry the supervisor read "Only the person who wrote an entry can edit or delete
  it", so the seven-state workflow could not be driven by the role it was built for. **Fixed:** `set_logbook_wo`
  (migration `20261104000001`) moves only `wo_state` and `wo_assigned_to`, for an active supervisor of the entry's hive,
  to an active member, with the trail line and the assignee's push; the entry's view offers the supervisor "Move the
  work order". The owner-only policy is not widened. Probe `logbook__a_supervisor_moves_a_work_order` (in the
  psql-probe-suite: the author refused, another hive's supervisor refused, an outsider refused as assignee, a direct
  UPDATE still 0 rows). Walked: the push reads "M-001 was assigned to you by Ramon Castillo", and the worker lands on
  the open list with the job.
- **The daily failure-signature scan re-wrote every standing alert with the model, every day (a defect).** One scan of
  Baguio upserted 42 alerts and made 42 AI calls, 41 of them the same pattern on the same evidence as the day before:
  the free-tier quota production shares (OpenRouter 200 a day). **Fixed:** a current alert with unchanged evidence keeps
  its detail; only a new, re-emerged or changed alert is written by the model. Edge function: a Leg B item at M7.
- **alert-hub could never show 30 of Baguio's 50 standing patterns (a defect).** The pattern read took the 20 newest,
  said "the 20 newest of 50", and Load more only paged what had been fetched. A pattern re-confirmed this week keeps its
  October date (the scan's deliberate rule), so it could sit out of reach for good. **Fixed:** the read takes up to 500
  current patterns (bounded: three rules per machine, 14-day expiry) and pages them 30 at a time.
- **Instrument lessons:** a supervisor's logbook opens on the query-first Team Feed, so a teammate's entry arrives as the
  "1 new team entry" badge (tapped), not in the list; the "card" a U reading checks is the record's own card (an
  attribute that names it, else a repeated list item), never a block that holds the "All workers" filter; a hop's
  premise needs data that exercises it (hand-off 5 runs on a machine with no standing alert, read from the database); a
  receiver who arrives by a push reads the push first; a system-raised alert names where it came from, not a person;
  every cleanup step runs alone (the first teeth run died on a wrong column and left three audit lines, an XP row and
  two "new device" registrations).

### §GJ.5 J3 walked (the PM month, Christine Dizon × Hector Salvador, Manila) and what preparing J9 found

J3 holds 5/5 in both passes: the supervisor's Add Asset wizard schedules a machine (found by the worker through
pm-scheduler's own search), it tops the worker's day planner (the rail behind "Open items" lists the 30 most urgent, so
the walk's machine is onboarded with its last service over a year back), the worker's completion is read in the asset's
Completion History by name and date, and analytics and the month's report state their figures. J2 re-walked 5/5 on the
stricter readings below. 668 GJ rows are banked; `gj-rows-hold` holds them all.

**The readings got stricter:** a page with no record marker is read for its own dated statement on 3G (it passed on
"the page loaded"); a statement must carry its value (analytics-report's toolbar word "Period" is not one); a page that
builds its statement on a tap gets the tap (Generate Report); navigation under slow 3G gets 150 s and anything over a
minute is said SLOW (analytics.html takes ~60 s at 390 - a reading for the performance lens).

**Preparing J9 found three defects in the hand-off of work, fixed with their probes:**
- **A job handed to you was in neither your logbook nor your day.** Every personal list is the entries you wrote, so a
  job a supervisor raised and assigned to a worker was pushed ("Open the Logbook to see it") to a page that could not
  show it. The logbook's open-jobs panel (where the push lands) and the day planner's open items now include the jobs
  assigned to you, each saying who raised it.
- **The assignee could not start or finish the job.** `advance_assigned_wo` (migration `20261104000002`) moves the work
  order to in progress or completed for the active assignee only; the entry offers "Started" / "Work done". Probe
  `logbook__the_assignee_moves_their_job_forward`.
- **A decision named nobody and pointed the wrong way.** An approved machine's owner was sent to the logbook and a
  rejected machine's owner was told to "open Inventory to see why". `notify_submission_decided` (migration
  `20261104000003`) names the supervisor and sends a machine to Asset Hub on that machine, a part to Inventory. Probe
  `hive__a_decision_says_who_and_where`.

**M7 release items so far:** migrations `20261104000001`..`03` (Leg A), `failure-signature-scan` (Leg B), logbook,
alert-hub and dayplanner (Leg C).

### §GJ.6 J9, J22, J23, J29, J17 walked

- **J9** (the supervisor's week, Lucena) 5/5 both passes: the job raised and handed on reaches the worker's day ("Assigned
  to you - raised by Marites Villanueva", §GJ.5's fix walked), the published shift plan, a worker's post, a submitted
  machine in the approval queue, and the decision pushed back naming the approver and landing on the machine.
  **Fixed: the crew could not tell who released their shift plan** - publishing tells the supervisor "released under your
  name", the plan carries `published_by` / `published_at`, and the crew saw only "published". shift-brain's pill now reads
  "Published by <name> · <Manila time>".
- **J22** (one machine's whole life, Lucena) 5/5 both passes: commissioned the product's way (the logbook's asset form,
  then the hive's approval queue) and read on the machine's own page ("Added and approved by Marites Villanueva on Nov 4,
  2026"); the worker's job on it chosen through the picker's search; its PM plan; its numbers; the trail line.
- **J23** (one spare part, Manila) 4/4 both passes: the part added to the shelf ("Added by Hector Salvador"), issued
  against a job through the logbook's own parts picker, the count moved 10 → 9 "by Christine Dizon".
  **Fixed: a machine's history named the job and not the part it consumed** - Asset Hub's history line now ends
  "· parts: V-belt B52 ×1", from the entry's own `parts_used`.
- **J29** (typhoon season, Baguio): the storm job pushed to the worker and opened on "Assigned to you"; an entry written
  with the network off (the browser set offline) synced to the supervisor's team feed when it returned; the week's
  downtime counted. The storm plan's publish needed its fixture: Baguio's night plan was already published, and
  `shift_plans_forward_only_status` rightly refuses published → draft for every writer, so the walk's setup runs with
  triggers off and the snapshot restores it.
- **Instrument lessons:** a record shown in a dialog reads as the dialog; a repeated row has children of its own (two
  lines with one class inside a row are not records); a list card may stay lean when the record's own page says who and
  when, and the route opens that page; a plan the product generates on the walk's first open is kept and set back to
  draft, never deleted (deleting it forced a fresh model call and left the second pass nothing to publish); **a
  data-writing walk is never wrapped in an outer timeout** - J23's first pass was killed mid-hop, its `finally` never ran,
  and its tagged rows were removed by hand.
- **J17** (sensor to the person, Manila) 3/3 both passes: a plant bridge posts twelve hours of normal vibration
  (2.0-2.2 mm/s) and then five high readings; the ingest flags the five against the machine's own baseline (|z| > 3), and
  the worker meets them on the alert hub, on the machine's page and on the home. Four defects fixed on the way:
  - **A machine that simply reports was "drifting out of band".** The anomaly composer's sensor source counted EVERY
    reading of the last 7 days, 25 points each, with no anomaly test - so any machine on a live bridge scored 100 within
    the hour, however normal its values (pass a: 41 healthy readings, 0 flagged, an anomaly raised anyway). It counts
    only the flagged readings now, and its evidence carries the newest one's time (mig 20261105000001; probe
    `hive__a_machine_that_reports_is_not_an_anomaly`, three of its legs FAIL on the old composer).
  - **Below Stair 3 the alert hub hid every measured anomaly** - and every seeded hive sits at Stair 1. The stair gate is
    right for the fused engine (a forecast that thin data makes lie); a flagged reading is a measurement against its own
    baseline of 12+ samples. Below Stair 3 the panel now lists the last 24 hours' flagged readings ("Sensor anomaly:
    vibration read 13.6 mm/s, 3-sigma off its own baseline · flagged reading <time> · Open the machine"); at Stair 3+
    the fused panel's "5 of 33" opens with **Show all**, and an active signal says when (newest flagged reading, or when
    it was last checked) - only acknowledged and resolved cards carried a time.
  - **The home's Today card said "vibration_mm_s flagged anomaly" and never which machine**, and its button linked
    `asset-hub.html?id=`, a parameter asset-hub never reads. The dashboard payload carries the machine, the reading and
    its unit (mig 20261105000002), the card reads "<machine>: vibration out of band" and opens that machine.
  - **The One Thing hid every other thing.** In a hive with a critical-risk asset (rank 100) a fresh sensor anomaly
    (rank 85) never reached the home and nothing said there was a second thing. Under the One Thing, the next two now
    each get a line that opens them, with their age, and past two a line says how many more.
  - Asset Hub's banner printed the column code and a bare value; it prints the parameter's name and the reading's unit.
- **Instrument lessons:** a bridge reports over time and the ingest judges a reading against what came BEFORE it - the
  first walk posted baseline and spike in one batch and nothing could be flagged; parameter names follow the platform's
  own convention (`vibration`, `temperature`, `current_draw`, whose unit the ingest derives) - a walk-invented
  `vibration_mm_s` read back with no unit.

### §GJ.7 G-SHIFT, G-SENSOR, G-MULTI

- **G-SHIFT** (the shift changes hands, Manila): 5/5 both passes: the outgoing worker's open job in the incoming worker's handover ("opened ... by Christine Dizon"), the plan the supervisor published ("Published by <name> · <time>"), the job on the incoming worker's logbook, their Started on it in the supervisor's ("in progress · Jericho"), and the printed handover naming him as incoming.
  - **The handover left out the shift that was handing over.** `shift-planner-orchestrator` carried "open entries
    created more than 8 hours ago", and a shift is 8 hours: a plan built at 14:30 cut off at 06:30, so every job the
    outgoing morning shift opened and could not finish - the thing a handover exists to pass on - was missing from the
    list the page heads "Jobs still open from the prior shift", while older backlog was carried. A job is now carried
    when it was opened before THIS shift began (the window's start in Manila time), and newest first: oldest-first, a
    hive with more open jobs than the cap of 30 carried its oldest backlog, and the briefing names only the first eight.
  - **A work-order pill named no one:** "in progress · CD", with the full name in a hover title a phone never shows. It
    names the assignee's first name.
  - The printed handover (hive.html) names the outgoing worker and, under "Incoming", the person it is handed to; the
    walk reads the document the page sends to the print window. Its A reading runs on the outgoing worker's connection,
    whose phone produces the paper (`aOnSender`).
- **G-SENSOR** (reading to PM, Lucena): 4/4 both passes: the bridge's spike on the worker's alert hub ("Sensor anomaly: vibration read 13.6 mm/s, 3-sigma off its own baseline"), the worker's Mark seen on the supervisor's card ("seen by David Velasco, <time>"), the PM the supervisor scheduled for that machine on the worker's list, and the worker's job on it in the supervisor's logbook.
  - **A flagged reading could be seen by no one on record.** The worker who walked to the machine had no way to say so,
    and the supervisor could not tell whether anyone had. Each measured card now carries the feed's own hive-wide
    "Mark seen" (`alert_dismissals`, under the person's name; the trail line names the machine and the reading, not
    the card's key), keyed by machine, parameter and Manila day so a new day's flag asks for fresh eyes; the
    supervisor's card reads "seen by <name>, <time>".
  - Instrument: the logbook's machine picker is searched by what a person types - the machine's name. The helper
    searched by the walk's tag, which only works for a machine the walk made and named with it (J22).
- **G-MULTI** (one person in two hives, Baguio and Batangas): 5/5 both passes.
  - **A push from one hive opened in the other.** Liza Mercado works in both plants. Supervisor A's "Work order
    assigned to you" linked `/logbook.html?status=Open` with no hive in it, and every page reads the hive the device
    last stood in - so, standing in Batangas, she opened a logbook where Baguio's job does not exist. The same held for
    an approval decision (asset-hub, inventory). Each push now names its hive (`&hive=<id>`, mig 20261105000003, probe
    `logbook__a_push_opens_in_its_hive`), and the shared start-up (`whStartupHive`, used by every hive-scoped page)
    seats that hive only after confirming, by account, that the person is an active member of it; it says "Opened in
    <hive>", removes the parameter; a link to a hive the person is not in leaves the page on their own hive and says so. Both
    cases are walked in a browser by gate `a-link-opens-in-its-hive` (`tools/prove_hive_link.mjs`), which FAILS on the
    pre-fix utils.js.
  - Walked: the link seats Batangas for her entry there; supervisor B finds that entry and not her Baguio one, and RLS
    agrees (1 row and 0); standing in Batangas, she opens A's push and reads "Assigned to you · raised by Ramon
    Castillo" in Baguio; B's PM is on her list in Batangas and not in Baguio; her Baguio entry's trail line is in A's
    trail and refused to B.
- **Instrument lessons (G-MULTI):** each cast member is seated in the hive they were drawn from, and the cleanup runs
  in every one; the I reading's witness must be outside EVERY hive the scenario stands in (outside only the home hive,
  it was a Batangas member reading Batangas rows); two tags in one walk must not be prefixes of each other - J9's act
  found hop 1's "<tag>-A" entry for hop 3's "<tag>" and read an unassigned job.
- **No group walk spends a model call on the shift briefing.** shift-brain builds a plan on the shift's first open,
  and its briefing is an LLM call - J9's walks spent one a pass just by arriving. The planner takes a LOCAL-ONLY
  `debug_fault_inject` (decided on the same local-runtime test callAI applies again inside), every walk session sends
  it, and the plan is built from the real rows with the deterministic fallback briefing. The guard that proves such
  hooks are dead in production (`validate_debug_echo_prod_safe.py`) had never been registered and had gone red against
  a correct gate after the W4 refactor; it is gate `debug-hooks-prod-dead` now and covers the planner's flag.
- **Instrument lessons:** the reader takes the smallest element carrying the marker, so a person's name alone is a weak
  marker where the same name labels other rows (in Manila the carry-over rows read "opened ... by <the supervisor>" and
  the publish was read off a carried job) - the publish hop reads the pill's own words, "Published by <name>"; a pass lost
  to a cause outside the product (the edge runtime restarting) is re-walked alone and merged onto the receipt, which
  keeps the older time; each cast member stands in the hive they were drawn from, and the cleanup runs in every one.

### §GJ.8 The contract half of a hand-off, walked where the cube never was

After all ten M7 scenarios held, **1,312 M7 rows were still open, every one on a contract layer** (AU AV CA CI H LB RL).
The banker took a contract row's half from the cube's closed row for the same page x layer x pillar x persona - and
for 25 of M7's (page, persona) cells the cube had never seeded one: no supervisor rows at all on logbook, pm-scheduler,
alert-hub, shift-brain, asset-hub, dayplanner, inventory or hive (the cube's supervisor rows sit on nine report pages).
Those rows were waiting on rows that were never going to exist. The plan's own rule closes them - "the contract
sub-layers close by the registered library provers per (page, persona), exactly as the cube did" - so the provers now
walk those cells:

- **`tools/lx_walk_args.py --gj M7`** turns a milestone's open GJ contract rows into the library walk's cells, cast by
  the walk's own rule (the receiving person: a non-admin supervisor or worker of the scenario's hive), and
  `tools/lx_walk.js` walks them through the Playwright MCP at both viewports. **44 cells, 1,060 rows, all hold.**
- **`tools/bank_lx_walk.py`** judges a GJ row with the same verdicts and KEEPS it in `.tmp/gj_contract/<id>.json` - it
  banks nothing; **`tools/bank_gj_rows.py`** banks the row when the group walk's receipt AND that verdict both hold, and
  a verdict is void once its page changes.
- **AU through F and I** is the identity-after-change replay's own rule (`bank_au_identity_rows.py`): the relations the
  page's source reads, graded on ONE unexpired token by a green report from a subject of the persona's own role.
  **H through F and I** is the header set the host serves for the path, the same bytes whoever asks
  (`prove_w4_layer_headers.check_page` against the local `vercel.json` substitute).
- **One defect, fixed:** hive.html, as a supervisor, answered a 429 on `get_adoption_risk_current` by running
  `compute_adoption_risk` (a write) and reading again - a failed read counted as a "stale" snapshot. A failed read now
  shows "Not loaded" and calls nothing more; the re-walk holds.
- **And one found re-walking J2:** with the analytics service down (stopped by me to free memory - a lesson kept in
  memory), every phase failed and the page's verdict said "Analytics unavailable" while its source chip said
  "Recomputed just now" over a tab with no result. A tab with no result now says the analysis could not run.
- **The result: every one of M7's 4,323 rows is banked** - all ten scenarios re-walked on the final prover, 1,104
  library verdicts holding, and the AU and H halves from their own provers.

### §GJ.9 M8 walked - the record's hand-offs (J4 J24 J14 G-LEAVE G-ADV J21 G-ESC)

**What preparing M8 found before a walk ran (the premise check, 2026-11-05).** Every hop is a data path; reading each
receiving page's own reads against the hop's claim found these gaps, each fixed at its cause:

- **J24, the machine's safety status** - the logbook showed the LOTO badge and the permit; the machine's own history
  (asset-hub) said nothing of either, and the hive's trail kept neither on the entry's line. Both now carry the
  lock-out, the permit and a safety-risk consequence.
- **J4, the trail before and after** - the trail named which fields a worker amended, never what they said before.
  `changed_fields {field: {from, to}}` rides the edit line; audit-log already rendered it.
- **J14 / G-LEAVE, the removed member told who and when** - "removed by a supervisor", undated. The removal is now
  stamped on the member's own row (`removed_by`, `removed_at`, mig 20261105000004, a trigger), the one row a removed
  person can still read; both notices name who, when, and what stays theirs.
- **G-LEAVE, the inherited job** - handing a departed member's open job on was a direct update that told nobody;
  it now sends the same "Work order assigned to you" push as every other assignment.
- **G-ADV, refused in words** - a foreign member opening an entry's link read "WorkHive did not answer, try again"
  (PGRST116 fell through to the outage sentence). No-row now has its own sentence, without confirming the record.
- **J21, the opt-in told to the hive** - only the supervisor's menu and the supervisor-only trail showed that the
  hive's figures were being shared. Every member now reads it on the roster, with who turned it on and when. The
  sector view (ph-intelligence) opens at Stair 3 and no local hive is above Stair 1: the walk shows the reader's hive
  at Stair 3 (a fixture, named in the receipt, put back after).
- **G-ESC, who reported it** - the Mod Queue said why a post was flagged, not who flagged it or when.
- **No walk spends a model call on a report**: analytics-orchestrator honours the LOCAL-ONLY `debug_fault_inject`
  (gate `debug-hooks-prod-dead`), and the report path - which shipped an empty `action_plan: {}` when no model
  answered - takes the prescriptive path's two steps (empty = none; the records' own plan).

**Three security holes found reading M9's premises, fixed in M8's release** (each verified through PostgREST as the
party, then guarded and probed with teeth): a dispute party could write the admin's decision (`marketplace_disputes`),
a client could rewrite a provider's quote (`service_offers`, no trigger at all), and a supervisor could rewrite a
member's reply / an author accept their own (`community_replies` - the posts had the rule, the replies never got it).

**J4 walked, 4/4 at both viewports (Alma Soriano x Corazon Bautista, Batangas).** The first walk held 3 of 4 and found a
defect no gate had seen: **the amendment trail had recorded no changed field for any edit since it began listing them**
(SL L2, 2026-10-21). It compared the saved values with `existing`, the list's own cached entry, which the online save
had already refreshed to the new values. W4410 (2026-10-12) had copied only the status. The save now copies the whole row
once, before anything writes. The trail then read the save's own stamps (`hive_id`, the AI-provenance list) as the
worker's changes, so those are left out and an empty list counts as nothing. The supervisor's trail reads
"ALMA SORIANO Edited logbook entry BRM-P-102 · just now · Changed: problem · Problem <before> → <after>". Hand-off 4
generates the report and reads one more Total Failure than the engine stated before the worker logged; the report's
plan, with no model answering, is the records' own.

**J24 walked, 4/4 at both viewports.** The worker logs a breakdown through the wizard's own Safety Isolation section
(LOTO + permit `PTW-…`, consequence "Safety risk"). The supervisor's card reads "🔒 LOTO PTW-… Safety risk". The
machine's history says "locked out (LOTO, permit …), safety risk". The trail line keeps the permit. The report the
supervisor generates states one more "failure classified as a safety risk" than the engine said before.

**J14 walked: the first walk held 2 of 4 and found two defects in what "leaving" leaves a person.**
- **A removed member could not read their own XP history.** `achievement_xp_log` is name-keyed. Its read policy and
  `my_recent_xp()` admit `auth_worker_names()`, which returns nothing for a member whose only membership is 'kicked'.
  Their achievements page kept the totals and said "No XP this week" for work just logged, while the notice told them
  their achievements stay theirs. A read-only sibling, `auth_own_history_names()` (mig 20261105000008), adds their own
  removed memberships' names, each guarded against a namesake. Only the XP log's read and `my_recent_xp()` use it;
  `auth_worker_names()` also decides marketplace inserts and is not widened.
- **The removal was told once.** A toast was stashed across one reload, then the hive was forgotten, so the next visit
  (the 3G re-read) was a plain "join or create" screen. `my_recent_removal()` (in mig 20261105000004) gives the person
  their own most recent removal within 30 days, with the hive's name, which they can no longer read themselves. The
  onboarding screen says it on every visit.

**J14 then held 4/4 at both viewports**: the removal notice names who, when and what stays theirs on every visit, 3G
included; the supervisor's logbook and trail keep the leaver's work under the leaver's name; the leaver's achievements
list their newest job ("Logbook entry submitted · 3m ago · +20").

**G-LEAVE walked, 4/4 at both viewports on its first walk.** The premise check had already fixed the hop that mattered:
handing a departed member's open job on (`assignDepartedEntry`, a direct update) now pushes "Work order assigned to you"
like every other assignment. The remaining worker's logbook reads "Assigned to you · raised by Christine Dizon", and the
roster they read no longer lists her.

**An instrument lesson the walks paid for twice:** a session restart marks background tasks "stopped" without stopping
their processes. A walk that removes a member is in a fragile state between its act and its cleanup. Check the
processes, and let a live walk finish, before cleaning up by hand.

**G-ADV walked, 3/3 at both viewports.** A Batangas worker holding a Lucena entry's link reads "Couldn't find this entry
in a hive you belong to. It may have been removed, or the link is for a hive you are not a member of. Your session is
fine." This replaced "WorkHive did not answer, try again". The machine's link reads "That asset link could not be
resolved in this hive". Neither draws the record. Two fixes came from reading it on 3G:
- The entry link waited for the whole logbook (a second full load) before trying the entry. It now opens the entry at
  once.
- The refusal arrived before the page finished loading, so its toast faded unseen. A refused link's sentence now stays
  above the list until dismissed.

**J21 walked, 3/3 at both viewports (Marites Villanueva × David Velasco, Lucena; Corazon Bautista, Batangas, reads).**
- Every Lucena member's roster card says "This hive shares its anonymised figures with the PH benchmarks - totals and
  averages only, never names or machines. Turned on by Marites Villanueva on Nov 5, 2026, 01:51 PM."
- The other hive's supervisor presses Generate and reads the honest below-the-floor sector view: "Not enough hives
  share their benchmarks yet: 1 of the 3 needed have opted in". Lucena and Marites are named nowhere on the screen, and
  the reader is refused Lucena's own row and figures.
- The first walk found the passage told what the figures rest on and not how old they are. Each "Based on" line now
  carries "in the report generated <date>".
- Fixtures, named in the receipt and put back after: the reader's hive shown at Stair 3, since the page opens at
  Stair 3 and no local hive is above 1; the consent and the network report are restored exactly.

**G-ESC hand-off 1 walked, at both viewports** (Christine Dizon reports a post; Hector Salvador's Mod Queue). The
supervisor's card reads "⚑ Reported by Christine Dizon, Nov 5, 2026, 02:06 PM: Spam or off-topic - Personal sales in
the plant feed". It said only the reason until the M8 fix. Hand-offs 2-3 are the platform's decision on the public
board, M10's (its premise is in m10_map). The walk reaches the post as a person does: the feed draws its cards as you
scroll, then its own "⋯" menu, then "Report this post".

**The contract half (the cube's library provers per page x persona).** `lx_walk_args.py --gj M8` gave the cells six at
a time, walked through the Playwright MCP at both viewports in three batches with 0 problems: 507 verdicts hold.

**All 2,240 M8 rows are banked.** The direct layers came from the seven scenarios' receipts, the contract half from 507 library verdicts (three batches, none failing). M10's hops on audit-log ride the same walks: 420 of its 885 rows are banked. The release gate's own audit then found the new definer functions still callable by `anon`. On Supabase a revoke from PUBLIC never reaches anon, which is granted explicitly on every new function. All five now name anon, and the three trigger functions refuse every caller. The psql suite then read the new reply guard as a breach: the write-authz recipe counted a cross-hive move's touched rows, and a trigger that pins `hive_id` touches the row and moves nothing. The generator now asks where the row sits (still visible in its own hive = `pinned`, otherwise the count fails); with the trigger and both policies lifted the move reads `1` and fails. 214 of 214 recipes hold.

### §GJ.10 M9 walked - marketplace, onboarding and integrations (J19 J1 G-ONB J31 G-MOD J7 J25 J5 J12 G-PUBLIC J8 J30 J15 G-SVC J6 J10 J27)

**Every hand-off that ended in silence, fixed at its cause.** Each scenario's premise was read against the receiving
page's own reads before a walk ran; the walks then found what reading could not. In order of harm:

- **A stranger read every seller's contact (security, J31).** `marketplace_sellers` was granted whole to `anon`, so the
  masking view's contact column was undone by reading the table under it. Column grants now give a stranger the badge
  (tier, verifications, sales, rating, response) and nothing else (mig 20261106000002; probe with teeth).
- **A provider's track record was the reader's own slice of it (J6).** "N jobs done · ★rating" on the quote a client
  chooses from was counted under the reader's RLS: every provider read "0 jobs done" to every client who had not hired
  them already (Hector Salvador 2 -> 0). One SECURITY DEFINER aggregate (`service_provider_record`) feeds the view, so
  every reader gets the same record - and the client's review, written into a field that says "a sentence for other
  clients", is now read: on the next client's quote and on the provider's console (mig 09; probe with teeth).
- **A person with two provider identities could not choose which one answered (J6).** A hive's members are its field
  crew, so a member with their own business holds two identities; the server picked "verified first" and never said
  which. Jericho Bonifacio's quote went out as his hive's team. `p_provider_id` (one of the caller's own) on quote and
  accept, and an "Answer as" choice whenever a request reached more than one (mig 12).
- **A quote that could not be honoured, and the provider's wallet sentence shown to the client (J6).** A provider takes
  a job only while holding 10% of it in credits; an identity with P0 could quote, and the client choosing it read "You
  need PHP600 in credits... Top up to accept it". A quote is now refused to the provider (with the amounts) when its
  identity cannot hold the job, and a balance spent before the client chooses is told to the client in their terms;
  the request stays open (mig 13; probe with teeth).
- **The provider's disputed job never said what the client reported (G-SVC).** The card said "the client reported a
  problem" while the client's reason and its time sat in the job's events. The job's own read carries the report - the
  status-change trigger writes a note-less 'disputed' event in the same instant, so the reason is the event that has one
  (mig 08; probe with teeth).
- **A worker never learned their password had been reset, and could not change it (J19)** - workers sign in with an
  address that receives nothing, so the emailed recovery link was the only change path. The reset is stamped on the
  account; sign-in tells them who reset it and when and asks for their own; everyone has a Change password control.
- **Moderation told no one (G-MOD)**: `moderate_reported_post` records the decision on the post, pushes the author and
  every reporter, and the community page reads it back (mig 03). **An accepted answer earned nothing (J7)**: +30 XP,
  reversed on un-accept, none for your own answer to your own question (mig 04).
- **No invite link, and a roster that said who but not when (J1, G-ONB)**; the welcome names the hive's supervisors.
- **A teammate's profile said "No badges yet" about badges kept private, and the top discipline was hidden on every
  profile by a stray selector (J25)**; a work order could be assigned to a typed name nobody holds.
- **A scope item, a linked calculation, a change order said nothing of who added it (J8, J30)** (migs 05, 06).
- **A CMMS's work orders were written under a supervisor's name and paid XP; its sync status never moved; what it
  imported could not be read (J15)** (mig 07, cmms-webhook-receiver).
- **A shared calculation was undated; a shared post had no link (G-PUBLIC, J31).**
- **The fleet owner's month had no cost in it (J10)**: no table carried a price. `inventory_items.unit_cost` (stamped
  by the server), the inventory form and detail, and an analytics card "Parts cost by machine" priced by the part's ID -
  a part logged by name only is counted unpriced, never guessed - with its basis said every time: "Priced N of M parts
  used ... Labour and outside services are not counted." (mig 10; probe with teeth; the fleet seeder prices its parts).
  The walk registers the unit the way a fleet owner does - integrations' "Add my vehicle" (the asset with its plate and
  odometer, its PM schedule and its starter parts in one act); the logbook's machine form has no vehicle type. Its
  first reading of the card found the row named "NBX 6851": the logbook's machine code for a vehicle is its plate, so
  the card now names the asset and keeps the code beside it ("Isuzu NLR delivery truck · NBX 6851").
- **A parts deal gone wrong had nowhere to go after the first word (J27).** A review could not be answered; a "Report
  listing" reached the founder console and its answer reached no one (the panel even sent a signed-in member's report
  with the public key, so it carried no account); a listing WorkHive took down told its seller nothing, and an
  unpublished one read "Draft: Pending Review". Now: one public answer per review from the listing's seller
  (`reply_to_listing_review`, the reviewer pushed); reports carry their sender's account and a separate "Answer to the
  sender" (the console's admin note stays internal - the first draft would have pushed it, caught before it shipped);
  "Your reports" in the feedback panel; a moderated listing pushes its seller and its card says why (mig 11).

**Found by the contract half and the suite, not by the scenarios:** analytics asked the same on-time figure once per
phase, so when its saved snapshots could not be read (a 429 with Retry-After 5 s) one refusal became five identical
requests - now asked once per hive and period, and again only on the person's own Refresh. And the prover's own
cleanup stranded rows: every step runs in `replica` mode to pass the guards, which silences ON DELETE CASCADE too, so a
walk's deleted post left its replies and XP awards behind (34 orphans across 7 tables, some from other provers'
fixture hives). The orphans are gone and the cleanup ends with a catalog-driven sweep of what each cascading key would
have removed. All 1,529 M9 contract rows were walked through the Playwright MCP and every batch holds.

**Re-premised on the product's real model (for Ian):** J25 badges are private by design; J12 / G-PUBLIC - a code join
is admission, there is no people-approval; J27 - the parts escrow-dispute loop was retired on 2026-08-03, so the walk
follows review -> answer -> report -> moderation (rebuilding escrow is a product decision); J6 - pre-match anonymity is
the design (the client sees a count per area, the provider a coarse area; names arrive with the quote); J7 - +30 XP is
a new economy entry.

**Fixtures, each named in its receipt:** G-SVC's finished job; J6's provider credits for the hold and the provider's
doing between "chosen" and "done"; J15's webhook secret.

### §GJ.11 M10 walked - founder and public hand-offs (G-ESC 2-3, G-PUBLIC, the audit-log hops of J4 J14 J19 J22 J24 G-MULTI)

**The premise check found the leak before any walk did.** M10's receiving pages are the founder console and the public
roadmap. Reading what the roadmap actually reads, before walking it:

- **The public roadmap would have published who sent each item (security, latent).** `feedback/index.html` read
  `platform_feedback` directly through the policy `is_public = true`, and anon and authenticated both held SELECT on every
  column. The page asked for seven harmless columns; the API answered whatever was asked. The first item the founder
  published would have handed any visitor:
  - the sender's email, account id, browser string, name and hive;
  - the founder's internal note.

  Proven as anon locally. Production had the same grants and 0 public items, so nothing had leaked. The board now reads
  `public_feedback_board()`, which carries the words, the kind, the status and when it was set, and the votes. The
  table's public policy is dropped and anon's read revoked (mig 20261106000014; probe with teeth).
- **Anyone could take back anyone's vote.** `platform_feedback_votes` was readable by `true`, so every visitor's vote token
  could be listed, and `toggle_feedback_upvote` takes a token. A visitor now reads only their own votes, by their own
  token (`my_feedback_votes`); the table is read by no client.
- **The gate that should have caught it was asking about rows, not columns.** `validate_public_read_surface` had declared
  the table's public branch intentional. It now asks the column question of every caller-blind read policy, with a live
  mutant in its self-test. It had also been red since M8 without any board showing it: it is skip_if_fast, and M8's
  `auth_own_history_names()` was missing from its caller vocabulary.
- **A report a supervisor cannot settle had nowhere to go (G-ESC hand-offs 2-3).** The Mod Queue offered Keep and Remove
  and nothing for what is not theirs to decide. "Send to WorkHive" files a private item: bound to the supervisor's
  account, linked to the post, carrying the reports' reasons and never a reporter's name, and never public (a CHECK holds
  it, the founder included). WorkHive's answer reaches the supervisor and every reporter, as a push that opens straight
  to "Your reports" (`?reports=1`). The reporter's community notice also says WorkHive decided, instead of "waiting for a
  supervisor" (mig 20261106000015; probe with teeth).
- **The privacy re-premise.** The census said the decision is "the status on the board". An escalation holds a hive's
  own post and the names of its members, so it is never on the public board. Its status reaches the two people it is
  about, on WorkHive's board page, in their own "Your reports".

**What the walk found that reading could not (G-ESC, three walks to 3/3 at both viewports):**

- **The founder's "Save changes" never saved.** The first walk read the escalation filed and bound to the supervisor, but
  WorkHive's decision stayed `new`. My own edit had put a line reading `row` above `const row` in the console's save
  handler. The script parsed, and every click threw before writing. Gate `scripts-parse` now carries a
  temporal-dead-zone lens (`tools/lib/tdz_reads.cjs`), which read 0 across all 202 files once its loop-head scoping was
  right.
- **"Resolved" said what, never who.** The reporter's "Your reports" line read "Resolved: <answer>", and the walk's
  who-check failed: the only "WorkHive" on the card was inside the founder's own words. Every decided state now names
  who decided, in the push's own sentence ("WorkHive resolved it"). The walk checks that sentence, not words in the reply.
- **The contract half:** the `feedback/index.html` library walk, 106 rows (one supervisor viewport re-walked after its
  sign-in left no session), 106/106 hold. **220 G-ESC rows banked.**

### §GJ.12 M11 walked - the group's UX face (every screen each member meets, graded in the walk)

**✅ Deployed 2026-11-07** - production serves `workhive-shell-v594` from `34e77d0b`; public smoke 120/120 and app smoke
26/26 at v594, both clean at 390 (PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_RUNBOOK.md, M11).

**What M11 measures.** M11's 80 rows are scenario × member. Each says: grade every screen THIS member meets in the
scenario, at phone-390 and desktop-1280, as the member lives it in the group walk. The instrument is
`tools/prove_group_journeys.mjs --survey`: each time the walk opens a page for a member it runs `survey_ufai_rubric.js`
there, settled, and again where the hand-off's statement is on screen. `tools/bank_gj_ux.py` banks a row only when every
page it claims has a survey at both viewports from one walk, one lens and under three hours old; any graded dim under
100% is a finding (fixing, 40), none is locking (60). A machine member's "screen" is the copy its functions speak back
(`critic_edge_fn_copy.grade()`).

**The first pass (2026-11-06) and the probes that named the offenders.** The surveys named dims, not elements, for most
findings. A live probe (`.tmp/m11_probe2.js`, signed in through the wall and waiting for a real session) opened each
page in the state the walk left it - a project opened, a report generated, a sheet up - and read the element.

**What the walks found, by class.**
- **Every screen of a single-page app is a page.** project-manager's opened project and pm-scheduler's asset screen had
  no h1 (the list's was hidden), no source chip (the sources filer drops a hidden screen's chip), no primary action.
  Each screen now names itself, says what its figures read and when, and leads with its main write. The opened project
  grades 100% at both widths.
- **A value rebuilt by undoing a transform.** analytics-report printed `17.400000000000006/100` on every machine
  (`100 - (100 - score)`), and the unbroken string widened the supervisor's phone page by 74px. The label prints the
  stored score, rounded.
- **A sentence that names a control that is gone.** The public feedback board told visitors to "tap the 💬 button" -
  retired on 2026-07-20 - and the page loads no nav hub, so nobody on it could send feedback. It has a Send feedback
  button now, an inline guide to the board, and an empty state that names that button.
- **A codemod that rewrote a selector, in production.** The hex-colour codemod (`tools/fix_token_literals.py`, cadf57fa)
  matched hex with `#…\b`, and `\b` ends at `-`: audit-log's `#feed` and the id `#fab-post` read as colours, and
  community's and marketplace's FAB rules became `var(--wh-rose-200, #fab)-post { … }`. The browser drops an invalid
  selector's whole rule, so both "post" buttons have rendered as bare grey buttons after `<main>` in production since
  cadf57fa. Its static proof could not see it (the `var()` resolves back to the same text). Selectors restored; the tool
  now ends a hex at `(?![\w-])` and skips selector position (`_in_selector`, self-test); `hex_to_var.mjs` carried the
  same `\b`. design-source-drift now FAILS on a `var()` in selector position (teeth: 8 hits on the shipped HEAD copies).
- **Section chrome that outlives its section.** marketplace's "Post a listing" FAB stayed on the Services tab beside the
  client's "Choose this provider" and "Hail now" - three primaries for a pane about hailing. It follows the listings
  grid now (by style: `#fab-post{display:flex}` beats `[hidden]`).
- **A record opened in a dialog is a screen with its own primary.** inventory's part detail had only tints (Use Stock,
  Restock), logbook's member entry offered a supervisor one outlined button; each now has one filled action.
- Copy (B3/E4), contrast (C2/C5), targets (F1/Z3), shapes (R3: toggles wear the pill, presses 8px), one primary per screen (A1/G3) - across the 27 pages the 80 rows meet.

**Seven false readings in the lens, each fixed with teeth both ways (`prove_rubric_teeth.mjs`).** V1: the top fold;
a control scrolled out of its own scroll box; a box its scroller clips away. W2: the hub standing down for a dialog.
I2: the shared skeleton's container mark. Z2: names the in-flow cause, not the fixed chrome the wider page carried out.
E3: "loaded when you open this page" states its freshness. Round 2: a control behind an open aria-modal dialog is not a
choice; a role=switch is a held state, not a CTA; a declared print document is paper. Round 3: the open dialog's own
primaries join the pool wherever it lives (the feedback panel and marketplace sheets sit outside `<main>`), and a
closed one (aria-hidden, translated away, opacity 0) is not open; a clickable card is card vocabulary, not an R3
control silhouette; seven-plus unseparated digits are an identifier, not a KPI; a row's own form submit is a row
action. A probe that grades a page with the real rubric (`.tmp/m11_rubric_probe.js`) told the lens apart from the page:
the board graded 100% signed in, so the walk had graded the panel open.

**Result.** 80/80 rows locking. Three rounds plus a short fourth: round 1 (22 scenarios) 35/80; round 2 (29) and round 3 (all 34, on the code that ships and the corrected lens) took it to 76/80; round 3b re-walked the four rows a mid-round lens narrowing or a fix had touched (J23, G-ESC, J30, J8) - 80/80. All 127 hand-offs hold at both viewports in every round. 324 screen surveys across 34 scenarios.

**The last three findings were each a cause one layer down from where the symptom showed.** J30's 130px sideways scroll survived a correct `white-space: normal` on the link pill: nav-hub.js appended a second tokens.css after the page's own styles on the 11 pages that import tokens through components.css, so tokens' `[class$="-pill"]{nowrap}` won a tie it should have lost (nav-hub now leaves a page that imports tokens alone). J23's cta=0 on logbook and asset-hub was the round-3 row-form rule reading a page's own form card as a row (narrowed to record rows: list items, or containers named for a record). J8's "done" pill was brand blue on its own tint (3.9:1), now the text-tuned blue.

| the batch ledger | `critic_found_ledger.json`: each held-red walk's failing classes and each bounced screen, appended by the batch (`tools/critic_found_append.py`) | 61 finds |

## §PRIORITY · The open book in the order it is worked — the less important last, and a push at each milestone (Ian, 2026-10-26)

**A MILESTONE IS A BLOCK OF THE OPEN BOOK (2026-11-04, Wave GJ).** M1..M6 are the tier boundaries; every later wave declares its own blocks in its rows (`gj.milestone`: M7..M11, named in `tools/group_journey_census.GJ_MILESTONES`, see §GJ.1). The queue is block-major, each milestone carries its own count, and the header names the block that is next.

Ian, with 20,314 rows open after the day's seeding: *"we have to prioritize the open trajectories roadmap because we have
massive open trajectories, so we put in the roadmap, we have to push to production when we achieve a considerable
milestone of our trajectories roadmap, but first we have to reprioritize the open trajectories, with less important one
to be on the last."*

**The order is derived, never felt.** `tools/trajectory_priority.py` ranks every open row (in scope and not closed by
the ledger's own rule) in two steps and writes `trajectory_priority.json`; the header's **PRIORITY QUEUE** block and the
registry's `next` pointer read it; `--head N` prints the next N ids.

1. **A TIER from what the row is:**

| tier | what it holds | why it comes where it comes |
|---|---|---|
| **T1** | the bug-hunt and bug-repro rows (BRH, BRP); OWN's defect-shaped lenses on production pages (jobs, dependencies, AI failure modes, WebKit, two devices, Back, search, low-end phones); the keep-abreast rows behind a trip past grace (the overdue pillars/comparisons, the push, the board's own truth) | a defect a real person meets today costs them now |
| **T2** | Wave SE (self-efficacy) and Wave OUT (use · return · repeat use) | the dependent variables of Ian's model — without them no later wave can show it moved anything |
| **T3** | the cube on production pages, weakest layer first (the ledger's closure per layer), F before I before U before A | where the person works |
| **T4** | the journey waves (W3-JN, W4, JS, CX-J), the evidence spine (KA-E), the public refresh and push rows (KA-R articles/calculators, KA-S) | the scenarios and the lane's health |
| **T5** | the cube on founder pages, then public pages (anon first, then the signed-in reader, then assistive) | fewer people, less often |
| **T6** | CX-UX (a rubric class never graded on a page), the accessibility-mode OWN rows, Back on public pages, KA-V (the engines' voice — Ian's monthly sheet), anything left | the long tail |

2. **A SCORE inside the tier, lexicographic and from the registry's own fields:** evidence first (fixing 0 · walked 1 ·
   locking-but-open 2 · specced 3) → the page class (production · founder · public) → the pillar (F 0 · I 1 · U 2 · A 3:
   what a worker loses money on before what merely slows them) → the persona, ordered by how many rows the program has
   already found worth walking as it (worker first, machine-client last — a measured proxy, not a ranking of people) →
   the layer's closure (weakest first).

**MILESTONES ARE TIER BOUNDARIES, AND EACH ONE PROPOSES A PUSH.** When T1 is empty the roadmap proposes a production
push (M1); again when T2 empties (M2), and so on. The push itself stays Ian's gate and follows `PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_RUNBOOK.md`
(Legs A/B/C, the comprehensive smoke, the IndexNow step). On seed day the queue read **T1 397 · T2 0 · T3 9,082 · T4 298
· T5 9,732 · T6 805 — M1 at 397 rows**; the header block carries the live numbers.

**What the ordering is NOT:** a reason to leave a tier unbuilt. T2 reads 0 only because SE and OUT are not seeded yet
(`tools/trajectory_outcome_gaps.py` derives them); a tier's rows are walked in their order, and a lower tier is never
touched while a higher one still has a buildable row — unless its instrument is occupied, in which case the pivot is
to the next tier's non-browser rows, not to a stop.

## §SL · The SUB-LAYER wave — every full-stack layer's sub-layers, on every production, founder and public page (Ian, 2026-10-14)

Ian, after the cause of his missing logbook assets turned out to be a CSP without `wss:` (WebKit threw on the realtime
socket, the start-up died before it loaded the assets, and every Chromium walk had passed): *"I am pretty sure that is
belong to a layer or sublayer of our full stack architectural layer SaaS, so we have to dig deeper to make numbers
trajectories for each full stack architectural layer and sublayers of my SaaS, with the aim to improve our overall UFAI
UI UX of my platform for every production/public/founder pages."*

**WHY SUB-LAYERS.** Until this wave the 13 full-stack layers carried ONE ask each (`LAYER_LENS`) and only LM had
sub-layers (§LM, 10). A layer-wide ask is answered by the first page that passes it, which is how the defect that bit
sat in production for a month: it is sub-layer **H1** (the headers the edge serves for what the page does) meeting
**A3/AV1** (a start-up that survives an optional subsystem, on every engine). Production had said so the whole time.
`client_errors`, read once and read-only, is committed as `production_error_groups.json` (no person identifiers): **55
errors on 10 pages since 2026-09-11**, "WebSocket not available: The operation is insecure." on nine of them (logbook 17,
pm-scheduler 8, hive 7, asset-hub 6, inventory 3, alert-hub 2, dayplanner 2, community 1, marketplace 1), every one
WebKit, plus three older null-element errors on the landing page. The plan named five pages; the snapshot names ten.

### The number — measured, printed with its arithmetic (`python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-sublayers --dry-run`, 2026-10-14)

One row per (page, layer, sub-layer) cell where the page's own source puts it in the sub-layer's ROSTER: `ALL` (a
contract every page keeps) or a source regex (the page contains what the sub-layer governs: a channel, a write, a date,
an upload). Pages, measured from disk by `served_pages()`: **production 27 · founder 12 · public 119 = 158**. Founder =
Ian's 12 admin, founder and developer surfaces, retired ones included; four of them held layers with no row at all.
