The rosters are the regexes measured on 2026-10-14 and approved in direction, kept verbatim in
`tools/sublayer_inventory.py` (`SUBLAYERS`) so the number Ian saw is the number seeded, with one restatement: C2's regex
ended in `window`, which matches `window.` in every script, so it measured ALL; it is declared ALL (same 158 cells) and
its ask says what every page owes. A roster is a CANDIDATE reach, not a verdict: a walk that finds a page outside the
sub-layer's real reach closes the row with that reading as its witness (the W4 n/a precedent), and the regex is
tightened on the forward path only, because the replay is anchored to the registry and no id ever moves. The sub-layers
follow the header's layer NAMES (Caching & CDN, Availability & Recovery); `LAYER_LENS`'s CA and AV asks ("crew
vocabulary", "AI truth") stay with the LXP rows that carry them. Both readings are recorded here so they never drift.

### What an SL row is, and how it closes

`title` = the sub-layer code, its ask, the persona, the page. `sl` carries layer, sub-layer, name, page, page class,
roster, persona, both viewports, instrument, engine, ask and the closing rule. Two instruments, declared on the row so a
title's keywords never re-route it (`live_walk_manifest` reads the declared one, as it does for LM):
- **contract** (2,160 rows: F2 F3 F5 · CA2 · H1 H2 H4 · S3 S4 S5 · L1 · CI1 CI2 CI3 CI4): settled in batches by a
  registered prover over every page of the roster (the W4 contract-layer precedent: the served bytes, a scan, a
  ratchet). Closes on the prover's live basis and the gate that reddens on revert.
- **walk** (1,799 rows, every other sub-layer): walked live as the page's cast through the chrome-devtools MCP at
  phone-390 AND desktop-1280 with the condition induced (an init script that makes a subsystem throw, a refused route, a
  demoted role, a renamed hive, a 1,000-row list), the postgres MCP the witness where it writes. The receipt
  (`record_mcp_walk.py`) names `--layer`, `--sublayer`, `--as-persona` and steps at both viewports.
- **engine webkit** (366 rows: AV1 and CI2 on every page, and every F row on the 10 pages production's `client_errors`
  named): the receipt must also say `--engine webkit`. The ledger holds the row open without it
  (`live_walk_manifest._sl_missing`).

**The cast.** Public pages, and a page only a signed-out visitor reaches (public-feed), are walked `anon`; a founder
surface the hub offers nobody is walked as `oversight`; every other page as the persona most rows walked it as, AMONG
THOSE WHOSE OWN ROUTE the journey-paths gate accepts (`sublayer_inventory.casts` asks the gate's own readers, so the
seeder and the gate cannot disagree about who may walk a page). Personas: anon 2,365 · worker 566 · fleet-supervisor 404
· oversight 328 · buyer 136 · solo-owner 74 · machine-client 46 · supervisor 40.

### Walk order (harm first)

1. **H1 + A3 + AV1 on the ten pages production's `client_errors` named** (logbook, pm-scheduler, hive, asset-hub,
   inventory, alert-hub, dayplanner, community, marketplace, index), in real WebKit and in Chromium, as each page's cast:
   the start-up shows its first list and writes nothing to `client_errors`. The provers this needs, from
   `prove_realtime_blocked_socket.mjs`: `prove_page_survives_optional_failures.mjs` (A3/AV1: fails on the pre-fix
   logbook at `90ed9a8e`, passes today) and `prove_webkit_startup_clean.mjs` (AV1/L1).
2. **L1** on every production page: the trail is read, and a gate reads `production_error_groups.json` on every board.
3. **AU1–AU4**, then **S1–S4**.
4. The batch provers over every page: F2/F3/F5, CA2, H1/H2, S3/S5, CI1/CI3/CI4.
5. **ENH-S**, the solar power-station planner (§ENH), then D, C, LB, RL and the remaining F/A/AV/CA, then OPC, then ENH
   P/L/J/C.

Relevant gates only per batch; the whole board stays Ian's gate.

### What seeding found before a single walk (2026-10-14)

The first seed's own gates reddened, and each finding was real:
- **`journey-paths` caught three of this wave's casts.** `worker` on analytics-report, whose only route runs through
  analytics.html (offered to supervisors and engineers), and `worker` on public-feed (linked only from the landing
  page's signed-out block). The cast rule had checked the page's own hub roles, not its route. It now walks each
  candidate through the gate's readers, and the 4,399 unwalked rows were re-seeded under it, with the same ids.
- **Nine older archetypes were red under the same gate**, which had last passed on the 2026-10-06 board. Seven LXC rows
  routed a buyer through hive.html to analytics.html, a route the hub never offers a buyer, and their walks followed it
  by direct navigation. They describe no path a real buyer takes, so they are **descoped**, the reason at the head of
  each basis and `pct -> 0` withdrawn at its end (VP59's precedent; reversible). Closed falls 12,037 → 12,030, the
  honest direction. Eight unwalked BRH rows (one BRH-J, seven BRH-K) were re-cast to their page's gate-checked cast.
- **The gate read descoped rows.** `declared_paths`, `declared_casts` and `declared_signin_roles` took the first row per
  archetype whatever its status, so the descoped rows kept their findings standing. They now skip descoped rows, like
  every other consumer. That unmasked one banked W4 design row (W45963), whose route had been padded for a buyer from
  the supervisor list; it is re-padded from the buyer's own. The design lens studies marketplace-seller itself, so its
  receipt is unchanged.

Program after seeding: **16,666 in scope · CLOSED 12,030 · 72.2% — OPEN 4,636** = 237 BRH + 3,959 SL + 335 ENH + 105
OPC. The critic extension gained 4,399 pending rows the same instant (R3: every in-scope trajectory has one): 57.6%.

### §SL.1 Walk 1 — H1 + A3 + AV1 on the ten pages production named: 30 of 30 closed, and the policy blocked what no load could see (2026-10-14)

**The instruments.** `tools/prove_page_survives_optional_failures.mjs` (gate `page-survives-optional-failures`): each
page in real WebKit AND Chromium, signed in as its cast through the product's own form, every document served the
SHIPPED vercel.json CSP and Permissions-Policy (only the production Supabase origins mapped to the local stack), once as
served and once with every optional subsystem failing (the WebSocket and indexedDB.open throw SecurityError,
speechSynthesis absent, geolocation denied, Notification/share/clipboard refused, page-view writes failed). The verdict
is production's own signal: an insert into `client_errors` with context `uncaught-error` or `unhandled-rejection`.
**40/40 clean. Teeth:** the pre-fix logbook (`90ed9a8e`) writes `unhandled-rejection: WebSocket not available: The
operation is insecure.`, the exact message Ian's iPhone wrote for a month. Then the chrome-devtools MCP, at a true 390 and
1280, as each page's cast (Bryan Garcia for the worker and buyer pages, Leandro Marquez for the supervisor's), the same
failures induced by `navigate_page`'s `initScript` before any page script and `client_errors` intercepted in-page: **40
readings, 0 uncaught**, the logbook listing its 30 assets in every one.

**Banked** (`tools/bank_sl_walk.py`): H1 ×10 from the prover (both engines clean, the capability gate green), A3 ×10 and
AV1 ×10 from the MCP receipts, each AV1 receipt carrying its WebKit half as the named witness (no MCP drives WebKit; the
recorder now refuses a WebKit receipt that does not name its run). **30 of 30 CLOSED** by the ledger's own predicate.

**What the walk found, and why no page load could.** Production's policy granted `img-src 'self' data: https:` with no
`blob:`, and declared no `media-src` at all, so media inherited `default-src 'self'`. Both fire on a person's ACTION,
never at load, so the 40/40 matrix could not see them; a capability scan of what the code DOES with a URL it made did.
Measured in real Chromium and WebKit under the shipped header (an `img-src blob` and a `media-src` violation each), and
read from the live production response. What production did:
- **resume.html: every photo failed** with "Could not load image" (its compression `Image()` loads a blob: URL);
- marketplace and marketplace-seller: the listing preview broke until the upload returned;
- **every photo through `utils.js whCompressImage` (logbook fault photos) uploaded uncompressed**, its blob: load
  failing silently into the original-file fallback;
- latent: any storage or blob: audio (tts-speak, Piper, the voice journal; no production page plays one today).

**Fixed** (`c1192af4`, not pushed): `img-src` gains `blob:`, `media-src 'self' blob: <the Supabase host>`; `_headers`
brought back in line with vercel.json, including the `wss:` entry it never received. **The gate built for this class
had two blind spots:** `csp-covers-what-ships` audited `_headers`, the Cloudflare file Vercel never reads, and only
load-time hosts. It now audits vercel.json, fails on drift, and checks capabilities (a blob: rendered as an image needs
`img-src blob:`, a played audio a `media-src` naming its source); the pre-fix policy yields 10 findings, the fixed one 0.

**Recorded for later sub-layers, not failed here:** with indexedDB denied (Safari with storage blocked), five pages log
`offline-queue drain: <table>: The operation is insecure.` once per visit, caught and capped (L1 working; whether a
person can still save offline is AV2's question). The hive board renders more under failure (its not-live notice, AV3).

### §SL.2 Walk 2 — L1 on every page, S1 and S2 by refusal: the public funnel was dark, two write gaps were real, and the probes misread four things as leaks (2026-10-14)

**L1 found a dark half.** `client_errors` accepted inserts only from signed-in members (RLS) and the capture backbone
(`utils.js whLogError`) sent only through a Supabase client. So every anonymous visitor's error went nowhere: **all
119 public pages** (every learn guide, every calculator, about / feedback / privacy / terms load no `utils.js`), every
production page before sign-in, and two pages that load `utils.js` but never build a client (design-system, status).
Fixed in the platform's own pattern for anonymous telemetry (`analytics_events` already accepts anonymous inserts):
- migration `20261014000002`: an anonymous row may carry only the two uncaught contexts and **no** hive, name or account;
  proven through PostgREST as the anonymous role: the honest row lands (201); claiming a hive, a name or a free-form
  context is refused (401 ×3); an anonymous read returns nothing;
- `wh-error-capture.js`: the same net without `utils.js` or supabase-js, deduped, capped at 20 per load, pathname only;
  bootstrapped idempotently by `wh-i18n-lite.js` (synchronous, in `<head>`) and `wh-feedback-fab.js` (on every public
  page, lazy-loaded by `nav-hub.js` too), so it reaches all 119 pages and every future one with a 2-file change;
- `utils.js`: a backbone with no client hands its uncaught errors to the net (loading it once, queueing the error that
  triggered the load) instead of dropping them; the net stands down only where the backbone can actually SEND.
- the read half: `production-errors-read` (`tools/validate_production_error_groups.py`) fails while any (page, message)
  group in `production_error_groups.json` lacks a resolution: a fix a registered gate holds, not seen after the fix, or
  an open row. All 16 groups are answered today (the WebKit socket error by `a2f9a45f`; the landing page's null
  `#su-username` reads and `_tt` by code that no longer reaches them).

**The proof** (`tools/prove_error_capture_everywhere.mjs`, gate `error-capture-everywhere`): every page of the L1
roster, as its cast, in real WebKit and Chromium, an uncaught error AND an unhandled rejection thrown after start-up;
each must arrive with the page's own pathname, the engine in the user agent, and the person where there is one (an
anonymous row must carry none). One real anonymous write per engine lands in the table through the policy and is
removed after it is read. Teeth: the pre-change shared scripts (`b74b63a5`) capture nothing. **316 readings: WebKit 158 of 158, Chromium 158 of 158** (three Chromium readings re-taken after the no-client hand-off and a polling fix; the first run's problems are kept on them). **L1: 158 of 158 closed.**

**S1 by refusal, not by browser.** S1 and S2 were seeded as browser walks; a browser cannot show that a read was
refused, and the postgres MCP connects as the table owner (it bypasses RLS). Re-declared (59 rows, unwalked) to the
instrument the W4 S layer used: `tools/prove_w4_layer_s.py`, a member of ANOTHER hive on the authenticated path in a
rolled-back transaction must read zero of this hive's rows while the page's own member is served. Extending its gate
(`w4-layer-entitlement`) to the 35 S1 pages first read as eleven "leaks"; each was the instrument, read from the policy:
- a page reading a table AND its truth view made two `_fx_<name>` scratch tables in one session (the recipe now keeps
  colliding names apart; every other recipe is byte-identical);
- the fixture "member of exactly one hive" was Leandro Marquez, a marketplace platform admin whose policies read every
  hive's inquiries by design (platform admins are now excluded from the fixture);
- the marketplace and hailing directories are cross-hive by their own policies (`mkt_listings_read`: published OR mine;
  `mkt_sellers_read`: any signed-in user, profile columns only; `service_providers_read`: authenticated, true), and
  `marketplace_inquiries` is person-scoped, not hive-scoped; each is classified with its policy as the stated reason;
- community posts are public OR hive-private by one policy, so the probe now requires zero of a foreign hive's PRIVATE
  posts rather than zero of all posts.
`w4-layer-entitlement`: **PASS 389/389** (150 pages: 25 refuse a foreign hive, 125 have nothing to refuse). **S1: 35
of 35 closed.** No real cross-hive READ leak was found.

**S2 found two real WRITE gaps.** `tools/gen_write_authz_recipes.py --sl` now measures each S2 page's written tables from
its own source (the hand-kept list covered 11 pages), runs every write probe through one exception-safe function (a
refusal returns its SQLSTATE instead of aborting the rolled-back transaction), treats an append-only table (no UPDATE
policy, or no UPDATE grant: the audit logs) as refusal-only, and adds the WITH CHECK half: a member must not be able to
MOVE their own row into a hive they are not in. It did, twice: `marketplace_sellers` (founder-console, marketplace-admin,
marketplace-seller, platform-actions) and `resume_documents` (resume) checked ownership on write and never the claimed
hive, so anyone could publish a seller profile or a resume under any hive's name. **Fixed** by migration
`20261014000003` (the row's hive must be NULL or one of the author's active memberships, `user_hive_ids()`; 0 of 17
sellers and 0 of 5 resumes already violated it, so no one is stranded): **5 FAIL before, 0 after (19 pass, 5 write no
hive-scoped table)**. The recipes land in `tools/psql_probes/`, where `psql-probe-suite` re-executes them on every board
(194/194 hold, after one stale read recipe was removed and one pre-existing probe's word-match - `ILIKE
'%UPDATE%inventory_items%qty_on_hand%'` caught a dashboard that only READS stock - was tightened to an actual UPDATE
statement, its teeth checked). **S2: 24 of 24 closed.** Both migrations reach production on Ian's push (the runbook's
migration leg).

### §SL.3 Walk 3, part 1 — AU2 by a differential: seven pages decided from a role the device remembered (2026-10-14)

**The oracle.** One person, two states of one server fact. Leandro Marquez, supervisor of Baguio Textile Mills, was
demoted to `worker` on the LOCAL database (restored after) and read twice per page and per viewport - the honest device
role, then a false `supervisor` written to the page's own storage before it loaded - at a TRUE 390 and 1280 through the
chrome-devtools MCP. Any control only the false role shows is a page deciding from the device. Every fixed page was also
read the other way (server `supervisor`, device `worker`) to prove no supervisor is locked out, and the solo cast
(integrations) was walked as Jun Salvador (`junvanowner`, no hive).

**Found, fixed, re-walked identical at both widths:**

| page | what the false role got |
|---|---|
| alert-hub | Approve brief / Reject on the AMC brief; Ack / Resolve on the alerts |
| audit-log | the filters, the search and "Export filtered entries to CSV" (13 vs 23 controls at 390) |
| community | the Mod Queue and "Share publicly with all WorkHive teams"; at 1280 Pin / Delete / Make public / Flag on others' posts |
| integrations | the whole CMMS console (SAP PM / Maximo import, Live Sync, API keys) - and so did a hive-less solo owner with a leftover role |
| plant-connections | the plant console instead of the denial |
| index | the supervisor actions - first through the cached role, then through nav-hub's display mode DERIVED from it |
| analytics | the Supervisor view, and "Recompute risk" gated on the cache behind the Predictive phase the at-rest read never opens |

resume's context pill printed the cached role ("Plant · supervisor"): a display, fixed the same way. analytics-report's
only read fed a test whose two branches were both `'supervisor'`: removed.

**The fix, once:** `utils.js whReconcileHiveRole(db, hiveId?)` reads the membership row by `auth_uid`, writes the answer
back to `wh_hive_role` and `wh_hives`, drops a DERIVED (never a chosen) `wh_nav_mode`, and treats a role on a hive-less
device as a leftover only when the account holds no active membership. Each page starts it beside its own first reads
and awaits it before the first role-gated render, so it adds no round trip. Pages keep their `typeof` guard: a device
still holding an older cached `utils.js` falls back to today's behaviour instead of breaking.

**The lock:** `role-reconciled` (`tools/validate_role_reconciled.py`, Security): a page that reads the stored role and
compares it OR shows it must reconcile - through the helper, or through its own membership read on a page this walk
verified. Presence alone is not proof such a read runs: index's only one is its no-hive resolver, and the gate's first
version passed it. **15 of 15 pages reconcile; teeth: all 9 pre-fix pages flag.** Two instrument lessons inside it:
`accept="image/*"` opened a fake block comment that hid resume's role read (the stripper now ignores a `/*` glued to a
word or a quote), and `wh_nav_mode_src`, written by nav-hub through a variable the inventory could not see, is now a
registered key.

**Settled:** AU2 **18 of 18 closed**. BRH-F: **6 reproduced, fixed, gated and closed** (BRH148, 150, 151, 152, 154, 155;
resume's pill reproduced on demand by serving the pre-fix page under a temporary name, removed after) and **2 descoped
as refuted live** (BRH149 analytics-report: both branches identical; BRH153 marketplace-admin: the read is never compared
or shown, and the page's gate is the server's platform-admin check). No migration in this part; the nine page edits and
`utils.js` reach production on Ian's push.

**A cost, reported:** the frames this walk reads in do not receive the MCP's no-model stub (an initScript reaches the top
page only), and alert-hub's brief compose and analytics' phases call `analytics-orchestrator` on load - **21 real model
calls, about 98K tokens** (Groq and OpenRouter free tiers, 3 on Google Gemini) before the edge log showed it. From here a
page that calls a model on load is read by direct navigation under the stub; the Playwright walks avoid this with a
context-level route adding `x-wh-walk-no-model`, which the chrome-devtools MCP cannot do.

### §SL.3b Walk 3, part 2 — AU3: "mine" followed the name the device remembered (2026-10-14)

**The oracle.** Walked in the Playwright MCP (the rows' declared instrument; its context route put
`x-wh-walk-no-model` on every edge call, so no model was called). The same signed-in account read each page twice
per viewport: the device remembering its own display name, then another real person's (Bryan with Wilfredo
Malabanan's, a worker in his hive; Leandro with Christine Dizon's, a supervisor; Jun, a solo owner, with Miguel
Santos's). **The first oracle masked both names to one token, and that hid a swap**: a "(you)" moving from one
member's row to the other's reads as identical text. The final pass masks them apart (`<ME>` / `<OTHER>`), which is
what found presence, the assistant's greeting and three name chips.

**Found and fixed** (each re-walked identical at 390 and 1280):
- **The wide union.** Seven `_mineFilter()` copies (logbook, hive, pm-scheduler, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix,
  community) and five inline copies (assistant ×2, achievements, marketplace-seller, and the teammate lookups in hive and
  community) built `auth_uid = me OR worker_name = name`, so a row bound to ANOTHER account matched by name: Bryan's
  logbook listed Wilfredo's 2,140 bound entries as his own (4,417 vs 2,277). The name half now reaches only
  `auth_uid IS NULL` rows, the legacy rows it exists for: 2,277 either way.
- **Ownership compared by name.** pm-scheduler marked five of Wilfredo's assets "yours", listed them under Mine and
  offered Delete on them; community took Leandro's own posts and reactions for someone else's; logbook's asset
  permissions, team-view tag and realtime self-echo; achievements' "you". A page-local `_isMine(row)` asks the
  account; community asks the base table for its own post ids, because the posts view omits `auth_uid` on purpose
  (20260831000001).
- **Identity announced or shown from the cache.** Presence on hive and community joined the channel AS the remembered
  person (teammates would see them online, "(you)" on the wrong row); the assistant greeted "Hi Wilfredo!" and read
  the grounding it calls "your job records" (logbook, schedule, badges, voice journal) by that name; index, hive and
  pm-scheduler chips, skillmatrix's header, and resume's CV prefill. These now ask the account before presence or
  the first paint, and `utils.js` `_whAnnounceName` repaints `#nav-worker` / `[data-wh-worker-name]` and announces
  `wh-identity-changed` whenever `restoreIdentityFromSession` corrects the cache.
- **An admin check by name.** marketplace-admin asked the allowlist for the remembered name; its read policy returns
  only the caller's own row, so no one could be elevated, but a real admin with a changed name was refused. It
  defers to `isPlatformAdmin(db)`, which asks with the server's names for the account.

**The lock:** `ownership-by-account` (`tools/validate_ownership_by_account.py`, Security): no wide union in either
form, and no ownership comparison against `WORKER_NAME` unless the line marks a deliberate fallback
(`name-compare-allow`). 88 pages and shared scripts pass; teeth: 46 sites in the 10 pre-fix pages.

**Settled:** AU3 **31 of 31 closed**. Postgres witness: across the walk, the only rows written under a false name are
143 `analytics_events` page views under the walker's own account. Every founder rollup counts
`COALESCE(auth_uid, worker_name)`, so none is miscounted. CLOSED 12,332 of 16,664.

### §SL.4 Walk 4 — S3, S4, S5, CA2, H2, CI1, CI4 and F5: one CSP for every page was a policy for none, a stored id could run script in the logbook, and 119 pages had no cache header where they are served (2026-10-15)

**S3, what was found.** vercel.json shipped one Content-Security-Policy for every page: the union of every origin any
page needs.
- The landing page named the chart library only analytics loads. Every calculator named the PDF service only
  engineering-design calls.
- `img-src https:` named every origin on the internet. The product's images come from four places: 'self', data:,
  blob: and the project's own storage. No code, seeder or stored listing has ever pointed an image anywhere else.
  Before 2026-05-02 no UI wrote `image_url`; since then only the storage upload has.
- `connect-src` still named the assistant Cloudflare Worker, five months after it was decommissioned. It survives
  only as a tombstone constant in voice-handler.js, and `validate_no_ai_gateway_bypass` forbids calling it.
- `script-src` named fonts.googleapis.com, which serves no page a script.

**S3, the structure built.**
- **`tools/build_csp_profiles.py` (gate `csp-exact-profiles`).** It generates each page's policy from its own code: its
  HTML plus every local script it loads, transitively. `sw.js` is excluded, since a service worker is not page code.
  - A host is kept only in the directive the code loads it through: a `<script src>` or `.js` URL, a stylesheet, an
    API base or fetch, and the socket form only where the product's own code opens a channel. Bundled supabase-js
    always carries the realtime client, so vendor code is not read for that.
  - A library's dependents follow it: gtag reports to Analytics' collectors, a Google Fonts sheet loads its faces from
    gstatic, and Turnstile draws its challenge in a frame.
  - The base rule is the universe the generator narrows. It never invents an origin.
  - Pages with one policy share one rule, written after every other rule so it wins. Sources are chunked under
    Vercel's length cap: 60 calculators × 3 request paths had run to 8,135 characters.
  - **156 served pages, 10 policies.** The base rule loses the dead worker, the script-src fonts host and the wildcard.
    `_headers`, the documented intent, matches it.
- **Every gate that read "the" CSP now reads each page's own.** `csp-covers-what-ships` took the first CSP in
  vercel.json, which is now only the fallback. It now also audits each of the 156 pages' code against the policy its
  path resolves to. The H1 prover serves each page its own policy.
- **One matcher.** `serve_vercel_headers.headers_for()` is shared by the server, `--resolve`, the covers gate, the H1
  prover and the S3 prover.
- **`tools/prove_csp_exact.mjs` (gate `csp-exact`).** A `--measure` run read 154 pages in Chromium, as each page's
  cast under the policy the deploy resolves for its path: 0 violations, and every origin measured live was already in
  the code read. The `--verdict` run judges two things against the policy each page is served:
  - COVERS: 0 violations, and every origin loaded is named;
  - NOTHING MORE: every origin named has a basis (loaded live, or a named file of the page's code loads it that way),
    and there is no scheme wildcard.
  - Teeth: under `a8ffe363`'s site-wide policy every page must fail NOTHING MORE.
  - **154/154 pages clean**, with every origin backed by a basis. Teeth: under `a8ffe363`'s site-wide policy all 154 pages name origins with no basis.

**CA2 + H2, what was found.** The 119 public directory pages are linked as `/learn/x/` and served at `/learn/x`
(trailingSlash false). No vercel.json rule matched that path. The `/(.*).html` rule never sees it, so their
freshness rested on a platform default the config never stated. It now does: `/(learn|tools)/:slug` and
`/(about|feedback|learn|privacy-policy|terms-of-service)` carry the HTML rule, mirrored in `_headers`.

**CA2 + H2, the structure built.** `tools/prove_cache_contract.py` (gate `cache-contract`, runs in `--fast`) walks
every page over HTTP against the local edge substitute, at every path a person reaches it by. It checks every asset
the page loads (its script closure, stylesheets, images) and `sw.js`:
- HTML is max-age=0 and must-revalidate;
- scripts and styles are the same, plus an ETag or Last-Modified validator;
- images are cached a year, immutable;
- `sw.js` is no-store;
- and the server sends exactly what vercel.json says.

"Locally alike" means that substitute. The dev seeder on :5000 is a rewriting test proxy that answers no-store, which
is fresher than every class, and nobody is served from it. Its first run caught three directory pages the first
hand-written rule had missed. Teeth: under `a8ffe363`'s vercel.json 119/119 directory pages fail, and with scripts
cached an hour (the 2026-10-14 incident) 155/155 pages fail.

**And a gate that had been red since the three pages were deleted.** `prove_deploy_headers.py` still read six
descoped rows whose pages were deleted on Ian's word, and failed on their 404s. It skips descoped rows now (33/33). This
is the same class `journey-paths` learned in §SL.


**CI1, a gate holds each page's contract, and proves it on that page.** A gate that reads every page but is blind to one
page's shape holds nothing there. `tools/prove_page_gate_teeth.py` (gate `page-gate-teeth`) breaks a temporary copy of
each page and runs two registered gates' own detectors on it:
- `csp-covers-what-ships` must redden on a script from an origin the page's own resolved policy does not name;
- `scripts-parse` must redden on an inline script that does not parse;
- and both must read the page clean as it is.

**155/155**, closed.

**CI4, every page in every registry its class needs.** `tools/prove_page_registries.py` (gate `page-registries`) reads
each registry from its own source:
- every page: the SL classes, the design ratchet's scope, its own generated CSP rule, the cache contract's roster;
- production and public pages: the served roster;
- public pages: `sitemap.xml`;
- production pages: the hub, as offered, parented, or linked from an offered page;
- founder pages: `FOUNDER_PAGES`.

The reverse holds too: no sitemap entry, hub href, shell page or founder name points at nothing. **The finding:** the
five founder pages were outside the design ratchet. Its scope now reads them, and the floor was re-measured with the
reason recorded (0 → 10). Teeth: a page taken out of its class's registry, and a planted dangling sitemap entry, are
each caught. **155/155**, closed.

**S5, no secret in anything a browser receives.** `tools/prove_no_secret_served.mjs` (gate `no-secret-served`) loads
each page as its cast and reads every response body it gets: the HTML, every script and stylesheet, and every
database and edge answer. It also reads the page's localStorage and sessionStorage. Three things are checked:
- the six secret VALUES `.env` holds, literally (reported by name, never printed);
- any JWT whose role is not `anon` or `authenticated`;
- seven key shapes (`sb_secret_`, `sk-`, `gsk_`, `AIza`, `ghp_`, `xox?-`, a PEM private-key block).

**155/155 pages receive none.** Teeth: logbook served a planted service_role-shaped token and a real `.env` value has
both caught.

**K, the founder findings the wider scope surfaced (BRH318–322).** founder-console and marketplace-admin are production
pages in the bug-hunt inventory, so their five pairs became K rows:
- founder-console's platform-checks dot blinked forever under a coloured glow, and said its state by colour alone. It
  now holds still, names the state in words through the same branches that pick the colour, and is neutral grey, not
  green, when nothing was read. It starts in its checking state, so colour and name agree from the first paint.
- The RAG dots lost their glow.
- A 38-character uppercase hero label became the short label its siblings are.
- marketplace-admin's toast eases out without the 0.56 overshoot.

The other four findings are on the two internal observability dashboards, which Ian scoped out of fix rows; the
ratchet holds them. Floor **10 → 4**. Walked through the MCP browser at 390 and 1280, as Bryan Garcia (the rows' cast, who meets each page's no-access gate) and as Leandro Marquez (a platform admin, admitted to the retired overlay). The probes read the page's own served CSS and computed styles. The first probe read the shared chrome's glows and the detector-excluded headings as this page's findings and was narrowed to the finding's own scope.

**S4, escaping proven by poisoning, and a stored-XSS hole it found.** `tools/prove_stored_text_escaped.mjs` (gate
`stored-text-escaped`) loads each S4 page as its cast. Every database read (tables and rpc) is answered with its stored
text carrying `<img src=x data-wh-xss onerror=…>`, and every table write is held so the poison never reaches the
database. The page must show the payload as text: no handler runs and no payload element exists.
- **Its first run found a real hole in logbook.** Every entry card drew `onclick="openModal('${e.id}')"` raw.
  `logbook.id` is a TEXT column the client writes (`pm-<time><random>`), with no constraint on its content. So any
  active member of a hive could store an id that closes the attribute and adds `autofocus onfocus=`, run for every
  colleague who opens the logbook. The walk saw the handler run four times.
- **The fix, at three levels.**
  - All four sites pass the id through `escJsAttr`. `escHtml` is not enough inside an attribute, because the browser
    decodes the entity before the JS runs.
  - A new gate, `handler-values-escaped`, holds every `${…}` in every inline handler to `escJsAttr`. That was 155
    sites in 10 files, including `e(...)`-wrapped values. The 2026-07-10 detector matched only the `escHtml(`
    spelling.
  - Migration `20261015000001` adds CHECK `logbook_id_is_a_token`, NOT VALID so it is safe on unmeasured production
    rows. It was applied locally, refuses a crafted id and admits a real one.
- **The instrument was taught three times, each from a reading it got wrong.**
  - Vacuity: a page that received free text and drew none fails as "not exercised". A page whose reads carry no free
    text records that as its reading.
  - `textContent`, not `innerText`: text in a collapsed panel was rendered, just not visible.
  - Identity: poisoning the reader's own name, hive and admin grant stopped the founder pages before they drew. Now
    the reader's own row stays clean while teammates' names, which other people wrote, are poisoned. The admin grant
    is passed through untouched, since the page only tests it.
  - Pages reached by a deep link or a tab are opened that way: the seller profile from its seller, integrations'
    Live Sync and API tabs.
- **Result: 36/36 pages show every poisoned value as text.** Teeth: logbook served a `utils.js` whose `escHtml`
  returns its input unchanged runs the payload 141 times.

**F5, first slices (built from the tokens, nothing the detector flags).**
- **The design ratchet reads 0 on every page.** The two observability dashboards' last four findings are fixed.
  llm-observability's six KPI labels were `<h3>`: labels, not headings. They made the outline jump h1 → h3 and sat at
  body size. They are labels now, with the same look. agentic-rag's hive-gate title is the gate's `<h2>`, and each
  page's type scale now climbs 1.25 from body. Floor **4 → 0**.
- **The public pages' corners are on DESIGN.md's radius scale, by role, not by nearest number.** 765 rogue radii on
  the 119 learn, calculator and directory pages:
  - section cards (`.toc`, `.faq-item`, `.author-card`, prose sections) go 14px → 16px;
  - pills go 100px → 999px;
  - buttons and the skip link's corner go 10px → 8px;
  - inline code and the priority chips go 6px → 8px.

  This was matched rule by rule on the selector. It also went into the three generators that write these pages and
  into the chrome fixers and `wayfinding.js`, so a regenerated page keeps it. The public pages now hold **0** rogue
  radii.
- **The tokens gate counted a spelling.** `.5rem` and `.75rem` are the legal 0.5rem and 0.75rem; it normalizes now.
  Its rogue-radius floor was 217 against a baseline of 216. K's watermark had added a 13px corner that
  design-tokens, never run after that CSS edit, did not catch. The watermark now takes the card's own corner
  (`inherit`), and the floor is **215**.
- **Then every page.** The public pages' 2,523 brand colours written in CSS became token references,
  `var(--wh-*, #hex)` (those pages load no `tokens.css`, so the fallback paints). SVG attributes, meta theme-color and
  canvas colours stay literal. The 35 root app pages' 208 off-scale corners went onto the scale by role:
  - cards 12px, and hero, gate and section cards 16px;
  - controls, chips and focus rings 8px;
  - thin bars, tracks and handles 999px;
  - sheets `16px 16px 0 0`, with a single-corner property getting one value;
  - chat bubbles keep an 8px tail corner;
  - search highlights, mini calendar cells and spark bars square (0), the closest the scale has to their 2–3px.
  The mapping read 126 CSS rules by selector, 74 inline corners by what their style says the element is, and 13
  JS-built styles (notices, toasts, buttons) by hand. The root pages' 25 bare brand hex values became token
  references. **page-craft 155/155 at 0**; the design-tokens floors fell 216 → 17 corners and 143 → 141 hex across
  the root files. Two scanner misreads were fixed on the way, in the gate and the prover alike: an inline value
  read past its attribute's closing quote (`999px"></div>`), and `.5rem` was counted as off the scale.

**CI3 (held means measured).** The phone-fit lens and the live axe scan now read the program's pages: a public page
signed out, as its visitor, and each page's first measurement its floor.
- **Phone fit at 390: 155/155 fit, 0 issues.** The first full run read 153. The three retired founder pages

  overlay reads 6 findings, and the clean overlay reads 0. A `--pages` re-read now merges into the full run's record,
  each merged page stamped with its own time.
- **axe at 390: 155/155 scanned.** It found one defect class: `link-in-text-block` on 19 learn articles. The editorial
  e-mail link in the footer was told apart from its sentence by colour alone, #5FCCE8 on white/60 grey at 1.21:1
  against the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.1 asks of a colour-only link. The link is now underlined, on all 56 copies and in the

**F2 and F3 instruments.**
- **F2 (`prove_page_fit.py`, gate `page-fit`)** reads the phone-fit lens's own record at 320, 390 and 1280; a row
  closes at 0 on all three. A 1280 reading had been taken in a mobile, touch context, which is a tablet emulation no
  desktop reader sees. A context under 768 wide is now a phone; anything wider is a desktop with no touch and DPR 1.
  New gates: `phone-fit-320` and `phone-fit-1280`, over the whole roster with per-page floors per axis.
- **F3 (`prove_page_reachable.mjs`, gate `page-reachable`)** reads four things, each from the instrument that owns it:
  - **named:** axe-core's own accessible-name rules, run in the page at 1280;
  - **reached:** a REAL Tab walk at 1280 until focus comes back round. A composite widget's roving members (radio
    group, tablist, menu, listbox) count when one of them is reached. A repainted control is matched by its place and
    name, so a live poll cannot fake an unreachable one;
  - **visible focus:** each focused control's computed look against its look at rest, and its parent's for a
    `:focus-within` ring;
  - **44px target:** measured at 390 on a phone context. A link inline in a sentence is exempt under WCAG 2.5.5, and
    a checkbox is measured together with its label.

  Teeth run every time in the same contexts: a planted unnamed icon button, an invisible focus, a 20px target and a
  `tabindex="-1"` link must each be caught, and their clean twin must read 0. Per-page floors live in
  `page_reach_baseline.json`.

  The trial runs fixed three misreads in the instrument before the full sweep:
  - **A closed form is not a hidden input.** A control under `display:none` has a 0×0 box, which the
    visually-hidden test read as an sr-only input. Hive's closed create/join forms and two closed sheets read as
    12 controls "never reached". A control must now be rendered first.
  - **A date input is three tab stops.** Its month, day and year keep focus on the same element, and the walk read
    the repeat as coming back round. It stopped at logbook's date filter with 5 controls behind it.
  - **A withdrawn control is not a missed one.** `learn-link.js` folds the guide chip after 8 s or the first
    scroll and hides its dismiss button; Enter on the folded chip brings it back. The walk's own focus-scrolling
    folds it. Unreached now means still rendered when the walk ends.

  The trial also found a real defect. The 60 calculator pages wrote their FAQ as `<details class="faq">`, while the
  shell they share with the learn articles styles only `.faq-item`. So every question was a bare browser-default
  summary, 30px tall at 390. The markup now matches the shell, in the generator and the live pages: 183 questions
  are now 68–92px cards.

**F3 full sweep: 149/155 at the first read, then 155/155.** Two more instrument corrections and three page fixes:
- **The press budget follows the page.** Community loads more posts as focus scrolls the feed, so its tab order outgrew
  the 72 controls counted at rest. The budget fixed from that count ran out before the controls after the feed (load
  more, the FAQ, the post button). It is now re-counted from the live tab stops every 40 presses, with a cap of 900.
- **A scroll region is reached, not tapped.** Community's members-online strip is `role="region" tabindex="0"` so a
  keyboard can scroll it. WCAG 2.5.5 sizes what a pointer activates, so the 44px check now reads activatable controls
  only.
- **19 learn articles** came from `scaffold_article.py`, which pads the FAQ *card* and not the question. A one-line
  question was a 30px target with dead padding around it. The padding moved onto the summary, in the pages and the
  scaffold, so the whole card row is the target and the look is unchanged.
- **design-system's filter-chip specimen** was a `<span role="button">` with no tabindex, which the keyboard could not
  reach, beside a chip with no role. Every page that ships chips uses `<button type="button" aria-pressed>`, so the
  specimen is now two real toggle buttons.

Both corrections only widen what the walk reads, so the 149 pages read clean under the stricter version still hold.
`page_reach_baseline.json` holds no floor.

**CI2 and H4 instruments.**
- **CI2 (`prove_page_journeys.py`, gate `page-journeys`)** reads two walks, each in Chromium AND WebKit:
  - **Public pages:** `prove_public_journeys.mjs` (gate `public-journeys`) walks the reader's job signed out: arrive and
    read (200, an `<h1>`, a readable `<main>`), a calculator's worked example, the first FAQ answer, and the onward
    link *clicked* to a live surface. Teeth: a page with no `<h1>`, an empty `<main>` and a link to a missing page.
  - **App pages:** `live_page_journeys.mjs` registered jobs-to-be-done. It gained `--engine webkit` (gate
    `live-page-journeys-webkit`), whose artifacts take a `.webkit` suffix so the Chromium board and its ratchet are
    never written.

  12 of the 36 app pages had no registered journey. **K7** adds one each:
  - public-feed (a visitor reads the public posts; the count must match the database);
  - the seller profile (the listing count must match the database);
  - PH intelligence (a report, or the no-report state, as the database says);
  - the report sender (open the add-recipient sheet and cancel);
  - shift-brain (a brief, or the "nothing published yet" state);
  - status (read the board and refresh it);
  - design-system (press a chip specimen);
  - Platform Actions (the feedback count must match the database);
  - the four retired consoles: the "has moved" card and its own in-app link.
- **H4 (`prove_rollout.mjs`, gate `rollout`)** builds a returning device for real. `serve_vercel_headers.py` gained
  `--ref`, which serves every file as it was at a commit with that commit's own `vercel.json`, and `--local-supabase`.
  - A fresh profile visits each page while the origin serves the previous build: the newest commit whose
    `CACHE_NAME` differs from the working tree's. The old worker installs and keeps its copies.
  - The same origin then serves the working tree.
  - Visit 1 must run one build, never new HTML on old scripts. Visit 2 must run the new one. Only the new cache may
    remain.
  - Teeth: the new page with one shared script forced to its old bytes is caught as mixed.

  **Measured first (v528 → v529): 5/67.** 62 pages ran half new and half old on the first visit after a deploy:
  - App pages: the new HTML and `utils.js` (network-first) beside the old worker's precached `offline-queue.js`,
    `connectivity-widget.js` and `session-timeout.js` (cache-first).
  - Learn articles: last week's copy (cache-first) beside a new `wh-ga4.js`.

  Every device had moved by visit 2. The old worker's code answers visit 1, so `sw.js` alone cannot fix it, and
  `nav-hub.js`'s "a new version is ready" notice assumed a *waiting* worker while `sw.js` calls `skipWaiting()` and
  `clients.claim()`. The fix has two halves:
  - **`sw.js`:** every navigation, learn and tools included, and every same-origin script and stylesheet, precached or
    not, is network-first with a kept copy. `vercel.json` already sends `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so an unchanged
    file costs a 304, and the precache is the offline copy.
  - **`utils.js` and `wh-i18n-lite.js`:** the scripts the old worker fetches from the network. When the worker
    changes under a page a worker was already serving, the page reloads once onto the new build, unless the person
    has touched it. It never loops, guarded per page for a minute.

  Trial on three pages that were mixed: 3/3, each ending visit 1 on the new build after one reload; achievements and
  project-report show two because the anonymous device also passes through the sign-in redirect.

  **Full run: 67/67, H4 banked 67/67.** The service-worker gates rerun on the change found one more defect, an old
  one: `sw-navigation-fallback` read **0/11** (3/11 at HEAD). A cached response reached through a redirect cannot
  answer a navigation (its redirect mode is manual), and the precached `/offline-fallback.html` is, locally, the target
  of a redirect to `/workhive/`. So every offline navigation read `net::ERR_FAILED` instead of "Your connection
  dropped". Any cached answer handed to a navigation is now re-wrapped as a plain response. The 11th page,
  platform-actions, sat on "Checking access…" for as long as the device stayed offline (the admin check waits on an
  unreachable server). It now says it needs a connection and tries again on reconnect. **11/11, and all 19
  service-worker gates pass.**

  Instrument corrections on the way:
  - Public pages register no worker; `nav-hub.js` on app pages does. So the device opens the home page first, and
    `serviceWorker.ready` gets a ceiling.
  - The teeth must plant a script the probe page actually loads.
  - The prover serves on its own port, 5079. The deploy-headers and cache-contract gates serve the working tree on
    5077.

**The F5 walk's visual check found one more.** The avatar's level pill, raised to 12px on 2026-09-19 with
`line-height:1.5`, was 24px tall. Hung 8px below a 32px avatar, it covered three quarters of the circle, the initials
included: a 32×24 "60" over "BG" on every community post. It now uses `line-height:1.1` and no vertical padding and
hangs 11px, in the shared rule in `utils.js`. Measured live, it overlaps the initials by 0px at 32, 44, 52 and 72px
avatars.

**CI2, the first boards.**
- **Chromium board: 117/121 live.** Four journeys read gap, and three are oracles an intended product change made

  - **AR2's** report did not finish compiling in the long run, while AR1 compiled it. It is re-run alone.
- **Public journeys.** The first run lost every reading when WebKit's web process died under a calculator page:
  every await hung, and the prover wrote only at the end. Each walk now has a 90 s ceiling (recorded as a problem,
  never a pass), and results are written after every page.
- **The journey runner.** It gained per-journey (150 s) and per-critic (120 s) ceilings that it reports as a crashed
  target, which its recycle-and-retry already handles. A context close that hangs gives up after 10 s.
- **The feedback page's job is here, not onward.** Its `<main>` is a public roadmap a reader filters, so the public
  journey presses a filter chip there instead of following a link.

**The MCP walks ran under the service worker and could not see what they measured (2026-10-16).** The MCP browser's
default context is controlled by `sw.js`, and a `page.route()` never sees a request a service worker makes: a feedback
page that reads `platform_feedback` showed 0 REST requests to the route. So the F1 walk could not induce a list state,
and the AV1 and A3 walks could not see a `client_errors` insert. Every MCP walk now opens its own context with
service workers blocked (the prover harness's setting). AV1 was re-walked and re-banked under it, with teeth: a
planted uncaught error and a planted rejection were each seen as an insert.

**F1, each list's empty, error and loading state (62 rows).** The walk induced each list read in turn - answered empty,
answered 500, held 9 s and read at 1.5 s - at 390 and 1280. Its instrument grew six times before its readings could be
trusted:
- **Read by wording, not only by class.** "Could not load the roadmap right now. Try again" in a plain div read as
  silent to the class selectors.
- **Lists arrive by RPC and edge function.** The worker home reads `get_hive_dashboard` and analytics reads the
  analytics orchestrator; the old keep-pattern skipped every rpc named "hive" and never touched `/functions/v1`. In the
  empty state an object answer is hollowed the way an empty hive's would be: arrays emptied, counts zeroed, a nested
  record (the dashboard's `signature_alert`) nulled.
- **HEAD counts are reads** (the assistant's record counts). The shared chrome's own reads (follow-ups, unread counts)
  are not the page's lists.
- **A list behind the maturity gate.** No local hive is past Stair 1, so ai-quality, hive, alert-hub and ph-intelligence
  answer their one readiness read as the page's stair. plant-connections and integrations are walked as a supervisor;
  their lists are supervisor-only.

What it found and fixed:
- **The shared skeleton said nothing.** `whListSkeleton` / `whCardSkeleton` drew grey bars in an `aria-live` region
  with no text. They now take the list's name and caption the wait ("Loading your logbook entries…"), at all 42
  call sites. Gate `skeleton-labelled` fails a call that names neither a list nor `false`.
- **Waits that named the wrong thing, or nothing:**
  - Platform Actions kept "Checking access…" through its queue fetch.
  - The assistant's opening wait said "Thinking…" while it counted records.
  - The worker home's tile reserve was a blank band.
  - project-report's project chooser appeared only after its read.
  - skillmatrix's static skeleton had no words.
- **Empty states with no way on.** Community's leaderboard said "No activity yet." (its own comment promised the
  invitation); now it says who is missing and offers Write a post. plant-connections' CMMS tile said "No CMMS systems
  linked yet"; now it links to Integrations. skillmatrix's first run now says "No skill matrix yet."
- **Two retired pages still loaded.** llm-observability read `ai_cost_log` and agentic-rag-observability read
  `agentic_rag_traces` behind their "has moved" overlays. Both now return at the overlay, as founder-console and
  marketplace-admin already did.
- **The recorder learned that a held load is sparse by design.** Platform Actions' whole page is 99 characters while
  its queues fill. A `loading` step that names its wait and kept the person now arrives; any other thin step still
  fails.

**F4, plain words and honest labels (155 rows).**
- **119 domain acronyms with no gloss on 52 pages.** The live reader found MTBF, CMMS, LOTO, OEE, KPI and others with
  nothing on the page saying what they stand for, mostly in learn articles. The glossary gate had accepted a term
  taught somewhere in the learn cluster.
  - `tools/gloss_first_use.py` glosses each term at its first use in prose ("MTBF (mean time between failures)"), or
    with an `<abbr title>` where it appears only in a label, on all static pages.
  - `whAbbr()` in `utils.js` does the same for rendered text: community and public-feed posts, report names, the
    design-system guides.
  - Gate `jargon-glossed` holds both, and fails if the two registries drift apart.
- **Platform words, rewritten.** "pre-staging" and "deferred" were rewritten in five articles. The assistant's starter
  question now asks which asset "breaks down most often".
- **One basis-less figure.** project-manager's cards read "active 25%"; they now say "25% done". The other flagged
  figures were cleared by what the walk recorded with them: a column header on a page stating its window, a formula
  on the card, a worked example's RESULT table, or a denominator in the sentence.
- **The oracle now accepts "lockout".** LOTO's oracle accepts the OSHA spelling "lockout", in the shared prover too.

**C1, the hive's day and not the device's (25 rows), read as a differential.** Each page was opened twice at the same
pinned instant, 2026-10-16T02:00Z, which is Friday 10:00 in Manila and Thursday 22:00 in New York. One device clock was
Manila and the other New York, so a page dated by the hive's day reads and asks the same on both.
- **The two devices were made to differ only in their clock.**
  - Both answer the consent card the same way.
  - The page's clock-skew check is answered at the pinned instant.
  - Both are signed in, and each loads the page once unmeasured, before either is read. New York's sign-in had written a
    "new device" audit entry after Manila read the log.
  - The judge masks per-device chrome and treats a pure reordering, or a live latency number, as no difference.
- **It found three device-clock shapes the static gate did not count.**
  - alert-hub's brief read "composed live 10:00 AM" in Manila and "10:00 PM" in New York: `toLocaleTimeString` with no
    zone, 12 sites.
  - Platform Actions' queues read "7/29/2026, AM" against "7/28/2026, PM": `new Date(…).toLocaleString` with no zone,
    9 sites.
  - All 21 now use the hive's clock. `device-clock-day` gained P5 (time) and P6 (date-time), each holding 0.

**CA3, the old shared script heals (34 rows).** This uses `prove_skew_heal.mjs`'s method through the MCP browser. With
the real utils.js the page loads once with no refetch. With yesterday's copy, where the page's own guarded functions are
undefined, it refetches past the cache, reloads once and ends with every function present.
- **The heal roster had borrowed LX's "production" list.** It left out design-system, status and the two retired
  observability pages, and each of them guards utils.js functions. design-system's new `whAbbr` would have been skipped in
  silence. The roster is now the production list plus every root page on the SL roster, so 35 pages heal.
- **Teeth.** design-system and status as committed at b79380df: one load, no refetch, every guarded function still missing.

**CA1, the shell is held under the current version and replaced on the next deploy (37 rows).** Each row walks two devices
with the worker allowed, both installed from the home page. The first is on the current build: the page's whole shell (its
document and every same-origin script and stylesheet) is held in the cache named by sw.js's live `CACHE_NAME`, at 390 and
1280. The second installs the previous build (sw.js served once at registration, its `CACHE_NAME` renamed `-prev`). The
browser's own update check then fetches the real sw.js, which is new bytes at the same URL, exactly a deploy. The device
held `-prev`, then `-prev` was gone and the whole shell was held under the current name. All 37 pass on v534.
- **The first instrument walked a deploy that never happened.** It rewrote the UPDATE fetch to `-next`, but a
  registration's update check never reaches `context.route` (only the registration fetch does). The device got identical
  bytes, no worker installed, and 13 rows read 0/N. Measured: one routed fetch, `update()` installing nothing, caches
  unchanged for 20 s. Hence the two-device model.
- **A page registered the worker a second time.** report-sender.html still called `register('/sw.js')` beside nav-hub.js's
  central, derived-root registration (T44). In production that is the same worker. Under the local `/workhive/` prefix it is
  a second registration at another URL and scope, and on the walk its activate deleted the first one's cache. The call is
  gone (sw v534), and `pwa-sw-central-register` now refuses a literal `register()` path in every shipped page and script
  (teeth on report-sender as shipped in 683ecea5). Before this it read only nav-hub.js.
- **A worker whose script Playwright fulfilled could not reach the local stack.** On the current-build device the two
  retired observability pages read 0 characters: their admin check (`isPlatformAdmin`) never resolved with the sw.js route
  in place, and resolved true without it. Only the previous-build device routes sw.js now; the current-build device
  installs from the network.
- **Found on the way, in production:** the worker answered every page's Poppins stylesheet with 503 (sw.js's own CSP named
  no font host), and twelve learn figures were a 404 (trailingSlash:false + bare sources). Both fixed and deployed on
  2026-10-16, with gates `sw-proxy-within-csp` and `deploy-payload` rule 4.

**CA4, a page offline says whether it is the kept copy or the fallback (127 rows).** Each row walks two devices with the
worker allowed and installed from the home page. On the first, the page is opened once online, then the network is cut
and the page opened again. It must render itself and say it is the copy kept from a visit. On the second, the page was
never opened, and the offline fallback must say the page is not available offline yet. All 127 pass at 390 and 1280.
- **The kept copy said nothing.** The fallback was always clear. A learn article and a calculator answered from the kept
  copy rendered in full with no sign the network was gone, that it was a saved copy, or how old it was. The logbook
  said "you are offline" four ways and never that the page itself was the last visit's copy. Only the worker knows it
  answered from the kept copy. sw.js now hands a failed navigation's cached copy through `_keptNav`, which marks the HTML
  (`<meta name="wh-kept-copy">` with the cached response's own Date) and adds the precached `/offline-banner.js` where it
  is missing. The bar says "You are offline. This is the copy of this page saved on this device on <date, Philippine
  time> - it may be out of date." Gate `kept-copy-says-so`.
- **Offline is not "no".** On the kept copies, Shift Brain sent a signed-in supervisor to the sign-in page: `getUser()`
  offline answers no user plus an `AuthRetryableFetchError`, and the page read that as a dead session. Every admin page
  showed the founder a blank screen for about 10 s and then "Founder access only" / "Platform Admins Only", because
  `isPlatformAdmin()` answered false when its reads failed. `whPlatformAdminAnswer()` now keeps 'yes' / 'no' /
  'unreachable' apart (`isPlatformAdmin` stays `=== 'yes'`, fail-closed). Five admin gates keep the page closed offline
  and say "You're offline. <page> needs a connection to check your access", then reload on reconnect. Shift Brain takes
  the device's own session when the server cannot be reached. Gate `offline-is-not-no`.
- **Instrument.** The walk's status list kept the first four status elements, and the logbook's bar was the fifth, so
  the walk now reads the bar and the mark directly. utils.js changed mid-wave, so the 36 signed-in rows were re-walked on
  v536. The 91 public pages load no utils.js and their evidence stands.

**H3, every page installs and opens as the app (93 rows).** Each row is walked as its cast on the local edge substitute
(production paths and vercel.json's headers, pages pointed at the local stack), at 390 and 1280. Chromium's own
installability check reports no error on the page itself. The manifest answers 200 with a name and display standalone.
Its start_url is in scope and answers 200. The 192 and 512 icons answer as images, and the worker controls the page.
93/93.
- **The edge substitute was pointing the pages at production.** `--local-supabase` only widened the CSP, and the pages
  still named the production Supabase URL and key. Starting this walk, the cast's sign-in POSTed the test account to
  production's login function (400, no account, nothing written). `--local-stack` now rewrites the URL and key in served
  HTML and JS, from the local tester's own constants. `--local-supabase` keeps its meaning because the rollout prover
  compares served bytes to files.
- **The browser's verdict was "in-incognito" for every page.** Every context `browser.newContext()` makes is
  non-persistent, and Chromium's check stops there. The verdict is now read in the MCP browser's persistent context,
  as the cast (its session loaded, the final URL recorded, the identity cleared after). Teeth: `offline-fallback.html`,
  which links no manifest, reports `no-manifest`, while the about page reports none.

**D2, whose rows a page shows is decided by the account, never by a display name (25 rows).** AU3's oracle on D2's
roster: the same signed-in account reads each page twice per viewport, first with the device remembering its own name,
then another real person's (AU3's pairs, else a hive-mate). The reads are compared with the names masked apart
(`<ME>` / `<OTHER>`), text and controls. All 25 are identical at 390 and 1280, and every page that keeps the cache
corrects it to the account. founder-console and platform-actions leave the remembered name in place but never show it.
- **Teeth.** logbook.html as served at `e8e02917^`, before AU3's fix: Bryan with Wilfredo's name remembered differs by 8
  lines and 5 controls.
- **Instrument.** The first D2 call hung for the MCP's full 30 minutes on an unbounded `page.evaluate` with the host at
  0.28 GB free, and wedged the MCP until Playwright's own Chrome processes were stopped. The walker's reads are now
  bounded at 25 s, and a timed-out read fails the row.

**D1, every figure says where it came from (99 rows) - measured, not yet built; a design choice for Ian.** Learn
articles state their sources and date; calculators carry the "formula-only" chip. The app pages show figures in
sections with no chip: analytics has 118 figures in six metric sections under one chip, and inventory's tiles, the PM
scheduler's three counters and Asset Hub's figures have none. The lineage roadmap's per-figure "where did this come
from?" reveal (`display_provenance.json`, 58 figures on 18 pages) never shipped. The choice is one chip per figure
section, which goes against "silence is golden" status chrome, or a per-figure tap-to-reveal built from the
provenance map.

**Ian's decisions, 2026-10-16 (asked, answered):**
- **D1: per-figure reveal.** The page stays quiet; tapping a figure (or a small info control) reveals its source and the
  view it reads, built from `display_provenance.json`. Not a chip per section.
- **D3: 30-day recoverable deletes.** A delete becomes a soft delete (`deleted_at`): the item disappears, an Undo toast
  and a "Recently deleted" view restore it for 30 days, then it is purged. This matches the privacy policy's 30-day
  purge. It covers the hard deletes on `inventory_items`, `schedule_items`, `asset_nodes`, `pm_assets`,
  `project_links` and `project_roles`, and every read of those tables must exclude deleted rows.

**D3, what a page deletes stays recoverable for its retention window (21 rows) - built to Ian's choice, walked, 21/21.**
Eight tables now delete recoverably: the six above, plus `logbook` (logbook.html deleted entries outright too, "This
cannot be undone") and `community_posts`. A delete stamps `deleted_at`; the row and everything under it (FMEA modes,
sensor readings, a part's stock ledger, a PM asset's completions) survive; an Undo toast and a "Recently deleted" list
on each page bring it back; the daily retention job removes it after the hive's window (30 days, never less).
- **How.** One restrictive SELECT policy per table hides deleted rows from every read that runs as the person (pages,
  invoker views, invoker RPCs). Trash, restore and the list are invoker functions (`wh_trash`, `wh_restore`,
  `wh_recently_deleted`), so each table's own UPDATE policy decides who may delete or restore; Postgres refuses a client
  UPDATE that hides its own row under such a policy (probed), so the three functions relax the rule by a
  transaction-local flag. Readers that bypass RLS filter themselves: the 13 truth views, 12 security-definer functions
  and 13 direct edge-function reads (`20261016000002`). The shared component is utils.js `whTrash` /
  `whRecentlyDeleted`; the offline queue drains a queued delete through `wh_trash`.
- **Kept at the person's action.** Trashing signed-off work still needs a supervisor (the approval guard learned the
  `deleted_at` transition); the audit log records delete, recover and purge; XP a logbook entry earned is taken back on
  delete and given back on restore, from the delete's own reversal rows (the weekly XP-log purge now keeps them while
  the entry waits). A deleted entry's AI knowledge (`fault_knowledge`) is removed and rebuilt from the outbox on
  restore. A tag or part number a deleted row still holds says where it is; a re-added project link or role replaces
  its deleted copy.
- **Found on the way.** (1) A deleted public community post stayed readable by anyone through the API for its 30 days
  (the read policy shows every public post; only the page filtered) - now 0 rows for anon, 1 without the policy
  (rolled-back teeth). (2) "Adjustable by supervisor" (plant-connections) and "a data-retention policy you can set"
  (sensor article) were false: no hive had a retention row and creating one was locked. `set_hive_retention` sets the
  deleted-items window, floored at 30 days. (3) Nothing purges the audit trail, and no job reads the audit or AI
  windows, yet plant-connections listed "1,095 days audit, 90 days AI" under "daily cron purges", and the DOLE article
  told plants their records would be lost after a 3-year default. Both now say what the system does: records and their
  audit trail are never purged; the only scheduled removal is a deleted record after its window; AI cost records go
  after 365 days for every hive. (4) That article's FAQ said an edit records why; its own body says there is no field
  for why. (5) integrations.html's vehicle wizard hard-deletes rows it created seconds earlier - kept, with a reasoned
  `d3-allow`, because a trashed copy would hold the vehicle's tag and collide with a retry.
- **Walk.** Deleting pages (dayplanner, inventory, logbook entries and assets, pm-scheduler, project-manager links and
  roles, community): the page's own delete and confirm, then hidden from the person's reads (1 -> 0), Undo (-> 1),
  delete again, the page's own Recently deleted, Restore (-> 1), at 390 and 1280. Reading pages: hive and
  project-report lost the probe from their responses and got it back; the assistant's own logbook count read 4 -> 3
  -> 4; the public feed dropped the post and the anonymous API read returned nothing. plant-connections: a supervisor
  set 45 days, a delete then reported 45, 20 was refused. Public pages: read as served, every retention sentence held.
- **Instrument, four errors of mine.** The "still on screen" check matched the toast that names the item; two probes
  shared one label; a cast in two hives opened the other one; a probe dated three days ago was off the day view.
  Each was caught by a reading that disagreed with the server and fixed before banking.
- **Locked.** Gate `deletes-are-recoverable` (static: no page deletes these tables outright, every trashing page opens
  Recently deleted, every service-role read filters, the offline queue drains into the trash; live: the hide policy,
  the invoker functions, every definer function and view says `deleted_at`, the purge covers every table). Its first
  run caught integrations.html and two view-backed functions. `cascade-confirm-parity` learned that `mySet.delete(id)`
  is not a PostgREST delete; `cron-health` learned that a restart stub (no start time) is not the latest run.
- **Not this sub-layer, queued.** The DOLE article says an edit is recorded with "the before and after values of what
  they changed"; the audit log keeps status, category and downtime for an edit, not every field. Open pages other than
  community do not learn of a teammate's delete until they reload (a hidden row's UPDATE reaches no subscriber).
  The privacy policy's "audit logs retained 10 years / 15 for incidents" holds as a floor (nothing purges them); its
  wording is Ian's.

**Banked:** S3 154/154, CA2 155/155, H2 155/155, CI1 155/155, CI4 155/155, S4 36/36, S5 155/155, F5 155/155, CI3 155/155, F3 155/155, F2 155/155, H4 67/67, CI2 154/155 (the ventilation calculator's WebKit read pending), H1 155/155, AV1 155/155 (re-walked with the worker blocked), A3 31/31, F1 62/62, F4 155/155, C1 25/25, CA3 34/34, CA1 37/37, CA4 127/127, H3 93/93, D1 99/99, D2 25/25, D3 21/21, D4 6/6, A1 32/32, A2 21/21, A4 30/30, AV2 33/33, AV3 14/14, AV4 24/24, C2 155/155, C3 88/88, LB1 33/33, LB2 34/34, L2 21/21, L3 31/31, L4 32/32 and BRH318–322 closed.


### §SL.5 Walk 5 — D4 files and storage: a photo taken off the screen stayed public, Remove could not be tapped or did not remove, and a defect photo was thrown away (2026-10-19)

**The ask.** "The platform must store the files this page takes in the right bucket under the right owner, and serve
them back." Six pages take files (the D4 roster: integrations, inventory, logbook, marketplace-seller, marketplace,
resume). Each was walked at phone-390 and desktop-1280 as its row's cast, the file handed to the page's own control: a
JPEG drawn in the page, or a text file carrying a unique marker. Every upload was asked of the bucket by its public URL
(no-store), a storage tap recorded every object with its owner and how long it lived, and a marker scan searched all
786 text and json columns and storage for what a page said it does not keep.

**Found and fixed.**
- **marketplace and marketplace-seller: an unsaved photo stayed in a public bucket.** Both pickers upload the moment a
  photo is picked, so the upload runs while the seller types. Remove, a second pick, closing the edit sheet unsaved and
  leaving the page each left the upload in `marketplace-listings`, served by its URL after the person took it off their
  screen. `whHeldUpload` (utils.js) now holds the upload a form has not saved: `hold` (a replacing pick deletes the
  last), `release` (Remove, an unsaved close), `commit` (the row names it), and on `pagehide` a keepalive DELETE with
  the persisted session. Walked: every replaced, removed, closed and abandoned upload answered 400; every saved one 200
  and drawn on its card; the tap saw only the uploader as owner and nothing left at the end. T134's delete-the-photo
  paths (deleted listing, saved replace) were re-walked and hold.
- **Remove photo could not be tapped (both pages).** The zone's file input is `position:absolute; inset:0`, so it
  covered the Remove button painted in flow beneath it: a tap on Remove opened the photo picker. Raised
  (`position:relative; z-index:1`) and given a 44px target. The walk found it by trying to click it.
- **inventory: Remove photo did not remove.** The save wrote `currentPhotoData || prev.photo`, so the old photo came
  straight back. The fallback guarded nothing (the edit form loads the photo from the same cached row). Walked: add with
  photo, reload (row and card carry it), remove + save, reload (row and card carry none).
- **logbook: the photo of a defect was thrown away.** "Snap a photo of the defect" sent the picture to
  visual-defect-capture and the entry kept the AI's words about it, not the picture. The capture now becomes the
  entry's photo when the entry has none, at the entry's own budget (one encoder, `lbEncodeEntryPhoto`, shared with
  Attach Photo), never over a photo the person attached; Retake takes it back off; a fresh entry resets the capture.
  Walked: the saved photo's length matched the capture exactly, owner and hive right, drawn after a reload.
- **Read and kept nowhere, now said so.** The vehicle manual (only its text leaves the browser), the CMMS export
  (parsed in the browser), both GCash receipt uploads and the nameplate scan read a file and keep nothing - measured:
  each marker in none of 786 columns, no storage object - but only resume.html said so. Each now carries one sentence.
- **A gate that misread the safer code.** `validate_inventory.py` had failed `delete_scoped` since D3: the recoverable
  delete goes through `wh_trash` (SECURITY INVOKER, the caller's RLS), and the check still looked for the hand-written
  `.eq('hive_id')` it replaced - and then matched ".delete()" in D3's own comment. It now accepts the trash path with
  comments stripped, and still fails a hard delete beside it.

**Instrument, three errors of mine.** Logbook's hidden toast ships the text "Entry saved." in its markup, so a reader of
`#toast` saw a save that never happened (the page's own duplicate guard had answered); the toast is `position:fixed`,
so `offsetParent` is always null and a visibility test built on it saw nothing. The listing lookup walked up from a
Delete button until it found the title and reached the list, which holds every title: it deleted the other probe. Each
was caught by a reading that disagreed with the database, fixed, and re-walked.

**Locked.** Gate `file-storage-owned` (`tools/validate_file_storage.py`, 12 mutation tests): every file input on every
served page has a walked disposition (a new one fails until walked); bucket pickers hold, release and commit; Remove sits
above the input; no photo fallback; both inline photo tables keep their server cap (`check_inline_image_size`); each
read-only intake's function stores nothing and its page says so; the defect capture shares the entry encoder; the
voice assistant's file helper stays uncalled. Live: no object older than an hour in the public bucket that no listing
names - its first run found a June probe's photo whose account no longer exists, removed.

**Not this sub-layer, queued.** A tab the phone's OS kills while a photo is held fires no `pagehide`, so that upload
can still be left behind; the live check sees it after an hour, and a server-side sweep would close it. The résumé
reader was held off by the no-model rule, so the walk proved what is stored (nothing), not what is read.


### §SL.6 Walk 6 — A1 a refusal has a sentence: a visitor was addressed as a member, refusals were called outages, and failed reads drew empty states (2026-10-19)

**The ask.** "The platform must answer every refused or failed request on this page with a sentence a person can act
on." 32 pages (27 production, 5 founder), each as its row's cast at phone-390 and desktop-1280, in its own browser
context with service workers blocked. An init script patched fetch before any page script, so supabase-js built its
client around it, and the page's own reads were failed from the first byte three ways: 500 internal server error,
PostgREST's stock 42501 permission denied (a refusal no guard authored), and on the two pages that call one at
start-up, the platform's real 429 body. Graded on the sentences the page NEWLY said, in place or in any live region it
showed while settling: failure- or refusal-shaped with a next step; no machine text; no new empty state over a failed
read; a refusal named as a refusal; an outage never blamed on permission or on the device's connection; a visitor never
addressed as a member. A condition the page never reached is ungraded. The vocabularies are `tools/session_signals.mjs`.

**Found and fixed.**
- **A visitor was addressed as a member.** The shared refusal sentences (whReadError, whWriteError, the page-wide
  notice) said "with this account... Your session is fine. Ask a supervisor" - to the public feed's signed-out reader,
  three false statements. `_whSignedOut()` (the persisted session, read synchronously) gives a visitor "WorkHive does
  not show X to visitors who are not signed in. Sign in to see it."
- **A refused member was offered Sign in.** The notice chose its button by matching /session/ in its own text, and the
  refusal says "your session is FINE". It now decides by its identity: a visitor gets Sign in, a refused member no
  Reload at all (re-reading cannot turn a no into a yes; the sentence carries the step).
- **Refusals called outages.** The seller profile, ai-quality, PH Intelligence, the seller's wallet note and the
  marketplace verdict and grid answered a 42501 with "WorkHive did not answer, try again"; the audit log said "check
  your connection" for everything. Each now asks whReadError (or the page's own classifier), which reads the error.
- **Failed reads drew empty states.** asset-hub: "No approved assets in this hive yet" under "Could not load your asset
  fleet". hive: "No readiness snapshot yet. Sign in and add your first asset" (and the signed-in empty case no longer
  says "sign in"). shift-brain: "No plan exists for this shift yet - Generate now" while the verdict said a plan may
  already be published: a duplicate plan one tap away. Each failed read now owns its region.
- **Refused live refreshes went silent.** alert-hub's Action Brief and shift-brain's briefing dropped their
  "Refreshing..." line on a 429 and said nothing; both now say "The live refresh did not run: <the function's own
  sentence>. The brief below is the stored one."
- **Could not ask is not "no", on the server axis.** whPlatformAdminAnswer answered 'no' for a check the server failed
  or refused, so the founder console and Marketplace Admin showed their no-access gate to the founder; it answers
  'unreachable' on any error now (every caller still fail-closed), whAdminCheckOfflineText is true online too, and
  Platform Actions no longer tells a connected founder "you're offline".
- **Two gates that misread.** `write-failure-speaks` read a guard's else from a truncated window and reported
  community's un-react (which speaks) as silent; it reads the source now and still fails a silent write.
  logbook's unexplained-save sentence ("check your connection") names its cause through whWriteError.

**Instrument, kept honest.** Each PASS was read, not trusted: the first grading credited the seller profile's "did not
answer" for a refusal and missed the public feed's member sentence to a visitor, so the rules were tightened (a refusal
must be named, any wrong-cause sentence fails, an online walk never warrants "you're offline", a visitor never reads
"this account") and every batch was re-run under the final oracle on the final code.

**Locked.** Gate `refusal-has-a-sentence` (`tools/validate_refusal_sentences.py`, 9 mutation tests): the visitor
branches, the notice's identity rule, the admin check's 'unreachable', the online-aware gate sentence, 13 page anchors,
and a ratchet on hard-coded "did not answer" sentences (25, none may rise). `offline-is-not-no` and
`write-failure-speaks` ride with it.

**Not this sub-layer, queued.** Writes were held by the static gates, not induced page by page; achievements and
ai-quality still show a Retry beside a refusal (harmless, not helpful). The "did not answer" sentences left under the
ratchet are offline-or-outage branches and old-utils fallbacks.


### §SL.7 Walk 7 — A2 no double submit: every write held at one, and a second Leave could follow the first (2026-10-19)

**The ask.** "The platform must write once when a person taps twice or the network retries, on every write this page
makes." 21 pages, each as its row's cast at phone-390 and desktop-1280, in a service-worker-blocked context with
